body-autonomy-indian-law-timeline.en:
Who decides what happens to your body: you, a doctor, a husband, a judge or a government board? Since 1971 Indian law has answered that question many times, and not always in the same direction. Here are the turns that matter most, up to 2026, when the Supreme Court widened one right and Parliament took another back. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 1971: a law written for doctors and married women

**10 August 1971.** The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act receives the President's assent. It allows an abortion up to 12 weeks if one registered doctor forms the opinion, in good faith, that the law's grounds are met, and from 12 to 20 weeks only if two doctors agree [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The law speaks of a doctor's opinion, not a woman's request.

It also decides whose failed contraception counts. When a method used by "any married woman or her husband" fails, the anguish of the unwanted pregnancy may be presumed to gravely injure her mental health [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. An unmarried woman gets no such presumption.

One clause does point towards autonomy: an adult woman's own consent is the only consent the Act asks for, and it names no role for a husband [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

**24 September 2021.** Half a century later, an amendment takes effect [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]] and replaces "married woman or her husband" with "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Our explainer on the 2021 amendment compares the two texts.

## 2013-2018: dignity, identity and privacy

**April 2013.** In Lillu v. State of Haryana, the Supreme Court holds that the "two-finger test" violates rape survivors' right to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]].

**15 April 2014.** In NALSA v. Union of India, the court recognises transgender persons as a "third gender", upholds their right to self-identify their gender and extends them the protection of Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 and 21 [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Your gender is yours to name.

**2017.** A nine-judge bench delivers its privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, tying a woman's legal right to an abortion to her constitutional right to make reproductive choices under Article 21 [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**6 September 2018.** In Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, five judges unanimously read down Section 377 of the IPC. Consensual sex between adults of the same sex stops being a crime; non-consensual acts remain one [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

## 2022: the unmarried woman's choice

**29 September 2022.** In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, the Supreme Court holds that excluding unmarried or single women from abortion between 20 and 24 weeks would violate Article 14. They get the same access as married women [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The judgment builds on Suchita Srivastava (2009), which recognised a woman's reproductive autonomy, and on Puttaswamy.

It also reads "rape" in the abortion law to include marital rape: a wife pregnant from forced sex by her husband can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks as a survivor, without filing an FIR [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. That recognition stops at the abortion law. Our guide to the ruling has the details.

**31 October 2022.** Back to the two-finger test. In State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai, the court says it "has no scientific basis" and that anyone who conducts it in breach of its directions "shall be guilty of misconduct". It orders governments to send the Health Ministry's 2014 guidelines to every hospital, public and private [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Nine years after Lillu, the court still had to order the rules sent to hospitals.

## 2026: a right gained, a right taken back

**30 January 2026.** In Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India, the Supreme Court holds that menstrual health is part of the right to life under Article 21. It directs every school to provide working, separate toilets with water, free sanitary napkins and safe disposal [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

**13-25 March 2026.** Section 4(2) of the Transgender Persons Act, 2019 had given every person recognised as transgender "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. Parliament now removes it. The amendment bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha on 13 March and cleared by both houses within 12 days [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]].

**25 May 2026.** The amendment, which received the President's assent on 30 March, takes effect. A District Magistrate now issues a transgender certificate only after examining the recommendation of a medical board headed by a Chief Medical Officer or a deputy. The new definition excludes "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. In 2014 the court said you may name your own gender. In 2026, a board decides.

**17 August 2026.** As the Supreme Court hears challenges to the amendment, the Union says identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act will keep working while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

**1 September 2026.** The court says it is discontented with states' compliance. Of 39,439 girls' toilets identified as needing to be made functional, 4,745 are neither built nor under construction [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. In an order reported on 15 October, it gives states "one last opportunity" before contempt notices [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].

## What the timeline teaches

Most of these freedoms came from courtrooms, not Parliament: Lillu, NALSA, Puttaswamy, Navtej, X and Jaya Thakur are all Supreme Court judgments.

Change is slow. The married-only clause stood for half a century, the two-finger test needed two judgments nine years apart, and months after the January ruling, thousands of needed school toilets had not even been started.

And what is won can be taken back. Twelve years after NALSA, a bill passed in 12 days handed the question of gender to a medical board. Whether that fits the Constitution is now for the court to decide.

One question is still open. Under Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on that exception; it said it would fix the final hearing for 9 or 10 December [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Until then, use what has been won, and keep watching: the answer to "whose body is it?" is still being argued.
body-autonomy-indian-law-timeline.hg:
Tumhari body ke saath kya hoga, yeh kaun tay karta hai: tum, doctor, husband, judge ya koi sarkari board? 1971 se Indian law is sawaal ka jawaab kai baar de chuka hai, aur hamesha ek hi direction mein nahi. Yeh rahe sabse zaroori mod, 2026 tak, jab Supreme Court ne ek haq bada kiya aur Parliament ne doosra wapas le liya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1971: doctors aur married women ke liye likha gaya law

**10 August 1971.** Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act ko President ki assent milti hai. Yeh 12 hafte tak abortion ki ijaazat deta hai agar ek registered doctor good faith mein yeh opinion banaye ki law ke grounds poore hote hain, aur 12 se 20 hafte ke beech tabhi jab do doctors raazi hon [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Law doctor ki opinion ki baat karta hai, woman ki request ki nahi.

Yahi law yeh bhi tay karta hai ki kiska fail hua contraception gina jayega. Jab "any married woman or her husband" ka use kiya hua method fail ho, toh maana ja sakta hai ki us unwanted pregnancy ki takleef uski mental health ko gambhir chot pahunchati hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Unmarried woman ko aisi koi presumption nahi milti.

Ek clause zaroor autonomy ki taraf ishaara karta hai: adult woman ki apni consent hi woh akeli consent hai jo Act maangta hai, aur isme husband ka koi role nahi likha [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

**24 September 2021.** Aadhi sadi baad ek amendment laagu hota hai [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]] aur "married woman or her husband" ki jagah "any woman or her partner" likh deta hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2021 amendment par hamara explainer dono texts ko saath rakh kar compare karta hai.

## 2013-2018: dignity, identity aur privacy

**April 2013.** Lillu v. State of Haryana mein Supreme Court kehta hai ki "two-finger test" rape survivors ke privacy, physical aur mental integrity aur dignity ke haq ka violation hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]].

**15 April 2014.** NALSA v. Union of India mein court transgender persons ko "third gender" ke roop mein recognise karta hai, apna gender khud identify karne ka unka haq barkaraar rakhta hai aur unhe Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 aur 21 ki protection deta hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Tumhara gender kya hai, yeh tum khud bataoge.

**2017.** Nau judges ki bench K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India mein privacy par apna faisla deti hai, aur woman ke abortion ke legal haq ko Article 21 ke under reproductive choices karne ke constitutional haq se jodti hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**6 September 2018.** Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India mein paanch judges ek raay se IPC ke Section 377 ko read down karte hain. Same sex ke adults ke beech consensual sex ab crime nahi rehta; non-consensual acts crime bane rehte hain [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

## 2022: unmarried woman ki choice

**29 September 2022.** X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department mein Supreme Court kehta hai ki unmarried ya single women ko 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion se bahar rakhna Article 14 ka violation hoga. Unhe wahi access milta hai jo married women ko [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yeh judgment Suchita Srivastava (2009) par khada hai, jisne woman ki reproductive autonomy ko recognise kiya tha, aur Puttaswamy par.

Yeh judgment abortion law mein "rape" ke matlab mein marital rape ko bhi shaamil karta hai: jo wife apne husband ke forced sex se pregnant hui ho, woh survivor ke roop mein 24 hafte tak abortion maang sakti hai, bina FIR file kiye [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yeh recognition abortion law par hi ruk jaati hai. Is ruling par hamari guide mein poori details hain.

**31 October 2022.** Wapas two-finger test par. State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai mein court kehta hai ki yeh test "has no scientific basis", yaani iska koi scientific aadhaar nahi hai, aur jo bhi uske directions tod kar ise kare woh "shall be guilty of misconduct", yaani misconduct ka doshi hoga. Court governments ko order deta hai ki Health Ministry ki 2014 guidelines har hospital ko bheji jayein, government ho ya private [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Lillu ke nau saal baad bhi court ko yeh order dena pada ki rules hospitals tak pahunchaye jayein.

## 2026: ek haq mila, ek haq wapas liya gaya

**30 January 2026.** Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India mein Supreme Court kehta hai ki menstrual health Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa hai. Court har school ko direction deta hai ki woh paani ke saath working, alag toilets, free sanitary napkins aur safe disposal ka intezaam kare [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

**13-25 March 2026.** Transgender Persons Act, 2019 ke Section 4(2) ne transgender ke roop mein recognised har insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity" diya tha, yaani apni mehsoos ki hui gender identity ka haq [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. Ab Parliament ise hata deti hai. Amendment bill 13 March ko Lok Sabha mein introduce hota hai aur 12 din ke andar dono houses se pass ho jaata hai [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]].

**25 May 2026.** Jis amendment ko 30 March ko President ki assent mili thi, woh laagu hota hai. Ab District Magistrate transgender certificate tabhi jaari karta hai jab woh ek medical board ki recommendation examine kar le, jiska head Chief Medical Officer ya deputy hota hai. Nayi definition "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" ko bahar rakhti hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. 2014 mein court ne kaha tha ki apna gender tum khud bata sakte ho. 2026 mein ek board tay karta hai.

**17 August 2026.** Supreme Court amendment ke khilaaf challenges sun raha hai, aur Union kehta hai ki 2019 Act ke under pehle se jaari identity cards case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

**1 September 2026.** Court kehta hai ki woh states ke compliance se discontent hai. Jin 39,439 girls' toilets ko functional banane ki zaroorat pehchaani gayi thi, unme se 4,745 na bane hain, na ban rahe hain [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. 15 October ko report hue ek order mein court states ko contempt notices se pehle "one last opportunity", yaani ek aakhiri mauka deta hai [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].

## Yeh timeline kya sikhati hai

Inme se zyada tar azaadiyan courtrooms se aayi, Parliament se nahi: Lillu, NALSA, Puttaswamy, Navtej, X aur Jaya Thakur, sab Supreme Court ke judgments hain.

Badlaav dheema hai. Married-only clause aadhi sadi tak tika raha, two-finger test ke liye nau saal ke gap par do judgments lage, aur January ki ruling ke mahino baad bhi hazaaron zaroori school toilets shuru tak nahi hue the.

Aur jo jeeta gaya hai, woh wapas liya ja sakta hai. NALSA ke baarah saal baad, 12 din mein pass hue ek bill ne gender ka sawaal ek medical board ko saunp diya. Yeh Constitution par khara utarta hai ya nahi, yeh ab court tay karega.

Ek sawaal abhi bhi khula hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke under, kisi aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex, agar wife 18 ya usse badi hai, law ki nazar mein rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne is exception par faisla nahi diya tha; usne kaha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December ko fix karega [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Tab tak jo jeeta gaya hai use use karo, aur nazar rakho: "body kiski hai?" ke jawaab par behes abhi bhi chal rahi hai.

body-parts-biology-lessons-skip.en:
Hand most Indian adults a blank outline of the human body and ask them to mark the cervix, the prostate and the whole of the clitoris. Few of us were taught enough to try. Reproduction is the chapter families skip and many classrooms rush, so adults who can label the parts of a flower cannot label their own. That gap shapes who gets screened for cancer, whose pain is taken seriously, and whether a child has words for what was done to them.

## The diagram nobody showed you

School diagrams are built around making babies. They show the uterus, ovaries and testes in cross-section, and they shrink to a dot, or leave out, any part whose job is sensation. The clitoris is the clearest case: few people have ever been shown a diagram of the whole organ.

Policy is no louder. India's National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words 'sex', 'sexual', 'sexuality', 'reproductive', 'puberty' or 'menstruation' in its 66 pages [[nep-2020-full-text]]. Adolescent health is left to separate health-ministry programmes, outside the main curriculum. So here is the map, in plain words.

## Outside: vulva, clitoris, penis, scrotum

The vulva is everything on the outside of a female body: the outer and inner folds of skin called labia, the clitoris, and two openings. The vagina is not the outside part; it is the passage inside. From front to back there are three separate openings: the urethra for urine, the vagina, and the anus. Urine never comes out of the vagina [[who-sexual-health]].

The visible clitoris is a small nub at the top of the vulva, partly covered by a hood of skin. Most of the organ is inside: a short shaft, two arms and two bulbs of spongy tissue on either side of the vaginal opening. It grows from the same tissue in the embryo that forms the penis, and swells with blood in a similar way. Its role is sensation, including sexual sensation. It plays no part in urination, periods or pregnancy.

The penis carries the urethra, the one tube through which both urine and semen leave, though never together: a ring of muscle shuts the bladder outlet during ejaculation. An erection is blood filling spongy tissue; there is no bone in it. Behind the penis, the scrotum holds the two testicles outside the body, because sperm develop best slightly cooler than body temperature.

## Inside: vagina, cervix, uterus and ovaries; testes and prostate

The vagina is a muscular passage that stretches a great deal and returns to shape. It cleans itself.

At its top is the cervix, the firm lower neck of the uterus. Its tiny opening lets period blood out and sperm in, and widens during childbirth. The uterus is a pear-sized muscular organ whose lining thickens every cycle and is shed as a period if no pregnancy begins. On either side sit the ovaries, which store egg cells and make hormones, and the fallopian tubes, where egg and sperm meet.

From puberty the testicles, also called testes, make sperm and testosterone. Sperm mature in the epididymis, a coiled tube behind each testicle, then travel up the vas deferens and mix with fluid from the seminal vesicles and the prostate, a walnut-sized gland just below the bladder. That mixture is semen; sperm are only a small part of it. The urethra runs through the prostate, which is why prostate trouble in older men usually shows up as difficulty passing urine.

## Why it matters: screening, pain and consent

Start with the cervix. HPV types 16 and 18 account for more than 80% of cervical cancer cases in India [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]], and the latest GLOBOCAN estimate puts India's cervical cancer deaths at 36,319 in 2024 [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Screening looks for changes in the cervix before they turn into cancer [[who-cervical]]. Yet in NFHS-5 (2019-21) only 1.2% of women aged 15-49 said they had ever had a cervical cancer screening test; even among women aged 35-49 it was 2% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. WHO's target for 2030 is 70% of women screened with a high-performance test by 35 and again by 45 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

One cause is simple: nobody asks for a test on an organ she has never been told she has. Protection now starts earlier too: since 28 February 2026 a free single-dose HPV vaccine has been offered to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]].

Then pain. Imagine a 19-year-old in Patna who tells her mother 'neeche dard hota hai', it hurts down there. She cannot say whether it is the vulva, the bladder or deep in the pelvis, and her mother has no more words than she does. The doctor receives a symptom with no address. WHO says an endometriosis diagnosis takes on average 4 to 12 years [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Pain that cannot be located is easy to call normal.

Then consent and safety. A child who knows the words 'penis', 'vulva' and 'anus' can tell a parent or a doctor exactly what happened. A child who only knows 'shame-shame' cannot. In its September 2024 ruling the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent and the harms of child sexual exploitation [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. The usual objection is that such teaching makes young people sexually active. The UN's technical guidance, revised in 2018, states that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Words to use with a doctor

You do not need Latin. You need three things.

- The part: 'on the outside, on the labia', 'inside the vagina', 'the left testicle', 'under the foreskin', 'when I pass urine'.
- The feeling: burning, itching, a lump, a sore, cramping, discharge and its colour.
- The timing: since when, constant or on and off, linked to periods, sex or passing urine.

If saying it aloud is hard, type it on your phone and hand the phone over, or point to a diagram. You can ask for a doctor of your own gender, or for a nurse to stay in the room. Teenagers can go to a government Adolescent Friendly Health Centre for counselling and clinical care [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

Teach these words to the children in your family in the same voice you use for 'elbow' and 'knee', and they will not have to learn them from a rumour.
body-parts-biology-lessons-skip.hg:
Zyada tar Indian adults ko human body ka ek khaali outline pakda do aur kaho ki isme cervix, prostate aur poora clitoris mark karo. Hum mein se bahut kam logon ko itna sikhaya gaya ki try bhi kar sakein. Reproduction woh chapter hai jo families skip karti hain aur bahut si classrooms jaldi-jaldi nipta deti hain, isliye jo adults phool ke parts label kar lete hain, woh apni body ke parts label nahi kar paate. Yahi gap tay karta hai ki cancer ki screening kiski hoti hai, kiske dard ko seriously liya jaata hai, aur kisi bachche ke paas yeh batane ke shabd hain ya nahi ki uske saath kya kiya gaya.

## Woh diagram jo kisi ne dikhaya hi nahi

School ke diagrams bachcha banne ke process ke aas-paas bane hote hain. Woh uterus, ovaries aur testes ko cross-section mein dikhate hain, aur jis bhi part ka kaam sensation hai use ek dot bana dete hain ya chhod hi dete hain. Clitoris iska sabse saaf example hai: bahut kam logon ne kabhi poore organ ka diagram dekha hai.

Policy bhi itni hi chup hai. India ki National Education Policy 2020 apne 66 pages mein ek baar bhi 'sex', 'sexual', 'sexuality', 'reproductive', 'puberty' ya 'menstruation' shabd use nahi karti [[nep-2020-full-text]]. Adolescent health ko health ministry ke alag programmes par chhod diya gaya hai, main curriculum ke bahar. Toh yeh raha map, seedhe shabdon mein.

## Bahar: vulva, clitoris, penis, scrotum

Vulva matlab female body ka bahar ka poora hissa: skin ke outer aur inner folds jinhe labia kehte hain, clitoris, aur do openings. Vagina bahar wala part nahi hai; woh andar ka passage hai. Aage se peeche teen alag openings hoti hain: urine ke liye urethra, phir vagina, phir anus. Urine kabhi vagina se bahar nahi aata [[who-sexual-health]].

Clitoris ka jo hissa dikhta hai, woh vulva ke top par ek chhota sa nub hai, jo skin ke ek hood se thoda dhaka rehta hai. Organ ka zyada tar hissa andar hota hai: ek chhota shaft, do arms, aur vaginal opening ke dono taraf spongy tissue ke do bulbs. Embryo mein yeh usi tissue se banta hai jisse penis banta hai, aur usi tarah blood se phoolta hai. Iska kaam sensation hai, jisme sexual sensation bhi shaamil hai. Urination, periods ya pregnancy mein iska koi role nahi hai.

Penis ke andar se urethra guzarta hai, wahi ek tube jisse urine aur semen dono bahar aate hain, lekin kabhi ek saath nahi: ejaculation ke waqt muscle ka ek ring bladder ka outlet band kar deta hai. Erection matlab spongy tissue mein blood bharna; isme koi haddi nahi hoti. Penis ke peeche scrotum dono testicles ko body ke bahar rakhta hai, kyunki sperm body temperature se thode kam temperature par sabse achchhe se bante hain.

## Andar: vagina, cervix, uterus aur ovaries; testes aur prostate

Vagina ek muscular passage hai jo bahut zyada stretch hota hai aur wapas apni shape mein aa jaata hai. Yeh khud ko saaf karta hai.

Iske top par cervix hota hai, uterus ki firm, neeche wali gardan. Iski chhoti si opening period ka blood bahar aur sperm andar jaane deti hai, aur delivery ke waqt chaudi ho jaati hai. Uterus naashpaati ke size ka muscular organ hai jiski lining har cycle mein moti hoti hai aur pregnancy shuru na ho toh period ban kar nikal jaati hai. Dono taraf ovaries hoti hain, jo egg cells store karti hain aur hormones banati hain, aur fallopian tubes, jahan egg aur sperm milte hain.

Puberty se testicles, jinhe testes bhi kehte hain, sperm aur testosterone banate hain. Sperm epididymis mein mature hote hain, jo har testicle ke peeche ek coiled tube hai, phir vas deferens se upar jaate hain aur seminal vesicles aur prostate ke fluid mein mil jaate hain. Prostate akhrot ke size ka gland hai, bladder ke theek neeche. Yahi mixture semen hai; sperm iska bas ek chhota sa hissa hote hain. Urethra prostate ke beech se guzarta hai, isiliye badi umar ke mardon mein prostate ki problem aksar peshaab karne mein dikkat ban kar saamne aati hai.

## Yeh kyun matter karta hai: screening, dard aur consent

Cervix se shuru karo. India mein cervical cancer ke 80% se zyada cases HPV types 16 aur 18 se hote hain [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]], aur latest GLOBOCAN estimate ke hisaab se 2024 mein India mein cervical cancer se 36,319 deaths hui [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Screening cervix mein hone wale changes ko cancer banne se pehle pakadti hai [[who-cervical]]. Phir bhi NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 1.2% women ne kaha ki unhone kabhi cervical cancer screening test karwaya hai; 35-49 saal ki women mein bhi yeh 2% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 2030 ke liye WHO ka target hai ki 70% women ki high-performance test se screening 35 saal tak ho aur 45 tak dobara ho [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

Ek wajah seedhi hai: jis organ ke baare mein kisi aurat ko kabhi bataya hi nahi gaya, uska test woh maangegi kaise. Protection ab pehle shuru hoti hai: 28 February 2026 se 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko government health facilities mein free single-dose HPV vaccine offer ki ja rahi hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]].

Phir dard. Patna ki ek 19 saal ki ladki ko imagine karo jo apni mummy se kehti hai, 'neeche dard hota hai'. Woh yeh nahi bata paati ki dard vulva mein hai, bladder mein hai ya pelvis ke andar gehra, aur uski mummy ke paas bhi usse zyada shabd nahi hain. Doctor tak ek aisa symptom pahunchta hai jiska koi address nahi. WHO kehta hai ki endometriosis ka diagnosis hone mein average 4 se 12 saal lagte hain [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Jis dard ki jagah batayi na ja sake, use 'normal' keh dena aasaan hota hai.

Phir consent aur safety. Jo bachcha 'penis', 'vulva' aur 'anus' shabd jaanta hai, woh parent ya doctor ko theek-theek bata sakta hai ki kya hua. Jo bachcha sirf 'shame-shame' jaanta hai, woh nahi bata sakta. September 2024 ke apne faisle mein Supreme Court ne comprehensive sex education recommend ki, jisme consent aur child sexual exploitation ke nuksaan cover hon [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Aam objection yeh hota hai ki aisi teaching se young log sexually active ho jaate hain. UN ki technical guidance, jo 2018 mein revise hui, kehti hai ki sexuality education se sexual activity, sexual risk-taking ya STI/HIV infection rates nahi badhte [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Doctor ke saamne kaun se shabd use karein

Tumhe Latin nahi chahiye. Tumhe teen cheezein chahiye.

- Part: 'bahar ki taraf, labia par', 'vagina ke andar', 'left testicle', 'foreskin ke neeche', 'peshaab karte waqt'.
- Feeling: jalan, khujli, lump, sore, cramping, discharge aur uska colour.
- Timing: kab se hai, lagataar hai ya aata-jaata hai, periods, sex ya peshaab se juda hai ya nahi.

Agar zor se bolna mushkil lage, toh phone par type karke phone doctor ko pakda do, ya diagram par point kar do. Tum apne gender ka doctor maang sakte ho, ya keh sakte ho ki ek nurse room mein rahe. Teenagers counselling aur clinical care ke liye government ke Adolescent Friendly Health Centre ja sakte hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

Apni family ke bachchon ko yeh shabd usi awaaz mein sikhao jisme tum 'kohni' aur 'ghutna' sikhate ho, aur unhe yeh shabd kisi afwaah se nahi seekhne padenge.

boys-learn-about-periods-supreme-court.en:
Imagine a Class 9 classroom in Kanpur. A girl stands up after a test and there is a stain on her skirt. Two boys laugh, a third makes a joke, and by lunch the whole section knows. She stays home the next day. Nobody in that room was ever taught what a period is. On 30 January 2026, the Supreme Court made that a school's problem. The judgment that made menstrual health part of the right to life under Article 21 also told schools to sensitise boys and male teachers [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Here are the answers boys rarely get.

## Why bring boys into a judgment about periods?

Because girls do not produce the shame around periods. It is produced around them. A 2016 review of Indian studies found that about a quarter of adolescent girls (24%) missed school during their periods, 77% were kept from religious activities such as visiting places of worship or praying, and only one in eight faced no restriction at all [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Only 48% had been told about menstruation before their first period [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Many girls learn the rules before they learn the biology.

The court's directions read like a map of where girls get pushed out: working toilets, free pads, spare uniforms for accidents, and sensitisation of boys and male teachers [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Toilets fix the building. Sensitising boys is about fixing the room.

Some parents worry that this talk will "spoil" boys. The evidence says otherwise. UNESCO's international guidance, built mainly on two evidence reviews, including a 2016 Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised trials, states that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity or risk-taking [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. It also says curriculum-based programmes contribute to later first sex, fewer partners and more condom and contraceptive use [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Our story on the 2007 sex-education bans tests the "culture" argument against that evidence.

## What actually happens in a period?

Roughly once a month, the lining of the uterus (womb) thickens, ready in case a pregnancy starts. When no pregnancy starts, the lining breaks down and leaves the body through the vagina as blood and tissue. That is a period. It is ordinary blood and tissue, not "dirty" or "impure" blood.

A period lasts 2 to 7 days, usually about 5, and the whole cycle, from the start of one period to the start of the next, usually runs anywhere from 21 to 35 days [[nhs-periods]]. Irregular periods are common in the first years after periods begin, during puberty [[nhs-periods]]. Over an entire period, most people lose only a few tablespoons of blood [[nhs-periods]].

What she uses matters for you too. In 2019-21, 49.6% of women aged 15-24 used cloth [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Cloth can be safe if it is washed with soap and dried properly, ideally in the sun. That needs privacy. If a brother smirks at the cloth on the line, she may dry it somewhere hidden and damp instead. Our story on cloth and periods explains why water, soap and privacy are the real hygiene problem.

## Pain, mood and stains: what is normal?

Cramps are common. Period pain happens when the womb tightens during a period. A hot-water bottle on the lower belly, a warm bath, a gentle massage or light exercise help many people; some need a painkiller.

But pain is not always "normal". A doctor should see anyone whose pain stops their usual daily activities, who has to change a pad every 1 to 2 hours, whose periods change or stop, or who bleeds between periods or after sex [[nhs-periods]]. One reason this matters: endometriosis, where tissue similar to the womb lining grows outside the womb, affects an estimated 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide, and diagnosis takes 4 to 12 years on average [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Every "it's normal, adjust" can add to that delay.

Mood changes before a period are real too. Bloating, sore breasts, irritability, mood swings and headaches are typical symptoms of premenstrual syndrome (PMS), and they usually ease once the period starts [[nhs-periods]]. They are hormones, not a personality flaw, and not a punchline.

Stains happen because flow is not perfectly predictable, especially in the teenage years. A stain is not carelessness.

## How can you help a sister, classmate or partner?

At home: if you are sent to buy pads, buy them the way you would buy bread, with no newspaper wrap and no jokes. If your sister lies down, do not comment; ask if she wants a hot-water bottle.

In class: if you see a stain, tell her quietly and offer your jacket or sweater to tie around her waist. Do not announce it, photograph it or forward anything. If she needs to go to the toilet or the sick room, help her leave without an audience. If your school has no working girls' toilet or no free pads, it is falling short of the Supreme Court's order; our guide to what the ruling says every school owes girls explains whom to approach.

With a partner: her period is not your inconvenience. Ask what helps instead of guessing. Take her pain seriously, and never make her justify it.

## What should boys stop saying?

- "Is she on her period?" when a girl is angry. Anger is not a symptom.
- "Gross" at a pad in a bag. It is a hygiene product, like soap.
- "Don't touch the pickle" or "don't enter the kitchen". Keeping her out of a kitchen, a temple or a cricket match has no medical basis.
- "Everyone has cramps, stop the drama." Pain that stops a normal day needs a doctor.
- "Why do girls get special treatment?" A spare uniform and a working toilet are not special treatment. The Supreme Court ordered them because menstrual health is part of her right to life.

Being the boy who does not laugh is easy. Being the boy who tells the others to stop is harder, and that is the boy the court is asking schools to raise.
boys-learn-about-periods-supreme-court.hg:
Socho, Kanpur mein Class 9 ka ek classroom. Test ke baad ek ladki khadi hoti hai aur uski skirt par stain hai. Do ladke hanste hain, teesra joke maarta hai, aur lunch tak poore section ko pata chal jaata hai. Agle din woh school nahi aati. Us room mein kisi ko kabhi sikhaya hi nahi gaya ki period hota kya hai. 30 January 2026 ko Supreme Court ne ise school ki zimmedari bana diya. Jis judgment ne menstrual health ko Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa bataya, usi ne schools se yeh bhi kaha ki boys aur male teachers ko is baare mein sensitise kiya jaaye [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Yahan woh jawab hain jo boys ko shayad hi kabhi milte hain.

## Periods wale judgment mein boys kyun?

Kyunki periods ki sharm ladkiyan khud paida nahi karti. Yeh sharm unke aas-paas paida ki jaati hai. 2016 mein India ki studies ke ek review ne paaya ki lagbhag har chauthi adolescent ladki (24%) ka periods ke dauraan school chhoota, 77% ko pooja ki jagah jaane ya pooja-paath karne jaisi religious activities se roka gaya, aur aath mein se sirf ek ladki par koi restriction nahi thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Sirf 48% ladkiyon ko pehle period se pehle iske baare mein bataya gaya tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Bahut si ladkiyon ko biology se pehle rules sikhaye jaate hain.

Court ke directions padho toh lagta hai jaise kisi ne map bana diya ho ki ladkiyan kahan-kahan se bahar dhakeli jaati hain: chaalu toilets, free pads, stain lagne par badalne ke liye spare uniforms, aur boys aur male teachers ka sensitisation [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Toilets building theek karte hain. Boys ko sensitise karna class ka mahaul theek karne ki baat hai.

Kuch parents darte hain ki aisi baaton se ladke "bigad" jaayenge. Evidence kuch aur kehta hai. UNESCO ki international guidance zyada tar do bade evidence reviews par based hai, jinmein 2016 ka ek Oxford review bhi hai jisne 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised trials dekhe. Yeh guidance kehti hai ki sexuality education se na sexual activity badhti hai, na risk-taking [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Yeh bhi kehti hai ki curriculum-based programmes pehla sex der se hone, kam partners, aur condom aur contraception ke zyada use mein contribute karte hain [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. 2007 ke sex-education bans wali hamari story "culture" wali dalil ko isi evidence par test karti hai.

## Period mein asal mein hota kya hai?

Lagbhag har mahine uterus (womb, bachchedani) ki andar wali layer moti hoti hai, taaki agar pregnancy ho toh woh ready rahe. Pregnancy nahi hoti, toh yeh layer toot kar vagina ke raaste blood aur tissue ke roop mein bahar aati hai. Yahi period hai. Yeh normal blood aur tissue hai, koi "ganda" ya "ashuddh" khoon nahi.

Ek period 2 se 7 din chalta hai, usually lagbhag 5 din, aur ek period ke start se agle period ke start tak ka poora cycle usually 21 se 35 din ke beech kahin bhi ho sakta hai [[nhs-periods]]. Periods shuru hone ke baad ke pehle kuch saalon mein, puberty ke dauraan, irregular periods common hain [[nhs-periods]]. Poore period mein zyada tar logon ka bas kuch tablespoon bhar blood nikalta hai [[nhs-periods]].

Woh kya use karti hai, isse tumhara bhi lena-dena hai. 2019-21 mein 15-24 saal ki 49.6% women kapda use karti thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Kapda safe ho sakta hai agar use sabun se dhoya jaaye aur theek se sukhaya jaaye, ho sake toh dhoop mein. Iske liye privacy chahiye. Agar bhai rassi par sookhte kapde ko dekh kar smirk kare, toh ho sakta hai woh use kisi chhupi, seelan wali jagah par sukhaye. Kapde aur periods par hamari story batati hai ki asli hygiene problem paani, sabun aur privacy ki hai.

## Dard, mood aur stains: kya normal hai?

Cramps hona common hai. Period ka dard isliye hota hai kyunki period ke dauraan womb tight hoti hai. Pet ke neeche hot-water bottle, garam paani se nahana, halki maalish ya halki exercise se bahut logon ko aaram milta hai; kuch ko painkiller ki zaroorat padti hai.

Lekin har dard "normal" nahi hota. Doctor ko tab dikhana chahiye jab dard ki wajah se roz ke kaam ruk jaayein, har 1 se 2 ghante mein pad badalna pade, periods badal jaayein ya ruk jaayein, ya do periods ke beech ya sex ke baad bleeding ho [[nhs-periods]]. Yeh kyun zaroori hai? Endometriosis mein womb ki layer jaisa tissue womb ke bahar badhne lagta hai. Duniya bhar mein reproductive age ki lagbhag 10% women ko yeh hota hai, aur diagnosis mein average 4 se 12 saal lag jaate hain [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Har "yeh toh normal hai, adjust karo" is delay ko aur badha sakta hai.

Period se pehle mood badalna bhi real hai. Bloating, breasts mein dard, chidchidapan, mood swings aur sar dard premenstrual syndrome (PMS) ke typical symptoms hain, aur period shuru hone par yeh usually kam ho jaate hain [[nhs-periods]]. Yeh hormones ka asar hai, personality ki koi kami nahi, aur joke ki cheez toh bilkul nahi.

Stains isliye lagte hain kyunki flow hamesha predict nahi hota, khaas kar teenage mein. Stain lagna laaparwahi nahi hai.

## Behen, classmate ya partner ki help kaise karo?

Ghar par: agar tumhe pads laane bheja jaaye, toh waise hi lao jaise bread laate ho, na newspaper mein lapetna, na koi joke. Agar behen leti hui hai, toh comment mat karo; bas poocho ki kya use hot-water bottle chahiye.

Class mein: stain dikhe toh use chupchaap batao aur kamar par baandhne ke liye apni jacket ya sweater do. Na announce karo, na photo lo, na kuch forward karo. Use toilet ya sick room jaana ho, toh bina audience ke nikalne mein help karo. Agar tumhare school mein ladkiyon ka chaalu toilet nahi hai ya free pads nahi milte, toh school Supreme Court ka order poora nahi kar raha; judgment ke hisaab se school ko ladkiyon ko kya-kya dena hai, is par hamari guide batati hai ki kisse baat karni hai.

Partner ke saath: uska period tumhari problem nahi hai. Guess karne ki jagah poocho ki use kis cheez se aaram milta hai. Uske dard ko seriously lo, aur usse kabhi safai mat maango.

## Boys ko kya bolna band karna chahiye?

- Ladki gusse mein ho toh "Periods chal rahe hain kya?" Gussa koi symptom nahi hai.
- Bag mein pad dekh kar "Chhi!" Pad bhi sabun jaisi ek hygiene cheez hai.
- "Achaar mat chhoona" ya "kitchen mein mat jaana". Period mein kisi ko kitchen, mandir ya cricket ground se door rakhne ka koi medical reason nahi hai.
- "Cramps toh sabko hote hain, drama band karo." Jo dard normal din rok de, uske liye doctor zaroori hai.
- "Ladkiyon ko special treatment kyun?" Spare uniform aur chaalu toilet special treatment nahi hain. Supreme Court ne inka order isliye diya kyunki menstrual health uske right to life ka hissa hai.

Na hansne wala ladka banna aasaan hai. Doosron ko tokne wala ladka banna mushkil hai, aur court schools se aise hi ladke taiyaar karne ko keh raha hai.

breasts-chests-growth-asymmetry-boys.en:
Imagine two cousins at a family wedding. A 13-year-old girl from Jaipur has noticed that one side of her chest is sore and bigger than the other, and her mother's only advice was "dupatta theek se lo". Her 14-year-old cousin from Patna has a tender swelling behind one nipple. He wears two vests in May and skips swimming at school. Neither of them is ill. Neither has been told anything. This guide is what someone should have told them.

## Breasts grow for years, rarely evenly

Breast development usually starts with a "bud": a small, firm, sometimes tender lump under the nipple. It often appears on one side first, and the other side can take months to catch up. Many girls assume a lump means something is wrong. At this age it almost always means growth has started.

From there, breasts keep changing for several years, often into the late teens. They rarely grow at the same speed. One breast being a little larger, higher or differently shaped is common, and for many adults it stays that way for life. Clothes and photos hide it; bodies do not.

Soreness during growth and before periods is common too. Do not squeeze or press a new bud to "check" it. Let it grow.

## Size, shape, stretch marks and nipples: the normal range

Breast size is set mostly by genes and body fat. No cream, oil, capsule, massage or exercise changes it, whatever the ad on your feed says. Breasts also change through the menstrual cycle, often feeling fuller and tender in the days before a period.

Stretch marks are lines where skin stretched faster than it could keep up during a growth spurt. They appear on breasts, hips and thighs, start red or purple, and fade to pale silver over time. They are harmless and very common.

Nipples come in many forms. Flat nipples, nipples that turn inward, a few hairs around the areola and small bumps on it are all normal. What matters is change: a nipple that has always turned inward is fine, while one that newly pulls in later in life should be checked.

## Bras, sport and back pain

A bra is a choice for comfort and support, not a medical requirement. There is no good evidence that wearing one, with or without underwire, causes cancer.

Sport is where a bra earns its place. A well-fitted sports bra reduces movement and the pain that comes with running and jumping. Some girls quietly drop out of games at exactly the age their chest starts to bounce. The fix is the right bra, not the bench. Large breasts can also cause neck, shoulder and back pain; an adult with persistent pain can discuss options, including surgery, with a doctor.

## Boys' chests in puberty

During puberty, many boys develop a firm, sometimes tender swelling under one or both nipples. Doctors call it gynaecomastia. It is caused by normal hormone shifts, and in most boys it settles on its own over months to a couple of years. It does not mean a boy is "turning into a girl", and it is not caused by masturbation or by eating "hot" or "cold" foods.

It still deserves a doctor's visit if the lump is hard, on one side only, growing fast, leaking fluid or still there after puberty. Gym steroids and some medicines can also cause chest swelling in men, which our guide to men's body checks covers. Men can get breast cancer too; it is rare, but a lump in a man's chest should never be ignored [[who-breast-cancer]].

Trans and non-binary teenagers who bind their chests should use binders made for it, never bandages or tape, and take breaks so the skin and ribs can rest.

## Breast awareness: knowing your normal

This is why the habit matters. Breast cancer is the most common cancer among Indian women: an estimated 2,37,231 new cases and 96,100 deaths in 2024, making up 30.4% of all cancers in women [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Yet only 0.6% of women aged 15-49 had ever had a breast cancer screening test in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Teenagers rarely get breast cancer, and most breast lumps are not cancer [[who-breast-cancer]]. The point of learning your normal at 16 is that, at 40, you notice when something changes. WHO lists the signs to act on: a lump or thickening, often painless; a change in size or shape; dimpling, redness or pitting of the skin; a change in the nipple or the skin around it; and bloody or unusual fluid from the nipple [[who-breast-cancer]].

The survey does not say why the figure is so low, and access to services is part of it. But shame does not help: a girl taught to hide her chest at 13 can become a woman who hesitates to show a doctor a lump at 45.

Teenagers can get confidential advice at Adolescent Friendly Health Centres in primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Adults can go to any government hospital. You can ask for a female doctor, or for another woman to be present during an examination.

The cousins at that wedding do not need a lecture. They need one adult to say: you are growing, you are normal, and if anything ever worries you, we will go to a doctor together.
breasts-chests-growth-asymmetry-boys.hg:
Ek family shaadi mein do cousins ko imagine karo. Jaipur ki ek 13 saal ki ladki ne notice kiya hai ki uski chest ki ek side dukhti hai aur doosri se badi hai, aur uski mummy ki ek hi advice thi: "dupatta theek se lo". Patna ke uske 14 saal ke cousin ko ek nipple ke peeche halki dard wali swelling hai. Woh May ki garmi mein do baniyan pehenta hai aur school mein swimming skip karta hai. Dono mein se koi bimaar nahi hai. Dono ko kisi ne kuch bataya bhi nahi. Yeh guide wahi hai jo kisi ko unhe batana chahiye tha.

## Breasts saalon tak badhte hain, aur kabhi barabar nahi

Breast development aksar ek "bud" se shuru hota hai: nipple ke neeche ek chhota, thoda hard, kabhi-kabhi dukhne wala lump. Yeh aksar pehle ek side aata hai, aur doosri side ko catch up karne mein mahine lag sakte hain. Bahut si ladkiyan sochti hain ki lump matlab kuch gadbad hai. Is umar mein iska matlab almost hamesha yahi hota hai ki growth shuru ho gayi hai.

Uske baad breasts kai saalon tak badalte rehte hain, aksar late teens tak. Dono kabhi ek speed se nahi badhte. Ek breast ka thoda bada, thoda upar ya alag shape ka hona common hai, aur bahut se adults mein yeh zindagi bhar aisa hi rehta hai. Kapde aur photos ise chhupa dete hain; body nahi chhupati.

Growth ke dauraan aur periods se pehle dard hona bhi common hai. Naye bud ko "check" karne ke liye dabao ya squeeze mat karo. Use badhne do.

## Size, shape, stretch marks aur nipples: normal kitna wide hai

Breast ka size zyada tar genes aur body fat se tay hota hai. Koi cream, tel, capsule, massage ya exercise ise nahi badalta, chahe tumhari feed par aane wala ad kuch bhi kahe. Menstrual cycle ke saath bhi breasts badalte hain; period se pehle ke dinon mein aksar bhare-bhare aur sensitive lagte hain.

Stretch marks woh lines hain jahan growth spurt ke dauraan skin utni tezi se stretch nahi ho paayi. Yeh breasts, hips aur thighs par aate hain, pehle laal ya purple dikhte hain aur time ke saath halke silver ho jaate hain. Yeh harmless hain aur bahut common hain.

Nipples bhi kai tarah ke hote hain. Flat nipples, andar ki taraf mude nipples, areola ke aas-paas kuch baal aur us par chhote-chhote daane, sab normal hain. Asli baat badlaav ki hai: jo nipple hamesha se andar muda hai, woh theek hai, lekin jo nipple badi umar mein achanak andar khinch jaaye, use check karwana chahiye.

## Bra, sport aur kamar dard

Bra comfort aur support ki choice hai, medical zaroorat nahi. Is baat ka koi accha evidence nahi hai ki bra pehenne se, underwire ho ya na ho, cancer hota hai.

Sport mein bra ka asli kaam dikhta hai. Sahi fit wali sports bra movement kam karti hai, aur daudne-koodne mein hone wala dard bhi. Kuch ladkiyan chupchaap games chhod deti hain, theek usi umar mein jab unki chest bounce karne lagti hai. Iska solution sahi bra hai, bench par baithna nahi. Bade breasts se gardan, kandhe aur kamar mein dard bhi ho sakta hai; jis adult ko lagataar dard ho, woh doctor se options discuss kar sakti hai, surgery samet.

## Puberty mein ladkon ki chest

Puberty ke dauraan bahut se ladkon ko ek ya dono nipples ke neeche thodi hard, kabhi-kabhi dukhne wali swelling ho jaati hai. Doctors ise gynaecomastia kehte hain. Yeh normal hormone changes ki wajah se hota hai, aur zyada tar ladkon mein kuch mahino se lekar ek-do saal mein apne aap theek ho jaata hai. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki ladka "ladki ban raha hai", aur yeh masturbation ya "garam" ya "thandi" cheezein khaane se nahi hota.

Phir bhi doctor ko dikhana chahiye agar lump hard ho, sirf ek side ho, tezi se badh raha ho, usme se fluid nikle ya puberty ke baad bhi bana rahe. Gym steroids aur kuch medicines se bhi mardon ki chest swell ho sakti hai; iske baare mein hamari men's body checks wali guide mein detail hai. Mardon ko bhi breast cancer ho sakta hai; yeh rare hai, lekin mard ki chest mein lump ko kabhi ignore nahi karna chahiye [[who-breast-cancer]].

Jo trans aur non-binary teenagers apni chest bind karte hain, unhe sirf isi kaam ke liye bane binders use karne chahiye, bandage ya tape kabhi nahi, aur beech-beech mein break lena chahiye taaki skin aur pasliyon ko aaram mile.

## Breast awareness: apna normal pehchano

Yeh aadat isliye zaroori hai. Breast cancer Indian women mein sabse common cancer hai: 2024 mein estimated 2,37,231 naye cases aur 96,100 deaths, aur women ke saare cancers mein iska hissa 30.4% hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Phir bhi 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 0.6% women ne kabhi breast cancer screening test karwaya tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Teenagers ko breast cancer bahut kam hota hai, aur zyada tar breast lumps cancer nahi hote [[who-breast-cancer]]. 16 ki umar mein apna normal samajhne ka fayda yeh hai ki 40 ki umar mein kuch badle toh tumhe turant pata chale. WHO ke hisaab se in signs par action lena chahiye: lump ya mota hissa, aksar bina dard ke; size ya shape mein badlaav; skin mein gaddhe, laali ya pitting; nipple ya uske aas-paas ki skin mein badlaav; aur nipple se khoon wala ya ajeeb fluid [[who-breast-cancer]].

Survey yeh nahi batata ki yeh figure itna kam kyun hai, aur services tak pahunch bhi ek wajah hai. Lekin sharm madad nahi karti: jis ladki ko 13 mein apni chest chhupana sikhaya gaya, woh 45 mein lump doctor ko dikhane mein jhijhak sakti hai.

Teenagers Adolescent Friendly Health Centres mein confidential advice le sakte hain, jo primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein hote hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Adults kisi bhi government hospital ja sakte hain. Tum female doctor maang sakti ho, ya examination ke time kisi aur aurat ko saath rakhne ko keh sakti ho.

Us shaadi wale cousins ko lecture nahi chahiye. Unhe bas ek adult chahiye jo kahe: tum badh rahe ho, tum normal ho, aur agar kabhi kuch pareshaan kare, toh hum saath mein doctor ke paas chalenge.

cloth-periods-water-soap-privacy.en:
Nearly half of India's young women, 49.6% of those aged 15-24, used cloth during their periods in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In the National Family Health Survey, a woman who relies on cloth alone is counted as not using a "hygienic" method. The survey records which product she uses. It does not ask the questions that decide whether her period is actually safe: was there clean water, was there soap, and was there a private place to wash the cloth and dry it in the sun?

## Myth: cloth is dirty

The myth goes like this. Cloth is old-fashioned and dirty, pads are modern and clean, and a girl using cloth is a health problem waiting to happen. The survey's definition seems to agree: it counts sanitary napkins, tampons, menstrual cups and even locally prepared napkins as hygienic, but not cloth [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Period blood does not make cloth dirty in some special way. A period is simply the part of the menstrual cycle when a woman bleeds from her vagina for a few days [[nhs-periods]]. Any cloth that soaks up blood has to be washed well and dried fully, like any other cloth. Britain's National Health Service lists reusable washable pads among ordinary period products [[nhs-periods]]. What matters is not the material but whether it can be kept clean.

## What the survey counts, and what it misses

The numbers do show change. In 2015-16, 62.1% of young women used cloth and 41.8% used sanitary napkins, and 57.6% used a method the survey counts as hygienic [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. By 2019-21, cloth was down to 49.6%, napkins were up to 64.4%, and the "hygienic" share had reached 77.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. (Menstrual cups were counted as hygienic only in the later round.)

Many women use more than one method, which is why the figures add up to more than the whole [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Picture, as an example, a college student in Patna who buys pads for long days outside and uses cloth at home to make a packet last. She sits in both columns.

What the survey misses is everything that decides whether either method is safe. It does not ask whether she had clean water, soap, a door that locks, or a sunny spot where wet cloth can dry without anyone objecting. A pad that cannot be changed for a whole school day is still counted as hygienic. A clean cloth, washed with soap and dried in the sun, is not.

## Who uses cloth, and why

The poorer the home, the more likely a girl is to rely on cloth. In 2019-21, 95.1% of young women in the richest households used a method the survey counts as hygienic. In the poorest households only 53.6% did, so nearly half used nothing the survey counts as hygienic [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The full divide, by schooling, village and tribe, is a separate story in this section. The point here is narrower.

This gap tracks money, not how much a girl cares about being clean. Pads cost money every month. Cloth is already in the house. Calling cloth "dirty" shames the girls who have the least, and it leaves the real problem untouched.

## Truth: how to use cloth safely

Cloth is safe when it is clean, dry and used only by you. The basics:

- Use soft cotton cloth. Synthetic fabric soaks up less and stays damp.
- Rinse it in cold water first, then wash it with soap and clean water.
- Dry it completely, in direct sunlight if you can. Cloth that stays damp, folded away under other clothes, can grow germs.
- Store dry cloth in a clean bag or box.
- Change it whenever it feels wet. Do not wear one piece all day.
- Wash your hands before and after changing.
- Never share cloth. Replace pieces that turn thin, hard or stained, or that smell even after washing.
- See a doctor or health worker for itching, a bad smell, unusual discharge or burning while passing urine. These need checking whatever method you use.

## Water and privacy, not just pads

Every one of those steps needs water, soap and privacy. That is why the Supreme Court's judgment of 30 January 2026 in Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India matters beyond free pads. The court held that menstrual health is part of the right to life under Article 21. It ordered all schools to provide working, separate toilets for girls with water, along with free sanitary napkins and safe disposal [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. It also ordered handwashing facilities, and it tied the right to menstrual health to the right to a dignified existence [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

Schools are where the gap shows first. About a quarter of adolescent girls in India (24%) missed school during their periods, according to a 2016 review that pooled Indian studies [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. A girl who cannot change, wash or even find water at school has a simple choice: sit through the day with wet cloth, or stay home.

The buildings have not caught up with the order. In an affidavit of 31 August 2026, the Centre told the court that of 39,439 girls' toilets identified as needing to be made functional, 4,745 were still a gap and 4,236 were under construction [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. How the states stalled is a story of its own. For a girl with cloth in her school bag, a toilet "under construction" means another month with no water and no lock.

Free pads are the part of the ruling that makes headlines. Water is the part that decides whether any method, pad or cloth, is safe. A girl with clean cloth, soap, a tap and a door that locks can manage her period safely. A girl with a free pad and no working toilet cannot. So the question to ask a school, a village or a family is not "pad or cloth?" It is "water, soap and privacy, or not?"
cloth-periods-water-soap-privacy.hg:
India mein 15-24 saal ki lagbhag aadhi ladkiyan aur women, yaani 49.6%, 2019-21 mein periods ke dauraan cloth use karti thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. National Family Health Survey (NFHS) mein jo woman sirf kapde pe depend karti hai, use "hygienic" method use karne walon mein nahi gina jaata. Survey bas yeh poochta hai ki tum kya use karti ho. Asli sawaal woh poochta hi nahi: kya saaf paani tha, kya sabun tha, aur kya kapda dhone aur dhoop mein sukhane ke liye koi private jagah thi? Period safe hai ya nahi, yeh inhi sawaalon se decide hota hai.

## Myth: kapda ganda hota hai

Myth kuch aisa hai. Kapda purane zamane ki cheez hai aur ganda hai, pads modern hain aur saaf hain, aur jo ladki cloth use karti hai woh bimaari ko invite kar rahi hai. Survey ki definition bhi yahi kehti lagti hai: woh sanitary napkins, tampons, menstrual cups aur locally bane napkins ko bhi "hygienic" ginta hai, par kapde ko nahi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Period ka blood kapde ko kisi special tarah se ganda nahi karta. Period bas menstrual cycle ka woh hissa hai jab kuch dinon tak vagina se bleeding hoti hai [[nhs-periods]]. Jis bhi kapde mein blood soak hua ho, use achhe se dhona aur poora sukhana padta hai, jaise kisi bhi doosre kapde ko. UK ki government health service NHS bhi reusable washable pads ko normal period products mein ginti hai [[nhs-periods]]. Matlab baat material ki nahi hai, baat yeh hai ki use saaf rakha ja sakta hai ya nahi.

## Survey kya ginta hai, aur kya miss karta hai

Numbers mein change clearly dikhta hai. 2015-16 mein 62.1% young women cloth use karti thi aur 41.8% sanitary napkins, aur 57.6% aisa method use karti thi jise survey hygienic maanta hai [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. 2019-21 tak cloth ghat kar 49.6% reh gaya, napkins badh kar 64.4% ho gaye, aur "hygienic" wala share 77.6% tak pahunch gaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. (Menstrual cups ko hygienic sirf baad wale round mein gina gaya.)

Kai women ek se zyada method use karti hain, isliye yeh figures jodo toh total se zyada aata hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ek example socho: Patna ki ek college student. Bahar ke lambe dinon ke liye woh pads khareedti hai, aur ghar pe cloth use karti hai taaki packet zyada din chale. Woh dono columns mein aati hai.

Survey wahi cheezein miss kar deta hai jo decide karti hain ki koi bhi method safe hai ya nahi. Woh nahi poochta ki saaf paani tha ya nahi, sabun tha ya nahi, darwaze pe lock tha ya nahi, ya dhoop mein koi aisi jagah thi jahan geela kapda bina kisi ke toke sookh sake. Jo pad poore school day mein badla hi na ja sake, use bhi hygienic gina jaata hai. Aur sabun se dhula, dhoop mein sookha saaf kapda? Woh nahi gina jaata.

## Cloth kaun use karta hai, aur kyun

Ghar jitna gareeb, utna zyada chance ki ladki cloth pe depend karegi. 2019-21 mein sabse ameer gharon ki 95.1% young women aisa method use karti thi jise survey hygienic maanta hai. Sabse gareeb gharon mein yeh sirf 53.6% tha, yaani lagbhag aadhi women aisa kuch use nahi karti thi jise survey hygienic ginta ho [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Padhai, gaon aur tribe ke hisaab se poora divide is section mein ek alag story hai. Yahan point thoda alag hai.

Yeh gap paise ka hai, is baat ka nahi ki kis ladki ko safai ki kitni parwah hai. Pads ke liye har mahine paise lagte hain. Kapda ghar mein pehle se hota hai. Cloth ko "ganda" bolna unhi ladkiyon ko sharminda karta hai jinke paas sabse kam hai, aur asli problem waisi ki waisi reh jaati hai.

## Truth: cloth safely kaise use karein

Cloth tab safe hai jab woh saaf ho, sookha ho aur sirf tumhara ho. Basics:

- Soft cotton ka kapda lo. Synthetic kapda kam soak karta hai aur geela rehta hai.
- Pehle thande paani mein khangalo, phir sabun aur saaf paani se dho.
- Kapda poora sukhao, ho sake toh direct dhoop mein. Jo kapda doosre kapdon ke neeche daba, geela pada rahe, usme germs pal sakte hain.
- Sookha kapda kisi saaf thaili ya dabbe mein rakho.
- Kapda geela lage toh badal lo. Ek hi kapda poora din mat pehno.
- Kapda badalne se pehle aur baad mein haath dho.
- Apna kapda kabhi share mat karo. Jo kapda patla, sakht ya daag wala ho jaye, ya dhone ke baad bhi badboo de, use replace kar do.
- Khujli, badboo, ajeeb discharge ya peshaab mein jalan ho toh doctor ya health worker ko dikhao. Method koi bhi ho, iski checking zaroori hai.

## Sirf pads nahi, paani aur privacy bhi

In sab steps ke liye paani, sabun aur privacy chahiye. Isiliye Supreme Court ka 30 January 2026 ka judgment, Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India, free pads se kahin aage ki baat hai. Court ne kaha ki menstrual health Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa hai. Court ne saare schools ko order diya ki ladkiyon ke liye alag, chalu toilets hon, unme paani ho, free sanitary napkins milein aur used pads ko safely phenkne ka system ho [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Court ne haath dhone ki facility ka bhi order diya, aur menstrual health ke right ko izzat se jeene ke right (dignified existence) se joda [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

School mein yeh gap sabse pehle dikhta hai. 2016 ke ek review ne India ki kai studies ko saath jod kar dekha, aur paaya ki lagbhag ek-chauthai, yaani 24% adolescent girls periods ke dinon mein school miss karti thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Jis ladki ko school mein kapda badalne, dhone ya paani tak ki facility na mile, uske paas do hi raaste hain: poora din geele kapde mein baithe, ya ghar pe rahe.

Ground pe kaam abhi order se peeche hai. 31 August 2026 ke affidavit mein Centre ne court ko bataya ki ladkiyon ke 39,439 toilets aise identify hue the jinhe chalu karna tha. Inme se 4,745 ki kami abhi bhi baaki thi aur 4,236 abhi ban hi rahe the [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. States ne is ruling ko kaise lataka diya, woh apne aap mein alag story hai. Par jis ladki ke school bag mein kapda hai, uske liye "under construction" toilet ka matlab hai ek aur mahina, bina paani aur bina lock ke.

Free pads wali baat headlines mein aati hai. Par paani decide karta hai ki koi bhi method, pad ho ya cloth, safe hai ya nahi. Jis ladki ke paas saaf kapda, sabun, nal aur lock wala darwaza hai, woh apna period safely manage kar sakti hai. Jiske paas free pad hai par chalu toilet nahi, woh nahi kar sakti. Toh school, gaon ya family se poochne wala sawaal "pad ya cloth?" nahi hai. Sawaal hai: "paani, sabun aur privacy hai, ya nahi?"

colourism-body-shaming-mental-health.en:
Imagine a 22-year-old in Lucknow whose parents have just put up her matrimonial profile. The first question every aunty asks is not about her degree. It is "rang kaisa hai?" Since she was 12 she has been told to stay out of the sun, rub besan and haldi on her face and eat less rice. Her 19-year-old brother is called "chhotu" and "sukha" at every function, and has started buying protein powders online. Neither of them would call this a mental-health problem. Over years, it can become one.

## Skin, weight, height: the comments that start at home

In many Indian homes, appearance is treated as a qualification. A newborn is praised for being "gora". A dark-skinned girl is told she will be "hard to marry". A heavier child is "motu" at school and "healthy" at home, said in a tone that means the opposite. Boys are graded on height and muscle, girls on skin and weight, and the matrimonial market writes those grades down as "fair, slim, tall".

Families usually mean it as care: "tere bhale ke liye bol rahe hain." But a comment repeated at every meal and every wedding teaches a child one lesson: your body decides your worth, and your body is not good enough. People with acne, vitiligo, a disability or a body that does not fit the template hear it loudest.

## The fairness business

Shame is profitable. Fairness creams, soaps and face washes for women and men line chemist shelves, and many photo apps offer "beauty" filters that lighten skin. Some brands have swapped the word "fair" for "bright" or "glow", but the promise of a lighter face is the same.

Skin colour is set mostly by genes and by melanin, the pigment that protects skin from the sun. No cream changes your genes. Some creams sold over the counter contain steroids. Used to lighten skin, they can thin it and cause acne, redness and rashes, and stopping suddenly can make the skin worse. Use a steroid cream only when a doctor prescribes it, for the condition and the time they prescribe.

## From shame to anxiety, depression and eating disorders

India's National Mental Health Survey, run by NIMHANS in 2015-16, found that 10.6% of adults had a mental disorder at the time of the survey and 13.7% had had one at some point in life [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Nearly 150 million Indians needed mental-health care, but fewer than 30 million were seeking it [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. For mental disorders, the treatment gap ranged from 28% to 83% [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]].

Overall, men were more affected (13.9% against 7.5% of women), and alcohol use disorder affected 9% of men against 0.5% of women. But depression and anxiety disorders were more common among women [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Women are also the people matrimonial profiles grade as "fair" and "slim"; the survey cannot show whether the two are linked, but the overlap is worth noticing.

The survey never asked about colourism or body-shaming, so no national number says how much distress appearance comments cause. The headline figures cover adults, not the teenagers who take those comments hardest, and they are a decade old. WHO counts pressure to conform with peers among the stresses of adolescence, and says media influence and gender norms can widen the gap between an adolescent's lived reality and their aspirations [[who-adolescent-mh]]. It also notes that eating disorders commonly begin in adolescence and young adulthood [[who-adolescent-mh]].

Eating disorders are serious mental-health conditions in which food becomes a way to cope with feelings. Signs include spending a lot of time worrying about weight and body shape, eating very little, avoiding meals with others, strict rules around food, exercising too much, and feeling cold, tired or dizzy; girls' periods may stop [[nhs-eating-disorders]]. Anyone can develop one, including boys and men; for some, the worry is about being too small rather than too big. Eating disorders can be treated, and people recover [[nhs-eating-disorders]].

## Pushing back: what to say, what to stop saying

You cannot rewrite your family overnight, but you can change what is said in front of you.

- **Stop the comment.** "Please don't talk about my body. If you're worried about my health, ask me how I am." Say it calmly, every time.
- **Drop the nicknames.** "Kaalu", "motu", "chhotu" and "sukha" are not affectionate when the person has never been allowed to object.
- **Parents:** praise effort and kindness, not looks. Do not compare siblings, and never put a child on a diet without a doctor.
- **Friends:** do not forward "glow-up" memes or rate people's photos in group chats. If online body-shaming turns sexual, or someone morphs or circulates a photo, it can be a crime; report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 [[cybercrime-portal]].
- **Marriage:** families can refuse to list skin colour in a profile, and refuse proposals that ask for "fair".

## Where to get help

If shame about your body is affecting your food, sleep, studies or relationships, call Tele-MANAS on 14416. It is the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock mental-health helpline, running since October 2022 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Teenagers can get confidential counselling at Adolescent Friendly Health Centres in primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. College counsellors and family doctors can refer you to a psychiatrist or psychologist.

If you are having thoughts of ending your life, call 14416 now, or 112 in an emergency. You do not have to earn help by being "sick enough".

The woman in Lucknow does not need a lighter face, and her brother does not need a bigger chest. They need the people around them to stop grading their bodies.
colourism-body-shaming-mental-health.hg:
Lucknow ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ko imagine karo jiske parents ne abhi-abhi uska matrimonial profile daala hai. Har aunty ka pehla sawaal uski degree ke baare mein nahi hota. Sawaal hota hai, "rang kaisa hai?" 12 saal ki umar se use bola ja raha hai ki dhoop mein mat niklo, chehre par besan-haldi lagao aur chawal kam khao. Uske 19 saal ke bhai ko har function mein "chhotu" aur "sukha" bulaya jaata hai, aur usne online protein powders khareedna shuru kar diya hai. Dono mein se koi ise mental-health problem nahi kahega. Lekin saalon tak chalta rahe, toh yeh wahi ban sakta hai.

## Skin, weight, height: woh comments jo ghar se shuru hote hain

Bahut se Indian gharon mein looks ko qualification ki tarah treat kiya jaata hai. Newborn ki tareef hoti hai ki "gora" hai. Saanwli ladki ko bola jaata hai ki uski "shaadi mushkil se hogi". Bhaari bachcha school mein "motu" hota hai aur ghar mein "healthy", us tone mein jiska matlab ulta hota hai. Ladkon ko height aur muscle par grade kiya jaata hai, ladkiyon ko skin aur weight par, aur matrimonial market in grades ko "fair, slim, tall" likhkar pakka kar deta hai.

Families aksar ise fikar hi samajhti hain: "tere bhale ke liye bol rahe hain." Lekin jo comment har khaane par aur har shaadi mein dohraya jaaye, woh bachche ko ek hi sabak sikhata hai: tumhari body tumhari value tay karti hai, aur tumhari body kaafi achhi nahi hai. Jinhe acne hai, vitiligo hai, koi disability hai ya jinki body template mein fit nahi hoti, unhe yeh sabse zor se sunna padta hai.

## Fairness ka business

Sharm se paisa banta hai. Women aur men dono ke liye fairness creams, soaps aur face washes chemist ki shelves par bhare pade hain, aur bahut se photo apps mein "beauty" filters hain jo skin ko halka kar dete hain. Kuch brands ne "fair" word ki jagah "bright" ya "glow" likhna shuru kar diya, lekin halke chehre ka promise wahi hai.

Skin ka colour zyada tar genes aur melanin se tay hota hai, woh pigment jo skin ko dhoop se bachata hai. Koi cream tumhare genes nahi badal sakti. Bina prescription ke bikne wali kuch creams mein steroids hote hain. Skin halki karne ke liye lagane par yeh skin ko patla kar sakte hain aur acne, redness aur rashes de sakte hain, aur achanak band karne par skin aur kharab ho sakti hai. Steroid cream sirf tab use karo jab doctor prescribe kare, usi condition ke liye aur utne hi time ke liye jitna doctor bataye.

## Sharm se anxiety, depression aur eating disorders tak

India ke National Mental Health Survey ne, jo NIMHANS ne 2015-16 mein kiya tha, paaya ki 10.6% adults ko survey ke waqt koi mental disorder tha aur 13.7% ko zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi raha tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Kareeb 150 million Indians ko mental-health care ki zaroorat thi, lekin 30 million se kam log care dhoondh rahe the [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Mental disorders ke liye treatment gap 28% se 83% tak tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]].

Overall, mardon par asar zyada tha (13.9%, jabki women mein 7.5%), aur alcohol use disorder 9% mardon mein tha aur sirf 0.5% women mein. Lekin depression aur anxiety disorders women mein zyada common the [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Matrimonial profiles mein "fair" aur "slim" ka grade bhi zyada tar women par hi lagta hai; survey yeh nahi bata sakta ki dono judi hui hain ya nahi, lekin yeh overlap notice karne layak hai.

Survey ne colourism ya body-shaming ke baare mein kabhi poocha hi nahi, isliye koi national number nahi batata ki looks par hone wale comments kitni takleef dete hain. Headline figures adults ke hain, un teenagers ke nahi jin par yeh comments sabse bhaari padte hain, aur yeh ek dashak purane hain. WHO peers ke jaisa banne ke pressure ko adolescence ke stress mein ginta hai, aur kehta hai ki media influence aur gender norms us gap ko aur bada kar sakte hain jo ek adolescent ki asli zindagi aur uski aspirations ke beech hota hai [[who-adolescent-mh]]. WHO yeh bhi kehta hai ki eating disorders aam taur par adolescence aur young adulthood mein shuru hote hain [[who-adolescent-mh]].

Eating disorders serious mental-health conditions hain jinme khaana feelings se cope karne ka tareeka ban jaata hai. Signs mein yeh shaamil hain: weight aur body shape ki chinta mein bahut time bitana, bahut kam khaana, doosron ke saath khaane se bachna, khaane ko lekar sakht rules, zaroorat se zyada exercise, aur thand lagna, thakaan ya chakkar aana; ladkiyon ke periods ruk sakte hain [[nhs-eating-disorders]]. Yeh kisi ko bhi ho sakta hai, ladkon aur mardon ko bhi; kuch ke liye chinta bahut bade hone ki nahi, bahut chhote ya patle hone ki hoti hai. Eating disorders ka ilaaj ho sakta hai, aur log recover karte hain [[nhs-eating-disorders]].

## Jawab dena: kya kehna hai, kya kehna band karna hai

Tum apni family ko raaton-raat nahi badal sakte, lekin yeh badal sakte ho ki tumhare saamne kya bola jaata hai.

- **Comment ko roko.** "Please meri body ke baare mein baat mat kijiye. Agar aapko meri health ki fikar hai, toh mera haal pooch lijiye." Shaanti se kaho, har baar.
- **Nicknames chhodo.** "Kaalu", "motu", "chhotu" aur "sukha" pyaar ke naam nahi hain jab us insaan ko kabhi mana karne ka mauka hi nahi mila.
- **Parents:** mehnat aur achhe bartaav ki tareef karo, looks ki nahi. Bhai-behnon ko compare mat karo, aur doctor ke bina bachche ko kabhi diet par mat daalo.
- **Friends:** "glow-up" memes forward mat karo aur group chats mein logon ki photos ko rate mat karo. Agar online body-shaming sexual ho jaaye, ya koi photo morph kare ya circulate kare, toh yeh crime ho sakta hai; cybercrime.gov.in par report karo ya 1930 call karo [[cybercrime-portal]].
- **Shaadi:** families profile mein skin colour likhne se mana kar sakti hain, aur un proposals ko bhi mana kar sakti hain jo "fair" maangte hain.

## Madad kahan milegi

Agar apni body ko lekar sharm tumhare khaane, neend, padhai ya relationships par asar daal rahi hai, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call karo. Yeh Health Ministry ki free, din-raat chalne wali mental-health helpline hai, jo October 2022 se chal rahi hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Teenagers ko Adolescent Friendly Health Centres mein confidential counselling mil sakti hai, jo primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein hote hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. College counsellors aur family doctors tumhe psychiatrist ya psychologist ke paas refer kar sakte hain.

Agar tumhe apni zindagi khatam karne ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh abhi 14416 call karo, ya emergency mein 112. Madad paane ke liye tumhe pehle "kaafi beemar" saabit hona zaroori nahi hai.

Lucknow wali us ladki ko halka chehra nahi chahiye, aur uske bhai ko badi chest nahi chahiye. Unhe bas yeh chahiye ki aas-paas ke log unki bodies ko grade karna band karein.

endometriosis-pain-dismissed-diagnosis-d.en:
Imagine a 15-year-old in Indore who misses two days of school every month because of period pain. Her mother says "sab ko hota hai": everyone gets it. An aunt says it will settle after marriage. The chemist hands over a painkiller. Years later, married and trying for a baby, she hears the word endometriosis for the first time. She is imaginary. The delay is not. WHO puts the average time to an endometriosis diagnosis at 4-12 years [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. For all of that time the pain was there. What was missing was someone who believed it.

## 'Sab ko hota hai': how pain gets normalised

Period pain is dismissed in three places. At home, because the women of the family often had pain too and nobody treated theirs. At school, because nobody explained what a normal period looks like. Only about half of adolescent girls in India (48%) had been told about menstruation before their first period, according to a 2016 review of studies [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. A girl who was never told what normal is has no way to know that her pain is not.

And sometimes in the clinic. WHO says that in many countries the public, families and most health workers do not realise that this kind of chronic pelvic pain is not normal [[who-endometriosis]]. A painkiller is quicker than an investigation, and "it will be fine after marriage" ends the conversation. Marriage is not a treatment for anything. That advice only tells a girl that her pain will matter once it affects a husband or a pregnancy.

## What endometriosis is

Endometriosis is a chronic disease in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, most often in the pelvis. It causes inflammation and scar tissue, and can affect someone from her first period until menopause [[who-endometriosis]].

WHO estimates that it affects 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide, about 190 million [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. India has no reliable estimate of its own, and the global 10% should not be applied to India as if it had been measured here. It is not the only common condition that goes unnamed: WHO estimates that up to 70% of women with PCOS do not know they have it [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]].

## Symptoms that are not normal

Cramps on the first day or two of a period are common. These are not:

- period pain so severe that you miss school, college or work;
- pain that ordinary painkillers do not control, or that makes you vomit or faint;
- pain that gets worse year after year;
- pain in the pelvis between periods, or pain during or after sex;
- pain while passing stool or urine during your period;
- very heavy bleeding, bloating, nausea or constant tiredness along with the pain.

Most of these are on WHO's list of endometriosis symptoms, which also includes anxiety, depression and infertility [[who-endometriosis]].

WHO says endometriosis is associated with infertility [[who-endometriosis]]. Infertility itself is common: about 17.5% of adults worldwide, roughly 1 in 6, experience it at some point in their lives [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. It affects men as well as women, and endometriosis is only one of its causes. But for some women, a fertility clinic is the first place where pain they were told to ignore gets a name.

## Why diagnosis takes years

Part of the delay lies in the disease itself. WHO notes that symptoms vary widely from person to person, which makes it hard for health workers to recognise [[who-endometriosis]]. WHO says a careful history of pain and bleeding can help, along with imaging such as an ultrasound or MRI. Sometimes keyhole surgery, called laparoscopy, is needed to confirm the disease, but treatment does not always have to wait for surgery [[who-endometriosis]].

Then there are the shortcuts that sell delay. Advertising medicines for period problems is illegal in India. Section 3 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans advertising any drug for "the correction of menstrual disorder in women" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].
