Ulti galti hai jaldbaazi ka label. Yeh kitni baar hota hai, is par hume koi national data nahi mila. Par risk samajhna mushkil nahi hai. Periods shuru hone ke baad ke pehle kuch saalon mein irregular cycles normal ho sakte hain, aur WHO kehta hai ki health workers ko insaan ki life stage dhyaan mein rakhni chahiye [[who-pcos]]. Us umar mein ek scan, bina hormone test aur bina follow-up ke, ek normal teenage cycle ko zindagi bhar ka label bana sakta hai.

Dono galtiyon ki keemat hai. Miss hua diagnosis matlab saalon tak diabetes ya heart risk ka koi check nahi. Galat diagnosis matlab darr, aisi pills jinki shayad zaroorat hi na ho, aur bahut si families mein "shaadi ki problem", jahan shayad koi medical problem hai hi nahi.

## Ek sahi check-up mein kya-kya hona chahiye?

National study ek achha model hai. Uske researchers sirf scan par nahi ruke: unhone poore diagnostic criteria lagaaye, aur jin women mein PCOS mila unki metabolic health bhi naapi [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]].

Metabolic tests utne hi zaroori hain jitna label. Study mein PCOS wali women mein 91.9% ke blood lipids abnormal the, 32.9% ko fatty liver disease thi, 24.9% ko metabolic syndrome tha aur 43.2% ko obesity thi [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. WHO ki salaah hai ki jin women ko PCOS abhi-abhi diagnose hua hai, unke insulin resistance aur heart risk ke liye aur blood tests hon [[who-pcos]].

Ek sahi work-up aisa dikhta hai:

- tumhare periods ki history, behtar ho ki likhe hue record se, kyunki cycle ki length har insaan mein alag hoti hai aur asli baat kai mahinon ka tumhara apna pattern hai [[nhs-periods]];
- high androgens ke signs ki jaanch, aur signs saaf na hon toh blood test;
- aise tests jo thyroid ki problem, high prolactin aur pregnancy ko rule out karein;
- jahan kaam ka ho wahan ultrasound, evidence ke ek tukde ki tarah, faisle ki tarah nahi;
- blood sugar, lipid profile, liver tests, weight, kamar ka naap aur blood pressure;
- tumhare mood ke baare mein sawaal, aur is baare mein ki tum apni body ko lekar kaisa feel karti ho, kyunki WHO PCOS ko anxiety, depression aur eating disorders se jodta hai [[who-pcos]].

## Doctor se kya poochun?

- Aap kaunse criteria use kar rahe hain, aur teen signs mein se mujhme kaunse hain?
- Aapne kya-kya rule out kiya, aur kaise?
- Kya mera blood sugar, cholesterol aur liver check hua hai, aur dobara kab check hona chahiye?
- Agar main teenager hoon, toh kya yeh abhi bhi normal shuruaati cycle ho sakta hai? Dobara kab dekhenge?
- Mere periods, meri skin aur baalon ke liye plan kya hai, aur agar mujhe kabhi pregnancy chahiye ho toh uske liye?

PCOS ka koi cure nahi hai, par treatment symptoms halke kar sakta hai aur long-term risks kam kar sakta hai [[who-pcos]]. "Shaadi ke baad theek ho jayega" par hamara myth-buster batata hai ki families women ko iske baare mein kya-kya kehti hain. Pehla step usse simple hai: aisa diagnosis jo rulebook se ho, ek scan se nahi.

pcos-myths-metabolic-not-marriage.en:
Imagine a 21-year-old in Lucknow whose periods come every two or three months. An aunt notices the hair on her chin and the weight she has put on, and says what many Indian families say: "Shaadi ke baad theek ho jayega." If anyone takes her to a clinic, the questions will be the ones a marriage market asks. Can she lose the weight? Can the hair be removed? Will she have children? Nobody asks about her blood. India's own research does. In an ICMR-funded national study, 91.9% of women with PCOS had abnormal blood fats and 32.9% had fatty liver disease [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. None of that shows in a mirror, and a wedding fixes none of it.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a long-term hormonal condition. WHO calls it a chronic metabolic condition that raises the long-term risk of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes and obesity [[who-pcos]]. Depending on which medical criteria are used, the same study found it in between 7.2% and 19.6% of Indian women aged 18-40 [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. Here are four things families say about it, and what the evidence says back.

## Myth 1: Marriage will fix it

The idea seems to be that a husband, sex or a pregnancy will "settle" the hormones. No such treatment exists. WHO says there is no cure for PCOS; treatment can improve quality of life and help with fertility [[who-pcos]]. A wedding changes a woman's address, not her insulin, her hormones or her ovaries.

What the myth does change is timing. A check-up gets postponed so that no "label" appears before the rishta. Then, if a pregnancy takes longer than the family expected, the condition nobody named becomes something she is blamed for. WHO estimates that up to 70% of women with PCOS worldwide do not know they have it [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]]. Treating PCOS as a marriage problem helps keep that number high. WHO also notes that symptoms such as infertility, obesity and unwanted hair carry social stigma that can damage family relationships, work and mental health [[who-pcos]].

## Myth 2: Only overweight women get PCOS

Weight is the sign families notice first, so it becomes the whole story: lose the weight and the problem goes away. In the national study, 43.2% of women with PCOS had obesity [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. That is a large share, but it also means more than half did not.

A slim young woman with irregular periods and acne can be told she "doesn't look like" someone with PCOS, and go years without a check. A heavier woman can be told her weight is the whole problem, and leave with a diet chart instead of a diagnosis. Both get the wrong message. Healthy eating and physical activity do matter in managing PCOS [[who-pcos]], but the metabolic risk shows up in blood tests, not only on a weighing scale.

## Myth 3: PCOS means you can never have children

The fear has a basis. WHO calls PCOS a leading cause of infertility [[who-pcos]]. But a leading cause of infertility is not a sentence of childlessness. PCOS often means the ovaries release eggs less regularly, so getting pregnant can take longer. WHO says women with PCOS can be supported to become pregnant, with treatments that include lifestyle changes, medicines or surgery to stimulate ovulation. They generally face a higher risk of complications in pregnancy, which is one more reason for regular care [[who-pcos]].

Infertility is also not a woman's problem alone. About 17.5% of adults worldwide, roughly 1 in 6, experience it at some point in their lives [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]], and that includes men. When a couple struggles to conceive, both partners need tests. A PCOS diagnosis does not make her the only suspect.

## Myth 4: A diet, a pill or an influencer can 'reverse' it

Search for PCOS on social media and you will find teas, seed mixes, supplements and 30-day plans that promise to "reverse" it. There is no cure to sell [[who-pcos]]. What works is slower and less photogenic: healthy eating, regular activity, and medicines a doctor chooses for each problem. Combined contraceptive pills, for example, can regulate the cycle and may reduce acne and extra hair [[who-pcos]]. Progress is measured in cycles and blood reports, not before-and-after photos.

Some of these ads are also illegal. Section 3 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans advertising any drug for "the correction of menstrual disorder in women" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. An ad for a pill, powder or tonic that claims to regulate your periods is exactly the kind of ad that law was written to stop.

## The truth: a metabolic condition to manage for life

Put the study's findings together and the picture has little to do with looks. Among women with PCOS, 91.9% had abnormal blood fats, 32.9% had fatty liver disease, 24.9% had metabolic syndrome (a cluster of risk factors for diabetes and heart disease) and 43.2% had obesity [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. These were women aged 18 to 40. WHO lists type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol, heart disease and liver disease among the conditions women with PCOS are at higher risk of, and recommends extra blood tests after a diagnosis [[who-pcos]].

So the useful questions are not "will she get married?" or "will it go after the baby?" They are: when were her blood sugar, cholesterol and liver last checked, and when is the next check? How is her mood? WHO says women with PCOS may experience anxiety, depression, eating disorders or a negative body image [[who-pcos]], and years of comments about her face and weight do not help. Our explainer on how PCOS is diagnosed sets out what a full check-up should include.

PCOS is managed the way a thyroid problem is managed: over years, with check-ups, and without shame. That care can start at 17 or 21. It does not need to wait for a wedding date.
pcos-myths-metabolic-not-marriage.hg:
Socho, Lucknow ki ek 21 saal ki ladki jiske periods do-teen mahine mein ek baar aate hain. Ek aunty uski chin ke baal aur badhta weight notice karti hain, aur wahi kehti hain jo bahut saari Indian families kehti hain: "Shaadi ke baad theek ho jayega." Agar koi use clinic le bhi jaye, toh sawaal wahi honge jo rishton ka market poochta hai. Weight kam hoga? Baal hat jayenge? Bachche honge? Uske blood ke baare mein koi nahi poochta. India ki apni research poochti hai. Ek ICMR-funded national study mein PCOS wali 91.9% women ke blood fats abnormal the aur 32.9% ko fatty liver disease thi [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. Inme se kuch bhi mirror mein nahi dikhta, aur shaadi inme se kuch bhi theek nahi karti.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) ek lamba chalne wala hormonal condition hai. WHO ise ek chronic metabolic condition kehta hai, jisse aage chal ke insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes aur obesity ka risk badhta hai [[who-pcos]]. Kaunse medical criteria use hue, uske hisaab se isi study ne 18-40 saal ki Indian women mein 7.2% se 19.6% tak PCOS paaya [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. Yeh rahi chaar baatein jo families iske baare mein kehti hain, aur unpe evidence ka jawaab.

## Myth 1: Shaadi se theek ho jayega

Soch shayad yeh hai ki husband, sex ya pregnancy hormones ko "settle" kar degi. Aisa koi treatment exist hi nahi karta. WHO kehta hai ki PCOS ka koi cure nahi hai; treatment quality of life behtar kar sakta hai aur fertility mein madad kar sakta hai [[who-pcos]]. Shaadi se ek ladki ka address badalta hai, uska insulin, uske hormones ya uski ovaries nahi.

Haan, yeh myth timing zaroor badal deta hai. Check-up taal diya jaata hai taaki rishte se pehle koi "label" na lag jaye. Phir agar pregnancy mein family ki umeed se zyada time lage, toh jis condition ka kabhi naam hi nahi liya gaya, uska blame usi pe daal diya jaata hai. WHO ka estimate hai ki duniya bhar mein PCOS wali 70% tak women ko pata hi nahi ki unhe yeh hai [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]]. PCOS ko shaadi ki problem samajhna is number ko high rakhne mein madad karta hai. WHO yeh bhi kehta hai ki infertility, obesity aur unwanted baal jaise symptoms ke saath social stigma juda hai, jo family relationships, kaam aur mental health ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai [[who-pcos]].

## Myth 2: PCOS sirf overweight women ko hota hai

Families sabse pehle weight notice karti hain, isliye wahi poori kahani ban jaata hai: weight kam karo, problem khatam. National study mein PCOS wali 43.2% women ko obesity thi [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. Yeh bada hissa hai, par iska matlab yeh bhi hai ki aadhe se zyada ko obesity nahi thi.

Ek patli ladki jiske periods irregular hain aur acne hai, use bola ja sakta hai ki woh PCOS wali "lagti hi nahi", aur woh saalon bina check-up ke reh jaati hai. Ek heavy ladki ko bola ja sakta hai ki uska weight hi poori problem hai, aur woh diagnosis ki jagah diet chart lekar ghar laut aati hai. Dono ko galat message milta hai. Healthy khana aur physical activity PCOS manage karne mein sach mein matter karte hain [[who-pcos]], par metabolic risk blood tests mein dikhta hai, sirf weighing scale pe nahi.

## Myth 3: PCOS hai toh kabhi bachche nahi honge

Is darr ki ek wajah hai. WHO PCOS ko infertility ki ek leading wajah kehta hai [[who-pcos]]. Par infertility ki leading wajah hona bachche na hone ki sazaa nahi hai. PCOS mein aksar ovaries kam regular tareeke se egg release karti hain, isliye pregnancy mein zyada time lag sakta hai. WHO kehta hai ki PCOS wali women ko pregnant hone mein support kiya ja sakta hai, aise treatments se jinme lifestyle changes, ovulation ko stimulate karne wali dawayein ya surgery shaamil hain. Unhe pregnancy mein complications ka risk generally zyada hota hai, jo regular care ki ek aur wajah hai [[who-pcos]].

Infertility akeli aurat ki problem bhi nahi hai. Duniya bhar mein lagbhag 17.5% adults, yaani roughly har 6 mein se 1, life mein kabhi na kabhi ise face karte hain [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]], aur ismein mard bhi shaamil hain. Jab ek couple ko conceive karne mein mushkil ho, toh dono partners ke tests hone chahiye. PCOS ka diagnosis use akeli suspect nahi bana deta.

## Myth 4: Koi diet, pill ya influencer ise 'reverse' kar sakta hai

Social media pe PCOS search karo toh chai, seeds ke mix, supplements aur 30-day plans milenge jo ise "reverse" karne ka promise karte hain. Bechne ke liye koi cure hai hi nahi [[who-pcos]]. Jo kaam karta hai woh slow hai aur photo mein utna achha nahi dikhta: healthy khana, regular activity, aur doctor ki chuni hui dawayein, har problem ke hisaab se. Jaise, combined contraceptive pills cycle regular kar sakti hain aur shayad acne aur extra baal bhi kam karein [[who-pcos]]. Progress cycles aur blood reports mein naapi jaati hai, before-and-after photos mein nahi.

Inme se kuch ads illegal bhi hain. Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 ka Section 3 kisi bhi aisi dawa ke ad pe rok lagata hai jo "the correction of menstrual disorder in women", yaani auraton ki period ki gadbad theek karne ke liye ho [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Kisi goli, powder ya tonic ka ad jo daava kare ki woh tumhare periods regular kar dega, bilkul usi tarah ka ad hai jise rokne ke liye yeh law bana tha.

## Sach: zindagi bhar manage karne wala metabolic condition

Study ke findings ko saath rakho toh tasveer ka looks se bahut kam lena-dena hai. PCOS wali women mein 91.9% ke blood fats abnormal the, 32.9% ko fatty liver disease thi, 24.9% ko metabolic syndrome tha (diabetes aur heart disease ke risk factors ka ek group) aur 43.2% ko obesity thi [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. Yeh 18 se 40 saal ki women thi. WHO type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol, heart disease aur liver disease ko un conditions mein ginta hai jinka risk PCOS wali women mein zyada hai, aur diagnosis ke baad extra blood tests ki salaah deta hai [[who-pcos]].

Toh kaam ke sawaal yeh nahi hain ki "shaadi hogi?" ya "baby ke baad chala jayega?" Sawaal yeh hain: uska blood sugar, cholesterol aur liver last kab check hua, aur agla check kab hai? Uska mood kaisa hai? WHO kehta hai ki PCOS wali women anxiety, depression, eating disorders ya negative body image face kar sakti hain [[who-pcos]], aur saalon tak chehre aur weight pe comments sunna kisi ki madad nahi karta. PCOS ka diagnosis kaise hota hai, is pe hamara explainer batata hai ki ek poore check-up mein kya-kya hona chahiye.

PCOS waise hi manage hota hai jaise thyroid ki problem: saalon tak, check-ups ke saath, aur bina sharm ke. Yeh care 17 ya 21 saal ki umar mein shuru ho sakti hai. Ise shaadi ki date ka intezaar karne ki zaroorat nahi.

period-leave-endometriosis-workplace.en:
Imagine a 27-year-old data-entry operator in Gurugram. For two days most months she can barely stand straight. She used up her sick leave by June, and her team lead jokes about her "monthly excuse". Nobody has told her that pain like hers can be a disease. Now imagine her cousin, who works on the family's fields in Vidarbha and has no leave to ask for at all. Both live in a country whose Supreme Court said on 30 January 2026 that menstrual health is part of the right to life under Article 21 [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Neither knows what that means for her working day.

## What is period leave, and what is it not?

Period leave, or menstrual leave, usually means a small number of paid days off that a worker can take during a painful period, often without a medical certificate and separate from ordinary sick leave. It is a workplace policy, not a treatment, and nobody should ever be made to take it.

The Supreme Court's January ruling does not create it. That case was about schoolgirls, and its directions were addressed to schools: working toilets with water, free sanitary pads and safe disposal [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. It sets a principle, that menstruation is a matter of health and dignity rather than shame, but it does not tell an employer what to do. Some employers and governments have announced period-leave rules of their own. Their terms vary, and this piece does not rate them. It looks at the evidence on pain, and at who any policy would actually reach.

## How bad can period pain get?

A period usually lasts between 2 and 7 days and comes back every 21 to 35 days [[nhs-periods]]. For many women the pain means cramps for a day or two. For some, it is a disease. WHO estimates that endometriosis, in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside it, affects about 10% of women of reproductive age, roughly 190 million worldwide, and takes on average 4 to 12 years to diagnose [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. We found no reliable estimate for India alone, so that global figure should not be read as an Indian one.

WHO is blunt about what the disease does to working life. Some people with endometriosis have debilitating pain that prevents them from going to work or school, which can mean lost income for them and their families. These harms, WHO adds, are made worse by stigma and by social beliefs that often ignore or downplay period pain [[who-endometriosis]].

Endometriosis is not the only condition that goes unnamed. WHO estimates that up to 70% of women with PCOS, a common cause of irregular and unpredictable periods, do not know they have it [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]]. A woman whose period can arrive without warning, at a workplace with no usable toilet, has a problem that toughness does not solve.

## What is the case for period leave?

The first argument is honesty. Periods already cost days. A 2016 review of Indian studies found that about a quarter (24%) of adolescent girls missed school during their periods [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. When girls like them start work, the bad days do not vanish. They get recorded as sick leave, unpaid leave or "unprofessional" behaviour. A named policy brings that hidden cost into the open.

The second is dignity. Describing your bleeding to a manager to get a day off is humiliating, and many women would rather work through pain than do it. A leave that needs no explanation removes that barrier.

The third is diagnosis. When severe pain becomes visible instead of being pushed through in silence, more women may ask why it hurts so much. With diagnosis taking 4 to 12 years [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]], anything that turns pain into a medical question rather than a test of endurance helps.

## What is the case against it?

The strongest objection is the hiring fear. If a rule makes women look costlier to employ than men, some employers may quietly hire fewer of them. In 2023-24, 41.7% of Indian women aged 15 and above were in the labour force, against 78.8% of men [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. In towns and cities, where working women are far more likely than in villages to hold regular salaried jobs, only 28.0% of women were in the labour force at all [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. A policy that gives employers one more excuse not to hire women would hurt the very people it means to help.

The second objection is reach. Period leave helps people with an employer, a payslip and a leave register. Among rural women workers in 2023-24, 73.5% were self-employed and only 7.8% had regular salaried jobs [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. For the cousin in Vidarbha, a period-leave rule changes nothing.

The third is stereotype. Some women worry that a special leave will feed the old idea that women are unreliable, or that every absence will be put down to "that time of the month". That is not an argument against taking pain seriously. It is an argument about how to do it.

## What can a fair workplace do, with or without a leave policy?

Most of what helps does not depend on what the policy is called:

- **Count period pain as sickness.** Sick leave should cover severe period pain, with no demand for intimate details.
- **Offer flexibility.** Where the job allows, let people shift their hours or work from home on the worst days.
- **Fix the basics.** A clean toilet with water, a bin for pads, and somewhere to lie down for a while. The Supreme Court ordered working toilets, free pads and safe disposal for every school [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. A workplace should not offer adults less.
- **Support diagnosis.** Health cover and time off for gynaecology appointments matter more than any number of leave days.
- **Train managers.** The joke about the "monthly excuse" is where many women decide to stay silent.

So what does a workplace owe the woman in Gurugram? At the very least, what the court has now promised every schoolgirl: a working toilet, no shame, and pain treated as a health matter. Whether that comes through a separate leave or through sick leave that actually covers her is a policy choice. Making her prove she is not faking it is not.
period-leave-endometriosis-workplace.hg:
Socho, Gurugram ki ek 27 saal ki data-entry operator. Zyadatar mahinon mein do din woh seedhi khadi bhi mushkil se ho paati hai. June tak uski sick leave khatam ho chuki hai, aur uska team lead uske "monthly bahaane" pe jokes maarta hai. Kisi ne use nahi bataya ki uske jaisa dard ek bimaari bhi ho sakta hai. Ab socho uski cousin ko, jo Vidarbha mein family ke kheton pe kaam karti hai aur jiske paas maangne ke liye koi chhutti hai hi nahi. Dono ek aise desh mein rehti hain jiske Supreme Court ne 30 January 2026 ko kaha ki menstrual health Article 21 ke under right to life ka hissa hai [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Dono mein se kisi ko nahi pata ki iska uske kaam ke din pe kya matlab hai.

## Period leave kya hai, aur kya nahi hai?

Period leave, ya menstrual leave, ka matlab usually kuch paid chhuttiyan hoti hain jo ek worker dard bhare period ke dauraan le sakta hai, aksar bina medical certificate ke aur normal sick leave se alag. Yeh workplace ki ek policy hai, koi ilaaj nahi, aur kisi ko bhi ise lene ke liye majboor nahi kiya jaana chahiye.

Supreme Court ka January wala faisla ise create nahi karta. Woh case school ki ladkiyon ke baare mein tha, aur uske directions schools ke liye the: paani wale working toilets, free sanitary pads aur safe disposal [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Yeh ek principle set karta hai, ki periods sharm ki nahi balki health aur dignity ki baat hain, par yeh kisi employer ko nahi batata ki use kya karna hai. Kuch employers aur governments ne apne period-leave rules announce kiye hain. Unki terms alag-alag hain, aur yeh article unhe rate nahi karta. Yeh dard ke evidence ko dekhta hai, aur yeh ki koi bhi policy asal mein kis tak pahunchegi.

## Period ka dard kitna bura ho sakta hai?

Period usually 2 se 7 din chalta hai aur har 21 se 35 din mein wapas aata hai [[nhs-periods]]. Bahut si auraton ke liye dard ka matlab ek-do din ke cramps hain. Kuch ke liye yeh ek bimaari hai. WHO ka estimate hai ki endometriosis, jisme uterus ki lining jaisa tissue uterus ke bahar badhne lagta hai, reproductive age ki lagbhag 10% women ko hai, yaani duniya bhar mein roughly 190 million, aur iska diagnosis hone mein average 4 se 12 saal lagte hain [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Humein sirf India ke liye koi reliable estimate nahi mila, isliye is global figure ko Indian figure na samjhein.

WHO saaf-saaf batata hai ki yeh bimaari kaam ki zindagi ke saath kya karti hai. Endometriosis wale kuch logon ko itna tez dard hota hai ki woh kaam ya school nahi ja paate, aur iska matlab unke aur unki families ke liye income ka nuksaan ho sakta hai. WHO aage kehta hai ki yeh nuksaan stigma aur un social beliefs se aur bada ho jaata hai jo period ke dard ko aksar ignore karte hain ya chhota bana dete hain [[who-endometriosis]].

Endometriosis akeli aisi condition nahi hai jiska naam hi nahi liya jaata. WHO ka estimate hai ki PCOS wali 70% tak women ko pata hi nahi ki unhe yeh hai [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]], jabki PCOS irregular aur unpredictable periods ki ek common wajah hai. Jis aurat ka period bina warning ke aa sakta hai, aur workplace pe koi usable toilet nahi hai, uski problem kisi bhi himmat se solve nahi hoti.

## Period leave ke paksh mein kya argument hai?

Pehla argument imaandari ka hai. Periods pehle se din cheen rahe hain. Indian studies ke ek 2016 review ke hisaab se lagbhag ek-chauthai (24%) adolescent girls periods ke dauraan school miss karti thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Jab aisi ladkiyan kaam shuru karti hain, toh woh bure din gayab nahi ho jaate. Woh sick leave, unpaid leave ya "unprofessional" behaviour ke naam se record hote hain. Ek naam wali policy is chhupi hui keemat ko saamne le aati hai.

Doosra argument dignity ka hai. Ek din ki chhutti ke liye manager ko apni bleeding ke baare mein batana humiliating hai, aur bahut si auratein aisa karne se behtar dard mein kaam karna samajhti hain. Jis leave ke liye koi explanation na dena pade, woh yeh rukaawat hata deti hai.

Teesra argument diagnosis ka hai. Jab tez dard chupchaap jhelne ki jagah dikhne lagta hai, toh zyada auratein pooch sakti hain ki itna dard kyun hota hai. Jab diagnosis mein 4 se 12 saal lagte hain [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]], toh jo bhi cheez dard ko sehne ka imtihaan nahi balki ek medical sawaal banaye, woh madad karti hai.

## Iske khilaaf kya argument hai?

Sabse bada objection hiring ka darr hai. Agar koi rule auraton ko mardon se mehnga employee dikhaye, toh kuch employers chupchaap kam auraton ko hire kar sakte hain. 2023-24 mein 15 saal aur usse badi Indian women mein se 41.7% labour force mein thi, jabki mardon mein 78.8% [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Towns aur cities mein, jahan kaam karne wali auraton ke paas gaon ke mukable kahin zyada regular salaried jobs hain, sirf 28.0% auratein labour force mein thi [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Jo policy employers ko auraton ko hire na karne ka ek aur bahaana de, woh unhi logon ko nuksaan pahunchayegi jinki madad ke liye bani hai.

Doosra objection reach ka hai. Period leave unhi ke kaam aati hai jinke paas employer, payslip aur leave register hai. 2023-24 mein rural women workers mein se 73.5% self-employed thi aur sirf 7.8% ke paas regular salaried job thi [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Vidarbha wali cousin ke liye period-leave ka koi bhi rule kuch nahi badalta.

Teesra objection stereotype ka hai. Kuch auraton ko darr hai ki ek special leave us purani soch ko hawa degi ki auratein reliable nahi hoti, ya har absence ko "mahine ke woh din" bol kar taal diya jayega. Yeh dard ko seriously lene ke khilaaf argument nahi hai. Yeh is baare mein argument hai ki ise kaise kiya jaye.

## Leave policy ho ya na ho, ek fair workplace kya kar sakta hai?

Jo cheezein sach mein madad karti hain, unme se zyadatar is baat pe depend nahi karti ki policy ka naam kya hai:

- **Period ke dard ko bimaari maano.** Sick leave mein period ka tez dard cover hona chahiye, bina kisi personal detail ki demand ke.
- **Flexibility do.** Jahan kaam allow kare, wahan sabse bure dinon mein hours shift karne ya ghar se kaam karne do.
- **Basics theek karo.** Paani wala saaf toilet, pads ke liye dustbin, aur thodi der let kar aaram karne ki jagah. Supreme Court ne har school ke liye working toilets, free pads aur safe disposal ka order diya hai [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Ek workplace adults ko isse kam nahi de sakta.
- **Diagnosis mein support karo.** Health cover aur gynaecology appointments ke liye time off, leave ke kitne bhi dinon se zyada matter karta hai.
- **Managers ko train karo.** "Monthly bahaane" wala joke hi woh jagah hai jahan bahut si auratein chup rehne ka faisla kar leti hain.

Toh Gurugram wali aurat ke liye workplace ki kya zimmedaari hai? Kam se kam woh sab, jo court ne ab har school jaane wali ladki se promise kiya hai: ek working toilet, koi sharm nahi, aur dard ko health ka maamla samajhna. Yeh ek alag leave se aaye ya aisi sick leave se jo sach mein use cover kare, yeh policy ka choice hai. Use yeh saabit karne pe majboor karna ki woh natak nahi kar rahi, koi choice nahi hai.

period-protection-rich-poor-divide.en:
Imagine two 17-year-olds in the same district. One finds a packet of sanitary pads in the monthly shopping and changes in a bathroom with a lock. The other washes a piece of old cloth, dries it under other clothes so that nobody sees it, and hopes it holds through the school day. India's national health survey shows that the line between these two lives runs largely through family wealth. In 2019-21, 95.1% of women aged 15-24 in the richest households used a hygienic method of period protection. In the poorest households, 53.6% did [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## The headline progress: 57.6% to 77.6%

On paper, this is a success story. In 2015-16, only 57.6% of Indian women aged 15-24 used a hygienic method during their periods; 62.1% used cloth and 41.8% used sanitary napkins [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. By 2019-21 the figure had risen to 77.6%. Pad use climbed to 64.4%, and cloth fell to 49.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Read the number carefully. The survey counts sanitary napkins, locally made napkins, tampons and menstrual cups as hygienic. Cloth is not counted, even though cloth that is washed and dried properly can be safe. Many women use more than one method, so the shares add up to more than 100. And the number counts products, not conditions: it does not ask whether a girl has water, soap, privacy or a bin.

The average also hides who was left behind. The poorest young women in 2019-21 had still not reached the level that India as a whole had in 2015-16.

## The wealth line: 95.1% against 53.6%

The survey ranks households by what they own and splits them into five equal groups. In the richest group, hygienic protection is almost universal at 95.1%. In the poorest, it is 53.6%: nearly half of these young women used no method the survey counts as hygienic [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

This is not a gap in cleanliness. A girl in a poor home is not dirtier or more careless than a girl in a rich one. She has less money. On a tight budget, a monthly packet of pads has to compete with everything else the household needs.

Periods already cost many girls school days. A 2016 review of studies from across India found that about a quarter of adolescent girls (24%) missed school during their periods [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. A few days lost every month add up over a school year.

## School, village and tribe

Schooling draws the same line, even more sharply. Among young women with 12 or more years of schooling, 90.3% used a hygienic method. Among those who never went to school, only 43.5% did, fewer than half [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Where a girl lives matters too. The figure was 89.6% in towns and cities against 72.6% in villages, and 65.6% among young women from Scheduled Tribes (Adivasi communities) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Villages have moved faster than cities: in 2015-16, fewer than half of rural young women (48%) used a hygienic method [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. The progress is real. But the groups that started furthest behind are still furthest behind.

These categories overlap. A poor Adivasi girl in a village who left school early carries every one of these disadvantages at once. The survey cannot pull them apart, and neither can she.

## Period protection and body knowledge follow the same gradient

The same privilege line runs through what young people know about their own bodies. In 2019-21, only 11.6% of young women in the poorest households had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, against 29.2% in the richest. Among those with no schooling it was 8.7%; among those with 12 or more years of schooling, 28.0% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Even at the top, that is fewer than one in three, so nobody is being taught well. The poorest are simply taught least. The same 2016 review found that only about half of Indian girls (48%) had been told about menstruation before their first period, pooling the 88 studies that reported on this [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]].

The gap reaches into girls' lives in other ways. Among girls aged 15-19, 10.0% in the poorest households had already given birth or were pregnant with their first child, against 2.2% in the richest [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Wealth, schooling and caste are tangled, so these numbers do not prove cause and effect. What they show is that the same girls are left out again and again.

## What would close the gap

The data points to fixes that have little to do with lecturing girls about hygiene.

**Free products where girls already are.** On 30 January 2026, the Supreme Court held that menstrual health is part of the right to life under Article 21 and ordered free sanitary napkins, working girls' toilets with water, and safe disposal in schools [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. What that ruling requires of every school deserves a checklist of its own.

**Reach the girls the school gate misses.** In December 2024, the Union government told the court that a national menstrual hygiene policy for school-going girls had been framed, with distribution mainly through schools and anganwadis [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-reserved-2024]]. A policy built for school-going girls starts at the school gate. Of all the groups in this story, the lowest period-protection figure belongs to young women who never got there.

**Water, privacy and disposal, not just pads.** A free pad does little for a girl with no toilet, no water and nowhere to throw it away. Cloth is not the enemy. As our story on cloth and hygiene shows, the lack of water, soap and a private place to dry it is.

**Information before the first period,** for girls and for the boys who grow up around them.

The richest households already show what near-universal protection looks like. Whether every girl gets there depends on public money and public pressure, not on girls trying harder.
period-protection-rich-poor-divide.hg:
Imagine karo: ek hi district mein 17 saal ki do ladkiyan. Pehli ke ghar har mahine ration ke saath sanitary pads ka packet aata hai, aur woh aise bathroom mein pad change karti hai jismein kundi lagti hai. Doosri ek purana kapda dhoti hai, use baaki kapdon ke neeche chhupa kar sukhati hai taaki kisi ki nazar na pade, aur manati hai ki school ka poora din kisi tarah nikal jaaye. India ka national health survey dikhata hai ki in dono zindagiyon ke beech ki line zyadatar ghar ke paise se hokar guzarti hai. 2019-21 mein sabse ameer gharon ki 15-24 saal ki 95.1% ladkiyan aur aurtein periods mein koi hygienic method use karti thi. Sabse gareeb gharon mein yeh sirf 53.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Upar se dikhti progress: 57.6% se 77.6%

Kaagaz par yeh success story hai. 2015-16 mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 57.6% ladkiyan aur aurtein periods mein hygienic method use karti thi; 62.1% kapda use karti thi aur 41.8% sanitary napkins [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. 2019-21 tak yeh figure 77.6% ho gaya. Pads ka use badhkar 64.4% hua, aur kapda ghat kar 49.6% par aa gaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Par is number ko dhyan se padho. Survey sanitary napkins, local bane napkins, tampons aur menstrual cups ko hygienic maanta hai. Kapde ko nahi ginta, jabki theek se dhoya aur sukhaya gaya kapda bhi safe ho sakta hai. Bahut si aurtein ek se zyada method use karti hain, isliye sab jodo toh 100 se zyada aata hai. Aur yeh number sirf products ginta hai, haalaat nahi: yeh nahi poochta ki ladki ke paas paani, sabun, privacy ya dustbin hai ya nahi.

Average yeh bhi chhupa leta hai ki kaun peeche chhoot gaya. 2019-21 mein sabse gareeb gharon ki ladkiyan us level tak bhi nahi pahunchi thi, jahan poora India 2015-16 mein khada tha.

## Ameeri-gareebi ki line: 95.1% vs 53.6%

Survey gharon ko unke saamaan aur suvidhaon ke hisaab se paanch barabar groups mein baant deta hai. Sabse ameer group mein hygienic protection lagbhag har ladki tak pahunch chuka tha: 95.1%. Sabse gareeb group mein yeh 53.6% tha, yaani in gharon ki kareeb aadhi ladkiyan aisa koi method use nahi karti thi jise survey hygienic maanta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh safai ki kami ka mamla nahi hai. Gareeb ghar ki ladki ameer ghar ki ladki se zyada gandi ya laaparwah nahi hoti. Uske ghar mein paisa kam hai. Tight budget mein mahine bhar ke pads ke packet ko ghar ki baaki saari zarooraton se mukabla karna padta hai.

Periods pehle se hi bahut si ladkiyon ke school ke din kha jaate hain. India ki kai studies ko jod kar 2016 mein ki gayi ek review ke mutabik, kareeb ek-chauthai teenage ladkiyan (24%) periods ke dinon mein school miss karti thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Har mahine kuch din chhootein, toh saal bhar mein padhai ka bada nuksaan ho jaata hai.

## School, gaon aur tribe

Padhai yahi line aur gehri kar deti hai. Jinhone 12 saal ya usse zyada padhai ki, unmein 90.3% hygienic method use karti thi. Jo kabhi school nahi gayi, unmein sirf 43.5%, yaani aadhi se bhi kam [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Ladki kahan rehti hai, isse bhi farak padta hai. Shehron mein yeh figure 89.6% tha aur gaon mein 72.6%. Scheduled Tribe (Adivasi) communities ki ladkiyon mein yeh 65.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Gaon shehron se tezi se aage badhe hain: 2015-16 mein gaon ki aadhi se bhi kam ladkiyan (48%) hygienic method use karti thi [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. Progress sachchi hai. Lekin jo sabse peeche se chale the, woh aaj bhi sabse peeche hain.

Yeh saari cheezein aapas mein judi hain. Gaon ki koi gareeb Adivasi ladki, jiski padhai jaldi chhoot gayi, yeh saari mushkilein ek saath jhelti hai. Survey inhe alag nahi kar sakta, aur woh ladki bhi nahi kar sakti.

## Pads bhi, jaankari bhi: dono ek hi line par bante

Yahi privilege ki line is baat mein bhi dikhti hai ki young logon ko apni hi body ke baare mein kitna pata hai. 2019-21 mein sabse gareeb gharon ki sirf 11.6% young women ko HIV ki poori aur sahi jaankari thi, jabki sabse ameer gharon mein 29.2% ko. Jo kabhi school nahi gayi, unmein yeh 8.7% tha; 12 saal ya usse zyada padhi ladkiyon mein 28.0% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sabse upar bhi yeh teen mein se ek se kam hai, yaani theek se kisi ko nahi sikhaya ja raha. Bas sabse gareeb ko sabse kam sikhaya ja raha hai. Usi 2016 review ke mutabik India mein kareeb aadhi ladkiyon (48%) ko hi pehle period se pehle iske baare mein bataya gaya tha; yeh figure un 88 studies ko jod kar nikla jinhone yeh sawaal poochha tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]].

Yeh gap ladkiyon ki zindagi mein aur jagah bhi dikhta hai. 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon mein, sabse gareeb gharon ki 10.0% ya toh maa ban chuki thi ya pehli baar pregnant thi, jabki sabse ameer gharon mein 2.2% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Paisa, padhai aur caste aapas mein uljhe hue hain, isliye yeh numbers cause and effect prove nahi karte. Yeh bas itna dikhate hain ki baar-baar wahi ladkiyan peeche chhoot jaati hain.

## Yeh gap kaise bharega

Data jo raasta dikhata hai, uska ladkiyon ko hygiene par lecture dene se koi lena-dena nahi hai.

**Jahan ladkiyan hain, wahin free products.** 30 January 2026 ko Supreme Court ne kaha ki menstrual health Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa hai, aur schools mein free sanitary napkins, paani wale working girls' toilets aur safe disposal ka order diya [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Yeh faisla har school se kya-kya maangta hai, uski poori checklist alag se samajhne layak hai.

**School gate ke bahar wali ladkiyon tak pahuncho.** December 2024 mein Union government ne court ko bataya ki school jaane wali ladkiyon ke liye ek national menstrual hygiene policy ban gayi hai, jismein pads zyadatar schools aur anganwadis ke zariye baante jaane hain [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-reserved-2024]]. Par school jaane wali ladkiyon ki policy school gate se hi shuru hoti hai. Aur is story ke saare groups mein hygienic protection ka sabse kam figure unhi ladkiyon ka hai jo us gate tak kabhi pahunchi hi nahi.

**Sirf pads nahi, paani, privacy aur disposal bhi.** Jis ladki ke paas na toilet hai, na paani, na pad phenkne ki jagah, uske liye free pad bhi aadha solution hai. Dushman kapda nahi hai. Kapde aur hygiene par hamari alag story dikhati hai ki asli dushman hai paani, sabun aur kapda khul kar sukhane ki apni jagah ki kami.

**Pehle period se pehle jaankari,** ladkiyon ko bhi, aur unke aas-paas bade ho rahe ladkon ko bhi.

Sabse ameer ghar dikha chuke hain ki lagbhag har ladki tak pahunchna possible hai. Baaki ladkiyan wahan tak pahunchengi ya nahi, yeh public paise aur public pressure par tika hai, ladkiyon ke "aur koshish karne" par nahi.

period-protection-state-map.en:
In Puducherry, 99.1% of women aged 15-24 used a method of period protection that India's national survey counts as hygienic in 2019-21. In Bihar, 59.2% did, which means about four in ten young women there used none of them [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Same country, same survey, same age group. The difference is the state a girl happens to be born in, and what that state has, or has not, put within her reach.

## The national figure, and what it hides

Nationally, the picture improved fast. In 2015-16, 57.6% of women aged 15-24 used a hygienic method [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. By 2019-21, 77.6% did [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is the number that tends to appear in speeches.

A national average, though, blends very different places. Bihar's young women in 2019-21 were only a little ahead of where India as a whole had been in 2015-16, a full survey round behind the country. Madhya Pradesh, at 60.9%, was in the same position.

There is also a gap between rich and poor homes, which is a separate story in this section. This one is about geography: the line on the map that a girl cannot choose.

## The five states at the bottom

Five states sat at the bottom in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| State | Women aged 15-24 using a hygienic method, 2019-21 |
|---|---|
| Bihar | 59.2% |
| Madhya Pradesh | 60.9% |
| Meghalaya | 65.3% |
| Gujarat | 66.9% |
| Assam | 67.0% |

These five are not one kind of place. Two are large Hindi-speaking states, two are in the Northeast, and one, Gujarat, is in the west. No single explanation fits all five. That is why each state's own delivery deserves scrutiny: what actually reaches its schools, its anganwadis and its village shops.

The bottom of this map overlaps with other maps of what young women are denied. In the same survey, only 10% of young women in Bihar had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, against 69% in Mizoram [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Assam (11.7%) and Bihar (11.0%) were among the five states with the highest share of women aged 15-19 who had already given birth or were pregnant [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Overlapping maps do not prove that one problem causes another. They show where girls run into several walls at once.

## The states close to 100%

Compare Puducherry (99.1%) and Tamil Nadu (98.4%), where almost every young woman used a hygienic method [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Read the two differently. Puducherry is a small union territory, and survey estimates for small states and union territories come with wider margins of error; the same caution applies to Meghalaya at the bottom. Tamil Nadu is the stronger proof. It is one of India's biggest states, and it shows that near-universal coverage is not a small-place trick.

A high number is not a certificate, either. It measures what young women used, not whether every school has a working girls' toilet. When the Supreme Court checked compliance with its menstrual-health orders in September 2026, it flagged data discrepancies in the reports of several states, Tamil Nadu among them [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. How the states have stalled on those orders is the subject of a separate investigation.

## Cloth, pads and the survey's definition of 'hygienic'

Before you compare states, know what is being counted. The survey counts sanitary napkins, locally made napkins, tampons and menstrual cups as hygienic. Cloth is not counted, even though cloth that is washed and dried properly can be safe. Nationally, 49.6% of young women used cloth and 64.4% used sanitary napkins; the two add up to more than 100 because many women use both [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

So a state's figure measures access to products, not safety or dignity. A state where many young women use clean cloth, with water and a private place to dry it, may look worse on this map than life there really is. A state where girls have pads but nowhere to change them may look better. Why cloth itself is not the problem is the subject of our myth-versus-truth story on cloth.

One small change between rounds: the 2015-16 survey did not count menstrual cups as hygienic, and the 2019-21 survey did [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. It is a minor difference, so the comparison between the two rounds still holds.

## Holding your state to its number

Since 30 January 2026, this is no longer only a health statistic. The Supreme Court has held that menstrual health is part of the right to life under Article 21, and ordered free sanitary napkins, working girls' toilets with water and safe disposal in schools [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Delivering that is the job of state governments. In an order reported on 15 October 2026, the court gave states "one last opportunity" to report compliance and warned that it would issue contempt notices to the Chief Secretaries of states that failed to respond. The case is listed next on 14 December 2026 [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].

That makes your state's number a benchmark you can use. If you live in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Gujarat or Assam, ask your MLA and your state education department what has changed since 2019-21, and what they have told the court. If you live in a high-scoring state, ask who the remaining few per cent are, and whether anyone is reaching them.

Newer data is on its way. Provisional fact sheets from the next survey round, NFHS-6 (2023-24), were released in May 2026 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. This map uses the full 2019-21 report. When newer state figures on periods are confirmed, the question for every state will be the same: did the bottom move?
period-protection-state-map.hg:
2019-21 mein Puducherry ki 15-24 saal ki 99.1% ladkiyan aur aurtein periods mein aisa method use karti thi jise India ka national survey hygienic maanta hai. Bihar mein yeh figure 59.2% tha, yaani wahan kareeb har das mein se chaar young women inmein se koi method use nahi karti thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Wahi desh, wahi survey, wahi umar. Farak bas itna hai ki ladki kis state mein paida hui, aur us state ne uski pahunch mein kya rakha aur kya nahi.

## National figure, aur uske peeche kya chhupa hai

Poore desh mein picture tezi se badli. 2015-16 mein 15-24 saal ki 57.6% ladkiyan aur aurtein hygienic method use karti thi [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. 2019-21 tak yeh 77.6% ho gaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Speeches mein aksar yahi number sunai deta hai.

Lekin national average bahut alag-alag jagahon ko ek saath mila deta hai. 2019-21 mein Bihar ki ladkiyan 2015-16 ke poore India se bas zara si aage thi, yaani desh se poore ek survey round peeche. 60.9% ke saath Madhya Pradesh ka haal bhi yahi tha.

Ameer aur gareeb gharon ke beech bhi ek bada gap hai, jo isi section ki ek alag story hai. Yeh story geography ki hai: map ki woh line jise koi ladki khud nahi chunti.

## Sabse neeche ke paanch states

2019-21 mein yeh paanch states sabse neeche the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| State | Periods mein hygienic method use karne wali 15-24 saal ki women, 2019-21 |
|---|---|
| Bihar | 59.2% |
| Madhya Pradesh | 60.9% |
| Meghalaya | 65.3% |
| Gujarat | 66.9% |
| Assam | 67.0% |

Yeh paanchon ek jaise states nahi hain. Do bade Hindi-speaking states hain, do Northeast ke hain, aur ek, Gujarat, west mein hai. Paanchon par koi ek wajah fit nahi baithti. Isiliye har state ki apni delivery ko parakhna zaroori hai: uske schools, anganwadis aur gaon ki dukaanon tak asal mein kya pahunchta hai.

Is map ka neeche wala hissa doosre maps se bhi milta hai, jo dikhate hain ki young women ko kya-kya nahi mil raha. Isi survey mein Bihar ki sirf 10% young women ko HIV ki poori aur sahi jaankari thi, jabki Mizoram mein 69% ko [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 15-19 saal ki umar mein maa ban chuki ya pregnant ladkiyon ke maamle mein Assam (11.7%) aur Bihar (11.0%) top five states mein the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Maps ke aapas mein milne se yeh prove nahi hota ki ek problem doosri ki wajah hai. Isse bas itna dikhta hai ki kahan ladkiyan ek saath kai deewaron se takrati hain.

## Lagbhag 100% wale states

Ab Puducherry (99.1%) aur Tamil Nadu (98.4%) ko dekho, jahan lagbhag har young woman hygienic method use karti thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Par in dono ko alag nazar se padho. Puducherry ek chhota union territory hai, aur chhote states aur union territories ke survey estimates mein galti ki gunjaish zyada hoti hai; yahi savdhaani neeche wale Meghalaya par bhi lagti hai. Tamil Nadu zyada pakka saboot hai. Yeh India ke sabse bade states mein se ek hai, aur dikhata hai ki lagbhag har ladki tak pahunchna sirf chhoti jagahon ka kamaal nahi hai.

High number koi certificate bhi nahi hai. Yeh batata hai ki young women ne kya use kiya, yeh nahi ki har school mein girls' toilet chalu hai ya nahi. September 2026 mein jab Supreme Court ne apne menstrual health orders par compliance check kiya, toh usne kai states ki reports ke data mein gadbad pakdi, aur Tamil Nadu bhi unmein tha [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. States ne un orders ko kaise latkaya, yeh hamari ek alag investigation ka topic hai.

## Kapda, pads aur survey ki 'hygienic' wali definition

States compare karne se pehle jaan lo ki gina kya ja raha hai. Survey sanitary napkins, local bane napkins, tampons aur menstrual cups ko hygienic maanta hai. Kapde ko nahi ginta, jabki theek se dhoya aur sukhaya gaya kapda bhi safe ho sakta hai. Desh mein 49.6% young women kapda use karti thi aur 64.4% sanitary napkins; dono jodo toh 100 se zyada aata hai, kyunki bahut si aurtein dono use karti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yaani kisi state ka figure products tak pahunch naapta hai, safety ya dignity nahi. Jis state mein bahut si ladkiyan saaf kapda use karti hain, aur unke paas paani aur use sukhane ki apni jagah hai, woh is map par asal se bura dikh sakta hai. Jis state mein ladkiyon ke paas pads toh hain par change karne ki jagah nahi, woh asal se achha dikh sakta hai. Kapda apne aap mein problem kyun nahi hai, yeh kapde par hamari myth-vs-truth story mein hai.

Dono rounds ke beech ek chhota badlaav bhi hua: 2015-16 ke survey ne menstrual cups ko hygienic nahi gina tha, aur 2019-21 ke survey ne gina [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. Yeh minor farak hai, isliye dono rounds ka comparison phir bhi theek baithta hai.

## Apne state ko uske number par jawabdeh banao

30 January 2026 ke baad se yeh sirf health ka number nahi raha. Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki menstrual health Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa hai, aur schools mein free sanitary napkins, paani wale working girls' toilets aur safe disposal ka order diya hai [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Ise zameen par utaarna state governments ka kaam hai. 15 October 2026 ko chhapi report ke mutabik, court ne states ko compliance report karne ka "one last opportunity" diya, aur warning di ki jo states jawab nahi denge unke Chief Secretaries ko contempt notice jaayega. Case ki agli sunwai 14 December 2026 ko hai [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].

Isliye tumhare state ka number ek benchmark hai jise tum use kar sakte ho. Agar tum Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Gujarat ya Assam mein rehte ho, toh apne MLA aur state education department se poochho: 2019-21 ke baad kya badla, aur unhone court ko kya bataya? Agar tumhara state upar hai, toh poochho ki jo kuch percent ladkiyan bachi hain woh kaun hain, aur kya koi un tak pahunch raha hai.

Naya data bhi aa raha hai. Agle survey round, NFHS-6 (2023-24), ki provisional fact sheets May 2026 mein release hui [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yeh map 2019-21 ki poori report par bana hai. Jab states ke periods wale naye figures confirm ho jaayenge, toh har state se sawaal ek hi hoga: kya bottom upar aaya?

period-warning-signs-see-doctor.en:
Imagine a 16-year-old in Patna who changes her pad every hour on the heaviest days and feels dizzy on the stairs at school. Her grandmother calls it garmi. A neighbour recommends a tonic advertised on a wall near the bus stand. Nobody suggests a doctor, because nobody told the family which period problems are medical. Delay is common: WHO estimates that up to 70% of women with PCOS do not know they have it [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]], and that endometriosis takes on average 4 to 12 years to diagnose [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]].

## Normal varies, but within limits

Periods vary, and they are often irregular in the first few years. For most adults, a period comes every 21 to 35 days and lasts between 2 and 7 days [[nhs-periods]]. Cramps on the first day or two are common, and so is an occasional early or late period.

What matters is the pattern over several months, and change. A period that has become much heavier, more painful or unpredictable needs a check, even if your mother "also had it".

## Red flags: see a doctor this week

Book an appointment, without waiting for marriage or exams, if any of these apply:

- **Heavy bleeding:** soaking through a pad or tampon every one to two hours, passing large clots again and again, or bleeding for more than 7 days.
- **Signs of anaemia:** tiredness, breathlessness, dizziness or pale skin with heavy periods. Months of heavy bleeding drain the body's iron.
- **Periods that stop:** three missed periods in a row when a pregnancy test is negative, or no first period at all by 15 [[nhs-periods]].
- **Cycles out of range:** periods that regularly come sooner than every 21 days or later than every 35, or follow no pattern, especially alongside acne or extra facial and body hair, which can signal PCOS [[who-pcos]].
- **Pain that runs your life:** pain that keeps you home from school, college or work, that painkillers do not control, that gets worse year after year, or that comes with pain during sex or while passing stool or urine. WHO lists severe period pain, long-lasting pelvic pain and pain during sex, bowel movements or urination among the symptoms of endometriosis [[who-endometriosis]].
- **Bleeding out of turn:** bleeding between periods or after sex needs to be checked by a doctor [[nhs-periods]].

## Emergencies that cannot wait

Go to a hospital emergency department or call 112 for any of these:

- **Heavy bleeding with fainting, a racing heart or breathlessness.**
- **A sudden high fever, a rash that feels like sandpaper, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or confusion while using a tampon or menstrual cup.** These can be signs of toxic shock syndrome, a rare but serious condition. Remove the tampon or cup and tell the doctor you were using one [[nhs-tss]].
- **A missed period followed by sudden, sharp pain low on one side of the belly, bleeding, pain in the tip of the shoulder, dizziness or fainting.** This can be an ectopic pregnancy, one growing outside the womb, which needs urgent treatment [[nhs-ectopic]].

## Preparing for the appointment

A doctor can do far more with notes than with "my periods are bad". For three months, write down:

- the first day of each period and how many days it lasted;
- how many pads you used on the heaviest day, and whether you bled through to clothes or bedding;
- a pain score out of ten, and any school, college or work days missed;
- other changes such as acne, new hair growth, weight change or constant tiredness;
- every medicine, tonic or home remedy you have tried.

Which doctor? A gynaecologist is best, but a general doctor at a government health centre can start the tests and refer you. Teenagers can also use Adolescent Friendly Health Centres, which offer counselling and clinical care at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. You can ask for a woman doctor and bring someone you trust. You do not need to be married to see a gynaecologist, and you can ask what each test is for before you agree to it.

If you are under 18, know one rule: under POCSO, any sexual activity involving someone under 18 is an offence, and anyone who knows of such an offence, including a doctor, must report it. So a doctor cannot promise total secrecy [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. That is no reason to skip care. A trusted adult or the Child Helpline, 1098, can help.

## Quack ads and how to report them

Wall ads, newspaper classifieds and reels sell the same promise: a tonic, powder or "hormone balance" kit that will regulate periods or cure "PCOD". Section 3 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans exactly that: advertising any drug for "the correction of menstrual disorder in women", and also for "the procurement of miscarriage in women" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. The second clause matters: a pill sold to "bring on" a late period may really be meant to end a pregnancy. If your period is late and you could be pregnant, take a pregnancy test and see a registered doctor instead of buying anything.

A first conviction under the Act can bring up to six months in jail, a fine or both, and a repeat conviction up to a year [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

The law has been weakly enforced. In March 2025 the Supreme Court said that although the Act was more than 70 years old, "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit". It ordered every state to appoint enforcement officers within one month and to set up a way for the public to complain, such as a toll-free number or email, within two months [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. To use it:

1. **Save the evidence.** Photograph or screenshot the ad, with the date, place and any phone number or website.
2. **Find your state's complaint channel.** Check your state health or drugs control department's website.
3. **Go to the police if needed.** The offence is cognizable, so you can give a written complaint at a police station [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].
4. **Report it on the platform too,** as a misleading ad.

This is general information, not legal advice.

The girl in Patna does not need a stronger tonic. She needs a blood test, a doctor, and a family that knows dizziness on the stairs is a symptom, not a weakness.
period-warning-signs-see-doctor.hg:
Socho, Patna ki ek 16 saal ki ladki jo sabse heavy dinon mein har ghante pad badalti hai aur school ki seedhiyon pe use chakkar aate hain. Daadi kehti hain garmi hai. Ek padosan bus stand ke paas deewar pe likhe ad wala tonic suggest karti hai. Koi doctor ka naam nahi leta, kyunki family ko kisi ne bataya hi nahi ki period ki kaunsi problems medical hoti hain. Aisa delay bahut common hai: WHO ka estimate hai ki PCOS wali 70% tak women ko pata hi nahi ki unhe yeh hai [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]], aur endometriosis ka diagnosis hone mein average 4 se 12 saal lagte hain [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]].

## Normal alag-alag hota hai, par ek limit tak

Periods sabke alag hote hain, aur shuru ke kuch saal aksar irregular rehte hain. Zyadatar adults mein period har 21 se 35 din mein aata hai aur 2 se 7 din chalta hai [[nhs-periods]]. Pehle ek-do din cramps hona common hai, aur kabhi-kabhaar period ka jaldi ya late aana bhi.

Matter karta hai kai mahinon ka pattern, aur badlaav. Jo period pehle se kaafi zyada heavy, zyada dard wala ya unpredictable ho gaya hai, uska check-up zaroori hai, chahe tumhari mummy kahein ki "mujhe bhi aisa hi hota tha".

## Red flags: isi hafte doctor ko dikhao

Shaadi ya exams ka wait kiye bina appointment lo, agar inme se kuch bhi ho raha hai:

- **Heavy bleeding:** har ek-do ghante mein pad ya tampon poora bhar jaana, baar-baar bade clots aana, ya 7 din se zyada bleeding.
- **Anaemia ke signs:** heavy periods ke saath thakaan, saans phoolna, chakkar ya peeli skin. Mahinon ki heavy bleeding body ka iron khatam kar deti hai.
- **Periods ruk jaana:** lagaatar teen periods miss hona jab pregnancy test negative ho, ya 15 saal tak pehla period aaya hi na ho [[nhs-periods]].
- **Range se bahar cycles:** periods jo regularly 21 din se pehle ya 35 din ke baad aayein, ya jinka koi pattern hi na ho, khaas kar agar saath mein acne ya chehre aur body pe extra baal hon. Yeh PCOS ke signs ho sakte hain [[who-pcos]].
- **Aisa dard jo zindagi chalane lage:** dard jo tumhe school, college ya kaam se ghar pe rok de, jo painkillers se na ruke, jo saal-dar-saal badhta jaye, ya jiske saath sex ke dauraan ya potty-peshaab karte waqt dard ho. WHO periods mein tez dard, lambe samay tak rehne wala pelvic dard, aur sex, potty ya peshaab ke waqt dard ko endometriosis ke symptoms mein ginta hai [[who-endometriosis]].
- **Bewaqt bleeding:** periods ke beech mein ya sex ke baad bleeding ko doctor se check karwana zaroori hai [[nhs-periods]].

## Emergencies jo wait nahi kar sakti

Inme se kuch bhi ho toh hospital ke emergency department jao ya 112 call karo:

- **Heavy bleeding ke saath behoshi, dil ki dhadkan bahut tez hona ya saans phoolna.**
- **Tampon ya menstrual cup use karte waqt achanak tez bukhaar, sandpaper jaisa khurdura rash, ulti, dast, chakkar ya confusion.** Yeh toxic shock syndrome ke signs ho sakte hain, jo rare par serious condition hai. Tampon ya cup nikaalo aur doctor ko batao ki tum use kar rahi thi [[nhs-tss]].
- **Period miss hone ke baad pet ke neeche ek side achanak tez dard, bleeding, kandhe ke sire pe dard, chakkar ya behoshi.** Yeh ectopic pregnancy ho sakti hai, yaani womb ke bahar badhti pregnancy, jiska turant ilaaj zaroori hai [[nhs-ectopic]].

## Appointment ki tayyari

"Mere periods kharab hain" sunne se zyada doctor notes ke saath bahut kuch kar sakta hai. Teen mahine tak yeh likho:

- har period ka pehla din aur woh kitne din chala;
- sabse heavy din pe kitne pads lage, aur kya bleeding kapdon ya bedsheet tak pahunchi;
- das mein se dard ka score, aur school, college ya kaam ke kitne din miss hue;
- baaki badlaav jaise acne, naye baal, weight mein badlaav ya hamesha rehne wali thakaan;
- har dawa, tonic ya gharelu nuskha jo tumne try kiya.

Kaunsa doctor? Gynaecologist sabse achha hai, par government health centre ka general doctor bhi tests shuru karke aage refer kar sakta hai. Teenagers Adolescent Friendly Health Centres bhi ja sakte hain, jo primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling aur clinical care dete hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Tum lady doctor maang sakti ho aur kisi bharose wale ko saath la sakti ho. Gynaecologist ke paas jaane ke liye shaadi-shuda hona zaroori nahi hai, aur kisi bhi test ke liye haan kehne se pehle tum pooch sakti ho ki woh kis liye hai.

Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh ek rule jaan lo: POCSO ke under 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan se judi sexual activity offence hai, aur jise bhi aise offence ka pata ho, doctor bhi, use report karna padta hai. Isliye doctor poori secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakta [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh ilaaj skip karne ki wajah nahi hai. Koi bharose wala bada ya Child Helpline 1098 madad kar sakti hai.

## Jhola-chhaap ads aur unhe report kaise karein

Deewar ke ads, akhbaar ke classifieds aur reels ek hi promise bechte hain: ek tonic, powder ya "hormone balance" kit jo periods regular kar dega ya "PCOD" cure kar dega. Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 ka Section 3 bilkul isi pe rok lagata hai: kisi bhi aisi dawa ka ad jo "the correction of menstrual disorder in women", yaani period ki gadbad theek karne ke liye ho, ya "the procurement of miscarriage in women", yaani miscarriage karwane ke liye ho [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Doosra clause important hai: late period "laane" ke naam pe bechi gayi goli asal mein pregnancy khatam karne ke liye ho sakti hai. Agar period late hai aur pregnancy ho sakti hai, toh kuch bhi khareedne ki jagah pregnancy test karo aur registered doctor ko dikhao.

Is Act ke under pehli baar conviction pe chhe mahine tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain, aur dobara conviction pe ek saal tak [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Is law ko kamzori se lagu kiya gaya hai. March 2025 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki Act 70 saal se zyada purana hai, phir bhi "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit", yaani iska sahi maayne mein implementation hua hi nahi. Court ne har state ko ek mahine ke andar enforcement officers appoint karne aur do mahine ke andar public ke liye complaint ka tareeka banane ko kaha, jaise toll-free number ya email [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Ise use karne ke liye:

1. **Saboot sambhaal ke rakho.** Ad ki photo ya screenshot lo, date, jagah aur koi bhi phone number ya website ke saath.
2. **Apne state ka complaint channel dhoondo.** Apne state ke health ya drugs control department ki website check karo.
3. **Zaroorat ho toh police ke paas jao.** Yeh offence cognizable hai, isliye tum police station mein likhit complaint de sakti ho [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].
4. **Platform pe bhi report karo,** misleading ad ke roop mein.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Patna wali ladki ko zyada strong tonic ki zaroorat nahi hai. Use ek blood test, ek doctor, aur ek aisi family chahiye jo samjhe ki seedhiyon pe chakkar aana ek symptom hai, kamzori nahi.

preparing-child-for-first-period.en:
Imagine a Class 6 girl in Indore who finds blood on her underwear in the school toilet during the lunch break. Nobody has told her what it is. She decides she is injured or seriously ill, and she tells no one until the last bell. Her story is common. In a 2016 review that pooled Indian studies, only 48% of adolescent girls had been told about menstruation before it began [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. If nobody prepared you either, this guide is the conversation you were owed. Pass it on.

## Why the first talk usually comes too late

Most adults explain only after the first period, in a hurry, with the door shut, and often as a list of rules. The same review found that 77% of girls were kept from religious activities during periods and 24% missed school [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. The review pooled studies of uneven quality and is not a national survey, but the pattern is familiar: girls learn what they must not touch before they learn what a uterus is.

School may not fill the gap. India's National Education Policy 2020 does not use the words "puberty" or "menstruation" once in its 66 pages [[nep-2020-full-text]].

The usual fear is that talking early will make a child "grow up too fast". The evidence points the other way. UNESCO's 2018 guidance states that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity or risk-taking, and that curriculum-based programmes contribute to later first sex and more use of condoms and contraception [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Knowing how her body works does not push a child towards anything. It only removes the ambush.

## When to start, and what to say

Start earlier than feels natural. Puberty usually begins between 8 and 13 in girls, the timing varies widely, and the first period usually comes some time after the breasts start to develop [[nhs-periods]]. So the first conversation belongs at 8 or 9, or as soon as you notice breast buds, underarm hair or a clear or white discharge in her underwear.

Plan many small talks instead of one big one: while folding clothes, or when a pad advertisement comes on. Use the real words. A script that works:

> Inside your lower belly is the uterus. Every month it builds a soft lining. When there is no pregnancy, the lining comes out through the vagina as blood. That is a period. It is not an injury and it is not dirty.

Then add the promise that matters most: when it happens, tell me, and we will handle it together.

Bleeding usually lasts 2 to 7 days. The blood may be red or brown, and the amount is usually smaller than it looks on a pad. In the first years the gap between periods can be anywhere from 21 to 45 days, so an irregular start is expected [[nhs-periods]].

## A starter kit for school and home

A first period at school is manageable if the kit is already in the bag: a pouch with two pads, spare underwear and a paper bag for the used pad. Let her stick a pad onto underwear once at home, so that her first attempt is not in a school toilet. Teach three rules: change it several times a day, before it feels full, wrap the used pad and put it in a bin, and never flush it.

The kit depends on the home. In 2019-21, 64.4% of women aged 15-24 used sanitary napkins and 49.6% still used cloth [[nfhs5-india-2021]]; in 2015-16 only 41.8% used napkins [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. A mother who grew up with cloth may be teaching a product she never used at that age. Cloth washed with soap and dried fully in the sun can be safe, so teach it openly.

Agree on a plan for a stain: a sweater tied around the waist, and one named teacher to go to. Then ask the school where pads are kept. The Supreme Court's judgment of 30 January 2026 directed schools to provide free sanitary napkins and working girls' toilets with water, and it ordered menstrual-hygiene corners stocked with spare uniforms [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

Tell her when a doctor is needed: no period by 15, a pad soaked every 1 to 2 hours, bleeding beyond 7 days, or pain that stops her normal day [[nhs-periods]].

## Talking to sons too

Boys are often told nothing, then expected to behave well when a classmate has a stain on her skirt. The 2026 judgment told schools to sensitise boys and male teachers [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Home should not wait for school.

Tell your son the same biology in the same words. Then give him a role: fetch a pad without comment, lend a sweater, tell the others to stop laughing. He is owed his own no-surprises talk too: wet dreams, erections and a breaking voice are as ordinary as a period.

A father who can say "period" at the dinner table and buy pads without wrapping them in newspaper teaches both children more than a lecture does.

## Children's questions, honest answers

- **"Will it hurt?"** Cramps are common. A hot-water bottle, a warm bath and gentle movement help. Pain that stops school or play needs a doctor.
- **"Can I play, bathe, go into the kitchen?"** Yes. Restrictions during periods have no medical basis. If your family follows a custom, say that it is a custom, not a health rule, and that she is not impure.
- **"All my friends have it. Why don't I?"** Timing varies widely. Earlier or later than friends is normal.
- **"Am I a grown-up now?"** No. A first period means the reproductive system has started to mature. She is still a child, and no one, inside the family or outside it, may touch her private parts or ask her to keep a secret about her body.

You will not know every answer. "I don't know, let's find out together" is a complete answer. What matters is that she hears it from you first, before the day she needs it.
preparing-child-for-first-period.hg:
Indore ki Class 6 ki ek ladki ke baare mein sochiye. Lunch break mein school ke toilet mein use apne underwear par blood dikhta hai. Kisi ne use bataya hi nahi ki yeh kya hai. Woh maan leti hai ki use chot lagi hai ya koi badi bimaari ho gayi hai, aur aakhri ghanti tak kisi se kuch nahi kehti. Aisi kahani aam hai. 2016 ke ek review ne India ki kai studies ko jod kar dekha, aur usme sirf 48% adolescent girls ko period shuru hone se pehle uske baare mein bataya gaya tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Agar aapko bhi kisi ne taiyaar nahi kiya tha, toh yeh guide wahi baatcheet hai jo aapse honi chahiye thi. Ise aage badhaiye.

## Pehli baat aksar der se kyun hoti hai

Zyada tar bade pehla period aane ke baad hi samjhate hain: jaldi-jaldi, darwaza band karke, aur aksar rules ki ek list ki tarah. Usi review mein mila ki 77% ladkiyon ko periods ke dauraan religious activities se roka jaata tha aur 24% school miss karti thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Is review mein alag-alag quality ki studies jodi gayi thi aur yeh national survey nahi hai. Par pattern jaana-pehchaana hai: ladkiyan pehle yeh seekhti hain ki kya nahi chhoona, aur uterus kya hota hai yeh baad mein.

School yeh kami poori kar dega, yeh zaroori nahi. India ki National Education Policy 2020 ke 66 pages mein "puberty" ya "menstruation" word ek baar bhi nahi aata [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Aam dar yeh hota hai ki jaldi baat karne se bachcha "waqt se pehle bada ho jayega". Evidence ulta kehta hai. UNESCO ki 2018 ki guidance kehti hai ki sexuality education se na sexual activity badhti hai, na risk lena, aur curriculum-based programmes se pehli baar sex der se hota hai aur condom aur contraception ka use badhta hai [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Apni body ko samajhna bachche ko kisi cheez ki taraf nahi dhakelta. Bas itna hota hai ki uski apni body use achanak chaunka nahi paati.

## Kab shuru karein, aur kya kahein

Jitna natural lagta hai, usse pehle shuru kijiye. Ladkiyon mein puberty aam taur par 8 se 13 saal ke beech shuru hoti hai, timing sabki alag hoti hai, aur pehla period aksar breasts ka develop hona shuru hone ke kuch samay baad aata hai [[nhs-periods]]. Isliye pehli baatcheet 8 ya 9 saal ki umar mein honi chahiye, ya jaise hi aapko breast buds, underarm ke baal ya uske underwear mein clear ya white discharge dikhe.

Ek badi baat ki jagah kai chhoti-chhoti baatein plan kijiye: kapde tah karte waqt, ya jab TV par pad ka ad aaye. Asli words use kijiye. Ek script jo kaam karti hai:

> Tumhare pet ke nichle hisse mein uterus hota hai. Har mahine woh andar ek naram parat banata hai. Jab pregnancy nahi hoti, toh yeh parat vagina se blood ban kar bahar aa jaati hai. Isi ko period kehte hain. Yeh na koi chot hai, na koi gandi cheez.

Phir woh vaada jodiye jo sabse zaroori hai: jab aisa ho, mujhe batana, hum saath mein sambhaal lenge.

Bleeding aam taur par 2 se 7 din chalti hai. Blood laal ya brown ho sakta hai, aur jitna pad par dikhta hai, asal mein aksar usse kam hota hai. Shuru ke saalon mein do periods ke beech ka gap 21 se 45 din tak kuch bhi ho sakta hai, isliye shuruaat ka irregular hona expected hai [[nhs-periods]].

## School aur ghar ke liye starter kit

School mein pehla period sambhal jaata hai agar kit pehle se bag mein ho: ek pouch jisme do pads, ek extra underwear aur used pad ke liye ek paper bag ho. Ghar par ek baar use khud pad underwear par chipkane dijiye, taaki uski pehli koshish school ke toilet mein na ho. Teen rules sikhaiye: pad din mein kai baar badlo, poora bharne se pehle, used pad lapet kar dustbin mein daalo, aur use kabhi flush mat karo.

Kit mein kya hoga, yeh ghar par depend karta hai. 2019-21 mein 15-24 saal ki 64.4% women sanitary napkins use karti thi aur 49.6% ab bhi cloth [[nfhs5-india-2021]]; 2015-16 mein sirf 41.8% napkins use karti thi [[nfhs4-india-2016]]. Jo maa khud kapde ke saath badi hui, woh shayad beti ko aisa product sikha rahi hai jo usne us umar mein kabhi use nahi kiya. Sabun se dhula aur dhoop mein poori tarah sukhaya kapda safe ho sakta hai, isliye use bhi khulkar sikhaiye.

Stain ke liye plan pehle se tay kijiye: kamar par sweater baandhna, aur ek teacher ka naam jiske paas woh ja sake. Phir school se poochiye ki pads kahan rakhe hain. Supreme Court ke 30 January 2026 ke judgment ne schools ko free sanitary napkins aur paani wale chalu girls' toilets dene ka direction diya, aur aise menstrual-hygiene corners ka order diya jahan spare uniforms rakhi hon [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

Use yeh bhi bataiye ki doctor ki zaroorat kab hai: 15 saal ki umar tak period na aaye, har 1 se 2 ghante mein pad poora bheeg jaaye, bleeding 7 din se zyada chale, ya dard itna ho ki uska normal din ruk jaaye [[nhs-periods]].

## Beton se bhi baat kijiye

Ladkon ko aksar kuch nahi bataya jaata, aur phir unse umeed ki jaati hai ki jab kisi classmate ki skirt par stain ho toh woh theek se behave karein. 2026 ke judgment ne schools ko kaha ki ladkon aur male teachers ko sensitise kiya jaaye [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Ghar ko school ka intezaar nahi karna chahiye.

Bete ko wahi biology unhi words mein bataiye. Phir use ek role dijiye: bina comment kiye pad la kar dena, sweater dena, doosron ko hansne se rokna. Uska apna bhi ek no-surprises talk banta hai: wet dreams, erections aur badalti awaaz utni hi normal hain jitna period.

Jo father dinner table par "period" bol sakta hai aur pads ko akhbaar mein lapete bina khareed sakta hai, woh dono bachchon ko kisi lecture se zyada sikha deta hai.

## Bachchon ke sawaal, seedhe jawab

- **"Kya dard hoga?"** Cramps aam hain. Hot-water bottle, garam paani se nahana aur halki movement se aaram milta hai. Jo dard school ya khel rok de, uske liye doctor ko dikhana zaroori hai.
- **"Kya main khel sakti hoon, naha sakti hoon, kitchen mein ja sakti hoon?"** Haan. Periods ke dauraan rok-tok ka koi medical basis nahi hai. Agar aapki family koi riwaaz maanti hai, toh saaf kahiye ki yeh riwaaz hai, health rule nahi, aur woh impure nahi hai.
- **"Meri saari friends ko aa gaya. Mujhe kyun nahi?"** Timing sabki alag hoti hai. Doston se pehle ya baad mein aana normal hai.
- **"Kya ab main badi ho gayi?"** Nahi. Pehle period ka matlab bas itna hai ki reproductive system mature hona shuru hua hai. Woh ab bhi bachchi hai, aur family ke andar ya bahar koi bhi uske private parts ko chhoo nahi sakta, na usse uski body ke baare mein koi baat chhupane ko keh sakta hai.

Aapko har jawab pata nahi hoga. "Mujhe nahi pata, chalo saath mein pata karte hain" bhi ek poora jawab hai. Zaroori yeh hai ki woh yeh sab pehle aapse sune, us din se pehle jab use iski zaroorat pade.

puberty-staring-harassment-body-policing.en:
Imagine a 12-year-old in Lucknow in the summer her chest begins to grow. Three things happen within a month. A man at the kirana shop looks at her in a way she has no word for. Her grandmother hands her a dupatta. And her evening cricket in the lane ends, by a decision nobody announces. Nobody says anything to the man at the shop.

## New body, new rules

Breast growth is often one of the first visible signs of puberty in girls, and it often arrives while she is still a child in every other way. What arrives with it, in many Indian homes, is a rulebook: dupatta, loose kurta, no shorts, straight home from tuition, no playing outside, do not laugh loudly, do not talk to boys.

Each rule is offered as protection. Each also carries a message: your body has become a problem, and managing it is your job. The rules tend to come before any explanation. A 2016 review in BMJ Open that pooled Indian studies found that only about half of adolescent girls, 48%, had been told about menstruation before their first period [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Many girls get the restrictions first and the biology later, if at all.

## What the street does, and what the records miss

Families are not imagining the danger. In 2005, 12% of households told the India Human Development Survey that unmarried girls in their neighbourhood were "sometimes" or "often" harassed. Police records for the same year implied a figure of 0.06% of households, a gap of about 200 times [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. The comparison is old, but it is a rare direct measure of how much harassment never becomes a case.
