Current police numbers should be read with that gap in mind. In 2024, police registered 15,609 cases of sexual harassment of women and 9,865 of stalking, plus 3,502 cases of sexual harassment of a child under the POCSO Act [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are counts of who reached a police station, not of what happens on the way to school.

The timing is not a coincidence. UNICEF's 2024 global estimates found that most childhood sexual violence happens in adolescence, with a significant spike between ages 14 and 17 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. In India's 2007 government study, sexual abuse reported by children peaked at ages 12 to 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The age at which a girl is handed the rulebook is the age at which the risk really does climb.

But the rulebook guards the lane, and the data does not stop at the lane. In police records of penetrative sexual assault on children, the accused is someone the child knows in the great majority of cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A dupatta is no protection from a relative, a tutor or a neighbour who is welcome in the house.

## Why the burden lands on girls

Because she is the one the family can control. The man at the shop, the boys on the bikes and the uncle who "jokes" are harder to confront than a daughter is to restrict. Harassment is also treated as damage to the family's izzat, and by that logic the thing to reduce is her visibility.

The costs are hers. She loses sport, movement, friendships and sometimes school. She also learns a theory of harassment: it happens because of her body. A girl who believes that will not tell her parents about the man who touched her on the bus. She expects blame, and she expects to lose more freedom. Body-policing helps produce the silence that the 12% and 0.06% figures measure.

Boys absorb the mirror image: looking is natural, and coping with it is a girl's work. Boys are harassed and abused as well, and nobody prepares them either.

## What the Supreme Court says about clothes and 'provocation'

In 2023 the Supreme Court published a handbook for judges on gender stereotypes. It lists the belief that a woman's clothing invites sexual contact among false stereotypes. It tells judges to write "street sexual harassment" in place of "eve teasing", and plain "clothing" in place of "provocative clothing" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> "A man who touches a woman without her consent must not be permitted to take the defence that the woman invited his touch by dressing in a particular way."

That sentence is from the handbook [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. The criminal law matches it. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, sexual harassment (Section 75) carries up to three years in prison for its most serious forms and up to one year for sexually coloured remarks, and words or gestures meant to insult a woman's modesty (Section 79) carry up to three years. Stalking (Section 78) carries up to three years, rising to five for a repeat offence [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. None of these sections asks what she was wearing. When the person targeted is under 18, POCSO applies as well, and it protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What families, schools and boys can do instead

**Families.** Give information before rules. Explain breast growth and periods early, and say plainly that her body is not the problem. Promise her that if anyone stares, comments, follows or touches, the fault is his, and that telling you will not cost her cricket, tuition or her phone. Then keep the promise. If a rule is really about safety, such as sharing a route or a return time, apply it to sons too.

**Schools.** Stop "decency" lectures given only to girls. Give students a known person to report to, and act on complaints about staff, van drivers and men at the gate.

**Boys and men.** Do not stare, comment, follow or film. When a friend does, say "bas kar" and mean it. Leave the WhatsApp group that rates girls' bodies.

**When it happens.** Call 112 in an emergency, and 1098 if the person targeted is under 18.

In that lane in Lucknow, the cheapest thing to change was a 12-year-old's evening. The right thing to change was the man at the shop.
puberty-staring-harassment-body-policing.hg:
Lucknow ki ek 12 saal ki ladki ko imagine kijiye, us garmi mein jab uski chest badhna shuru hoti hai. Ek mahine ke andar teen cheezein hoti hain. Kirana shop par ek aadmi use aise dekhta hai jiske liye uske paas koi word nahi hai. Uski dadi use dupatta thama deti hain. Aur gali mein shaam ka cricket band ho jaata hai, ek aise faisle se jiska kisi ne elaan nahi kiya. Shop wale aadmi se koi kuch nahi kehta.

## Nayi body, naye rules

Ladkiyon mein breast growth aksar puberty ke sabse pehle dikhne wale signs mein se ek hota hai, aur yeh tab aa jaata hai jab woh baaki har tarah se abhi bachchi hi hoti hai. Bahut se Indian gharon mein iske saath ek rulebook bhi aati hai: dupatta, dheela kurta, shorts nahi, tuition se seedha ghar, bahar khelna band, zor se mat hanso, ladkon se baat mat karo.

Har rule protection ke naam par diya jaata hai. Har rule ke saath ek message bhi aata hai: tumhari body ab ek problem ban gayi hai, aur use manage karna tumhara kaam hai. Rules aksar kisi bhi explanation se pehle aa jaate hain. BMJ Open ke 2016 ke ek review ne, jisne Indian studies ko pool kiya, paaya ki sirf lagbhag aadhi adolescent ladkiyon, 48%, ko pehle period se pehle menstruation ke baare mein bataya gaya tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Bahut si ladkiyon ko pabandiyan pehle milti hain aur biology baad mein, agar kabhi mile to.

## Sadak kya karti hai, aur records mein kya chhoot jaata hai

Families khatre ki kalpana nahi kar rahi. 2005 mein 12% households ne India Human Development Survey ko bataya ki unke neighbourhood mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "sometimes" ya "often" harass kiya jaata tha. Usi saal ke police records se jo figure nikalta tha woh 0.06% households ka tha, yaani lagbhag 200 guna ka gap [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. Yeh comparison purana hai, lekin kitna harassment kabhi case nahi banta, iska yeh ek kam milne wala seedha naap hai.

Aaj ke police numbers ko isi gap ko dhyaan mein rakhkar padhna chahiye. 2024 mein police ne women ke sexual harassment ke 15,609 aur stalking ke 9,865 cases register kiye, aur POCSO Act ke under bachche ke sexual harassment ke 3,502 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh un logon ki ginti hai jo police station tak pahunche, us sab ki nahi jo school ke raaste mein hota hai.

Timing bhi ittefaq nahi hai. UNICEF ke 2024 ke global estimates ke mutabiq bachpan ka zyadatar sexual violence adolescence mein hota hai, aur 14 se 17 saal ke beech ek significant spike aata hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. India ki 2007 ki sarkari study mein bachchon ka report kiya hua sexual abuse 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein peak par tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jis umar mein ladki ko rulebook thamai jaati hai, usi umar mein risk sach mein badhta hai.

Lekin rulebook sirf gali ki chaukidari karti hai, aur data gali par nahi rukta. Bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke police records ke bahut bade hisse mein accused koi aisa hota hai jise bachcha jaanta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Dupatta us rishtedaar, tutor ya padosi se nahi bachata jiska ghar mein swagat hota hai.

## Bojh ladkiyon par hi kyun aata hai

Kyunki family usi ko control kar sakti hai. Shop wale aadmi, bike wale ladkon aur "mazaak" karne wale uncle se takrana mushkil hai; beti par pabandi lagana aasaan. Harassment ko family ki izzat ka nuksaan bhi maana jaata hai, aur is logic se jo cheez kam karni hai woh ladki ka dikhna hai.

Keemat wahi chukati hai. Uska sport, ghoomna-phirna, dostiyan aur kabhi-kabhi school bhi chhoot jaata hai. Woh harassment ki ek theory bhi seekh leti hai: yeh meri body ki wajah se hota hai. Jo ladki yeh maanti hai, woh apne parents ko us aadmi ke baare mein nahi batayegi jisne use bus mein chhua. Use blame ki ummeed hoti hai, aur thodi aur azaadi chhinne ki bhi. Body-policing wahi chuppi paida karne mein madad karti hai jise 12% aur 0.06% wale figures naapte hain.

Ladke iska ulta sabak seekhte hain: dekhna natural hai, aur use jhelna ladki ka kaam hai. Ladkon ko bhi harass aur abuse kiya jaata hai, aur unhe bhi koi tayyar nahi karta.

## Kapdon aur 'provocation' par Supreme Court kya kehta hai

2023 mein Supreme Court ne judges ke liye gender stereotypes par ek handbook publish ki. Yeh is belief ko false stereotypes mein ginti hai ki aurat ke kapde sexual contact ko invite karte hain. Yeh judges se kehti hai ki "eve teasing" ki jagah "street sexual harassment" likhein, aur "provocative clothing" ki jagah sirf "clothing" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> "A man who touches a woman without her consent must not be permitted to take the defence that the woman invited his touch by dressing in a particular way."

Yeh line usi handbook ki hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Matlab: jo aadmi kisi aurat ko uski consent ke bina chhue, use yeh defence lene ki ijazat nahi honi chahiye ki aurat ne apne pehnawe se us touch ko invite kiya. Criminal law bhi yahi kehta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke under sexual harassment (Section 75) ke sabse serious roop par teen saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai aur sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak, aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale words ya gestures (Section 79) par teen saal tak. Stalking (Section 78) par teen saal tak, aur dobara karne par paanch saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In mein se koi section yeh nahi poochhta ki usne kya pehna tha. Jab target kiya gaya insaan 18 se kam ho, to POCSO bhi lagta hai, aur woh ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Families, schools aur ladke iski jagah kya kar sakte hain

**Families.** Rules se pehle information dijiye. Breast growth aur periods ke baare mein jaldi samjhaiye, aur saaf kahiye ki problem uski body nahi hai. Usse promise kijiye ki agar koi ghoore, comment kare, peecha kare ya chhue, to galti uski hai, aur aapko batane se uska cricket, tuition ya phone nahi chhinega. Phir yeh promise nibhaiye. Agar koi rule sach mein safety ke liye hai, jaise route ya lautne ka time share karna, to use beton par bhi lagu kijiye.

**Schools.** Sirf ladkiyon ko diye jaane wale "decency" lectures band kijiye. Students ko ek jaana-pehchaana insaan dijiye jise woh report kar sakein, aur staff, van drivers aur gate par khade aadmiyon ki complaints par action lijiye.

**Ladke aur mard.** Ghooro mat, comment mat karo, peecha mat karo, film mat karo. Jab koi dost aisa kare, to "bas kar" kaho aur sach mein use roko. Us WhatsApp group se nikal jao jo ladkiyon ki bodies ko rate karta hai.

**Jab aisa ho.** Emergency mein 112 par call kijiye, aur target kiya gaya insaan 18 se kam ho to 1098 par.

Lucknow ki us gali mein sabse sasti cheez jo badli ja sakti thi, woh ek 12 saal ki bachchi ki shaam thi. Jo badalna chahiye tha, woh shop wala aadmi tha.

puberty-timing-early-late-questions.en:
Imagine two girls in the same Class 6 section in Nagpur. One began developing breasts at seven and got her first period at nine; a neighbour blames "too much mobile". The other is 13 with no sign of change, and her grandmother says doctors are for sick people. Neither child has been told what is happening to her body. That silence costs more than embarrassment, because these are also the years in which Indian children report the most sexual abuse.

## What is puberty, and when is it 'on time'?

Puberty is the stretch of years in which the brain signals the ovaries or testes to make sex hormones and a child's body becomes an adult's. It usually begins between 8 and 13 in girls and between 9 and 14 in boys. In girls the first sign is usually a breast bud, with the first period usually coming some time after it. In boys the testes grow first; the voice change, height spurt and facial hair follow.

That is a window five years wide. Two classmates of the same age can sit at opposite ends of it and both be healthy. The best clue is family: ask when parents and older siblings changed.

## Early, late or different: what does it mean?

Doctors call puberty early, or precocious, when breast development or pubic hair appears before 8 in girls, or testicular growth or pubic hair before 9 in boys. It is delayed when there is no breast development by 13, no testicular growth by 14, or no period by 15. These are lines for getting checked, not diagnoses.

Many late starters are simply following a family pattern. Other possible causes include long-term illness, being very underweight, eating disorders, and thyroid or pituitary problems. Whether a child is early or late, only a doctor can tell whether there is a cause that needs treatment.

Sometimes a check-up finds something the family never suspected: an intersex variation, meaning sex characteristics such as chromosomes, hormones or internal organs that do not fit the typical definitions of male or female. Some may first come to light around puberty, for example when periods do not start. It is a natural difference, not an illness, and the young person deserves privacy and a say over their own body.

Neighbourhood theories about phones, films or "hot" food are not a diagnosis; a doctor's check is. And a girl who looks 15 at 10 is still 10.

## When should we see a doctor, and which one?

Go if any of those lines is crossed, or if a worry will not go away. Start with a paediatrician or general physician, who may refer you to a hormone specialist (endocrinologist) or a gynaecologist. Expect questions about family history, a height and weight check, a brief examination, and sometimes blood tests and a hand X-ray. A child can ask what will be done and why, and have a parent or nurse present.

Many children need only monitoring. Hormone tablets, "height" powders and gym supplements are no substitute for a diagnosis and should never be given without a specialist's advice.

The government runs Adolescent Friendly Health Centres for adolescents [[nhm-afhc]], with counselling and clinical care at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Until October 2025 they were called "clinics"; the Health Ministry changed the name because, it said, a visit to a "clinic" was "looked upon with suspicion". By its count, about 1.7 crore adolescents used the services in 2024-25, a figure that may count visits rather than individuals [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

One limit on privacy: anyone who knows or suspects a sexual offence against a child, a doctor included, must report it to the police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Ordinary puberty worries do not trigger that duty, and the centres' own benchmark is privacy and confidentiality [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

## Why does the body talk have to start before 10?

Because the body can start at 8, and the explanation has to arrive first. A 2016 review in BMJ Open found that only about half of adolescent girls in India (48%) had been told about menstruation before their first period [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. A child who meets blood, or a wet dream, with no explanation learns one thing: this is shameful, do not ask.

An abuser depends on exactly that lesson. The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, which surveyed 12,447 children across 13 states, found that the sexual abuse children reported began as early as age 5, gained momentum from age 10 and peaked at 12-15 years [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Half the abusers were people the child knew or people in positions of trust, and of the children who reported sexual assault, 72.1% had told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The sample was purposive, not random, and the study is nineteen years old, so treat its numbers as a warning sign, not a current national rate.

> A child with words for the body can say what happened. A child taught that the body is unmentionable cannot.

Many parents fear that information works as an invitation. The UN's 2018 guidance on sexuality education says the opposite: it does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates, while abstinence-only programmes are ineffective in delaying first sex [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## What do I actually say to a child?

Short, true sentences, repeated over years, do more than one big talk.

To a six-year-old: "Every part of your body has a real name. Nobody may touch or look at your private parts except to keep you clean or healthy, and no adult should ask you to keep a secret about bodies. If it happens, tell me. You will never be in trouble."

To an eight-year-old: "In the next few years your body will start changing. It happens to everyone, at different times. One day you may find blood in your underwear, or wake up with it wet and sticky. Both are healthy. Here is what to do."

To the child who is first or last in class: "Your body has its own clock. If it worries you, we will ask a doctor together."

And if a child tells you someone has touched them: believe them, do not ask why they stayed quiet, and call Child Helpline 1098 or 112.
puberty-timing-early-late-questions.hg:
Nagpur ke ek school ki Class 6 ke ek hi section mein do ladkiyon ko imagine karo. Ek ke breasts saat saal ki umar mein develop hone lage the aur nau mein pehla period aa gaya; padosan iska dosh "zyada mobile" ko deti hai. Doosri 13 ki hai, uski body mein abhi koi change nahi aaya, aur uski dadi kehti hain ki doctor ke paas bimaar log jaate hain. Dono mein se kisi bachchi ko nahi bataya gaya ki uski body mein ho kya raha hai. Is chuppi ki keemat sirf sharmindagi nahi hai, kyunki yahi woh saal hain jinme Indian bachche sabse zyada sexual abuse report karte hain.

## Puberty kya hai, aur 'time par' kab hoti hai?

Puberty woh kuch saal hain jinme brain ovaries ya testes ko sex hormones banane ka signal deta hai aur bachche ki body adult ki body banti hai. Ladkiyon mein yeh aam taur par 8 se 13 ke beech shuru hoti hai, aur ladkon mein 9 se 14 ke beech. Ladkiyon mein pehla sign aksar breast bud hota hai, aur pehla period aam taur par uske kuch samay baad aata hai. Ladkon mein pehle testes badhte hain; awaaz ka badalna, height ka tezi se badhna aur chehre ke baal baad mein aate hain.

Yaani yeh paanch saal chaudi window hai. Ek hi umar ke do classmates iske do alag kinaaron par ho sakte hain aur dono healthy ho sakte hain. Sabse accha clue family hai: poochho ki mummy-papa aur bade bhai-behen mein changes kab aaye the.

## Jaldi, late ya alag: iska matlab kya hai?

Doctors puberty ko early ya precocious tab kehte hain jab ladkiyon mein breast development ya pubic hair 8 se pehle dikhe, ya ladkon mein testes ki growth ya pubic hair 9 se pehle. Delayed tab kehte hain jab 13 tak breast development na ho, 14 tak testes na badhein, ya 15 tak period na aaye. Yeh check-up karwane ki lines hain, diagnosis nahi.

Bahut se late starters bas apni family ka pattern follow kar rahe hote hain. Baaki mumkin wajahon mein lambi bimaari, bahut kam weight, eating disorders, aur thyroid ya pituitary ki problems shaamil hain. Bachcha jaldi ho ya late, sirf doctor bata sakta hai ki koi aisi wajah hai ya nahi jiska ilaaj chahiye.

Kabhi-kabhi check-up mein kuch aisa nikalta hai jiska family ko andaaza bhi nahi tha: intersex variation, yaani chromosomes, hormones ya andar ke organs jaise sex characteristics jo male ya female ki typical definition mein fit nahi hote. Kuch variations pehli baar puberty ke aas-paas saamne aa sakte hain, jaise jab periods shuru hi nahi hote. Yeh ek natural difference hai, bimaari nahi, aur us young person ko privacy aur apni body ke faislon mein apni baat rakhne ka haq hai.

Phone, films ya "garam" khaane wali mohalle ki theories diagnosis nahi hain; doctor ka check hi diagnosis hai. Aur jo ladki 10 ki umar mein 15 ki dikhti hai, woh phir bhi 10 ki hi hai.

## Doctor ko kab dikhana chahiye, aur kaun se doctor ko?

Tab jao jab upar wali koi line cross ho, ya koi chinta jaa hi na rahi ho. Paediatrician ya general physician se shuru karo; woh hormone specialist (endocrinologist) ya gynaecologist ke paas bhej sakte hain. Family history ke sawaal, height aur weight ka check, ek chhota sa examination, aur kabhi-kabhi blood tests aur haath ka X-ray ho sakta hai. Bachcha pooch sakta hai ki kya kiya jaayega aur kyun, aur mummy-papa ya nurse ko saath rakh sakta hai.

Bahut se bachchon ko sirf monitoring ki zaroorat hoti hai. Hormone tablets, "height" powder aur gym supplements diagnosis ki jagah nahi le sakte, aur specialist ki salah ke bina kabhi nahi dene chahiye.

Sarkar adolescents ke liye Adolescent Friendly Health Centres chalati hai [[nhm-afhc]], jahan primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling aur clinical care milti hai [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. October 2025 tak inhe "clinic" kaha jaata tha; Health Ministry ne naam badla kyunki, uske mutabik, "clinic" jaane ko "looked upon with suspicion", yaani shaq ki nazar se dekha jaata tha. Ministry ki ginti ke hisaab se 2024-25 mein kareeb 1.7 crore adolescents ne yeh services li; is figure mein log nahi, visits gine gaye ho sakte hain [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

Privacy ki ek limit hai: jise bhi kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence ka pata ho ya shaq ho, doctor samet, use police ko report karna hi padta hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Puberty ki aam chintaaon par yeh duty laagu nahi hoti, aur in centres ka apna benchmark privacy aur confidentiality hai [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

## Body ki baat 10 saal se pehle kyun shuru honi chahiye?

Kyunki body 8 mein shuru ho sakti hai, aur samjhana usse pehle pahunchna chahiye. BMJ Open ke 2016 ke ek review ne paaya ki India ki adolescent ladkiyon mein se sirf kareeb aadhi (48%) ko pehle period se pehle menstruation ke baare mein bataya gaya tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Jo bachcha bina kisi explanation ke khoon ya wet dream ka saamna karta hai, woh ek hi cheez seekhta hai: yeh sharm ki baat hai, poochhna mat.

Abuser theek isi sabak par depend karta hai. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse ne 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon ka survey kiya aur paaya ki bachchon ka bataya hua sexual abuse 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho jaata tha, 10 saal se tezi pakadta tha aur 12-15 years par peak karta tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Aadhe abusers bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale ya bharose ki position wale log the, aur jin bachchon ne sexual assault bataya, unme se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Sample purposive tha, random nahi, aur study unnees saal purani hai, isliye iske numbers ko warning sign samjho, aaj ka national rate nahi.

> Jis bachche ke paas body ke liye shabd hain, woh bata sakta hai ki kya hua. Jise sikhaya gaya ki body ka naam bhi nahi lena, woh nahi bata sakta.

Bahut se parents ko darr hota hai ki jaankari dena invitation dene jaisa hai. Sexuality education par UN ki 2018 guidance iska ulta kehti hai: isse sexual activity, sexual risk-taking ya STI/HIV infection rates nahi badhte, jabki abstinence-only programmes pehla sex delay karne mein ineffective paaye gaye hain [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Bachche se asal mein kya kahun?

Chhote, sachche sentences, jo saalon tak dohraaye jaayein, ek badi "talk" se zyada kaam karte hain.

Chhe saal ke bachche se: "Tumhari body ke har part ka ek asli naam hai. Tumhe saaf ya healthy rakhne ke alaava koi tumhare private parts ko chhu ya dekh nahi sakta, aur koi bada tumse body ke baare mein secret rakhne ko nahi keh sakta. Aisa ho toh mujhe batana. Tumhe kabhi daant nahi padegi."

Aath saal ke bachche se: "Agle kuch saalon mein tumhari body badalne lagegi. Yeh sabke saath hota hai, alag-alag time par. Ek din tumhe underwear mein khoon dikh sakta hai, ya subah woh geela aur chipchipa mil sakta hai. Dono healthy hain. Tab yeh karna hai."

Us bachche se jo class mein sabse pehle ya sabse aakhir mein badal raha hai: "Tumhari body ki apni ghadi hai. Agar chinta ho, toh hum saath mein doctor se poochhenge."

Aur agar bachcha bataye ki kisi ne use chhua hai: uski baat maano, yeh mat poochho ki ab tak chup kyun raha, aur Child Helpline 1098 ya 112 par call karo.

real-words-body-parts-abuse.en:
Imagine a six-year-old in Kanpur at bedtime. She tells her mother, "Bhaiya ne wahan chhua." *Wahan* could be her arm, her stomach, anywhere. Her mother, half asleep, says, "Achha, so jao." The girl has used the only word she owns for that part of her body, and it did not work. She may not try a second time.

In most Indian homes a child is taught aankh, naak, kaan and pet, and then the map goes blank. The blank gets filled with "su-su", "shame-shame", "neeche" and "wahan". This guide is about why that matters for a child's safety, and how to fix it.

## The words we use instead

A nickname is not the problem; "su-su" is a fine word for a toddler. The trouble starts when the nickname is the only word a child has, and when it arrives with a hush: a giggle, a "chhee". The child learns two lessons at once: this part of me has no proper name, and good children do not mention it.

The proper names are ordinary anatomy: penis, testicles, vulva (the outside), vagina (the passage inside), anus, buttocks, breasts and nipples. They are no ruder than "elbow". A family can keep its home-language word too, as long as the child also knows the standard one and has learnt that saying it aloud gets a calm answer.

## Who abuses, and how few children tell

Police records explain the urgency. In 2024, in 96.6% of penetrative sexual assault cases registered under POCSO, 42,634 of 44,126, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That group is broad: family members, neighbours and family friends, and also the "friends" and partners of older teenagers, because the law treats all sexual activity under 18 as an offence.

Of the 44,567 victims recorded that year, 831 were under six and 3,438 were aged six to 12: 4,269 children under 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These counts are minimums, because young children rarely disclose.

How rarely? The main government study is old. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of the children who reported being sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had reported it to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The sample was not nationally representative and predates POCSO, so treat it as a warning sign rather than a precise measure.

So the person harming a child is usually someone the child knows, and grooming depends on secrecy [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. The child's way out is to tell an adult, in words, something that adult does not want to hear.

## Why real words help a child disclose

The first reason is clarity. "Usne meri vulva ko chhua" cannot be mistaken for teasing. "Usne wahan tang kiya" can be waved away in a second.

The second is permission. A child taught that these parts are "shame-shame" concludes that talking about them is naughty, and carries the shame for what someone else did. Abusers use this, with lines such as "Yeh gandi baat hai, batayegi toh tujhe hi daant padegi." A child who has said "penis" and "vulva" at bath time without any adult flinching already knows the subject is allowed at home.

The third is being understood outside the home. If a case reaches the police, the law requires the child's statement to be recorded at home or at a place the child chooses, as far as practicable by a woman officer who is not in uniform [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The statement is still built from the child's own words. A nickname does not make an account less true, but a precise word leaves less room for doubt.

One honest limit: vocabulary does not stop abuse. A child who knows every term can still be targeted, and still be too frightened to speak. Preventing abuse is the adults' job; words remove one barrier among many.

## Teaching the names, age by age

**Toddlers and pre-schoolers.** Name the genitals at bath time, in the tone you use for "knee". Add one rule: these parts are private, nobody touches them except to keep you clean or healthy, and nobody may ask you to keep a secret about touching.

**Primary school.** Ask the child to name two or three adults they would tell, at least one outside the home. Teach sons the same words and rules: the 2007 study found more boys than girls among the children who reported sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

**Before puberty, and after.** Explain periods, breast growth, erections and wet dreams before they arrive, so the body's changes do not become a second secret. With teenagers, move on to consent, online "friends" and the law.

None of this is radical. In September 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent and the impact of exploitation, and suggested that the Union government consider an expert committee on health and sex education and POCSO awareness for children from an early age [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. These were suggestions, not binding orders. The UN's international guidance on sexuality education, revised in 2018, states that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity or sexual risk-taking [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Until schools do it, home is the classroom.

## If a child tells you

Stay calm; a shocked face teaches silence. Say three things: "I believe you. It is not your fault. You did the right thing by telling me." Let the child use their own words. Do not correct their vocabulary, and do not ask "why didn't you tell me earlier".

Do not promise to keep it secret. Under Sections 19 and 21 of the POCSO Act, anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it, and failing to do so is punishable with up to six months in prison, a fine, or both [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Say instead: "I will keep you safe, and I will tell only the people whose job is to stop this." Then call the Child Helpline, 1098, which runs round the clock [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The six-year-old in Kanpur did everything a child can do. The missing piece was a word, and it was never hers to supply.
real-words-body-parts-abuse.hg:
Kanpur ki ek chhah saal ki bachchi ko imagine kijiye. Raat ko sote waqt woh apni mummy se kehti hai, "Bhaiya ne wahan chhua." *Wahan* ka matlab uska haath ho sakta hai, pet ho sakta hai, kuch bhi. Mummy neend mein kehti hain, "Achha, so jao." Bachchi ne body ke us hisse ke liye apna iklauta word use kar liya, aur woh kaam nahi aaya. Ho sakta hai woh dobara koshish hi na kare.

Zyadatar Indian gharon mein bachche ko aankh, naak, kaan aur pet sikhaya jaata hai, aur uske baad map khaali ho jaata hai. Us khaali jagah ko "su-su", "shame-shame", "neeche" aur "wahan" bhar dete hain. Yeh guide isi baare mein hai: bachche ki safety ke liye yeh kyun matter karta hai, aur ise theek kaise karein.

## Asli naam ki jagah hum kya bolte hain

Nickname problem nahi hai; chhote bachche ke liye "su-su" bilkul theek word hai. Dikkat tab shuru hoti hai jab bachche ke paas sirf nickname hi ho, aur woh bhi dabi hui hansi ya "chhee" ke saath mile. Bachcha ek saath do baatein seekh leta hai: mere is hisse ka koi sahi naam nahi hai, aur achche bachche iska zikr nahi karte.

Sahi naam seedhi-saadi anatomy hain: penis, testicles, vulva (bahar ka hissa), vagina (andar ka raasta), anus, buttocks, breasts aur nipples. Yeh "kohni" se zyada gande words nahi hain. Family apni ghar ki bhasha wala word bhi rakh sakti hai, bas bachche ko standard naam bhi pata ho aur usne yeh seekha ho ki use zor se bolne par shaant jawab milta hai.

## Abuse kaun karta hai, aur kitne kam bachche batate hain

Police records batate hain ki yeh itna urgent kyun hai. 2024 mein POCSO ke under register hue penetrative sexual assault ke 96.6% cases mein, yaani 44,126 mein se 42,634 mein, accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh group kaafi bada hai: family members, padosi aur family friends, aur bade teenagers ke "friends" aur partners bhi, kyunki kanoon 18 se kam umar mein har sexual activity ko offence maanta hai.

Us saal record hue 44,567 victims mein se 831 chhah saal se chhote the aur 3,438 chhah se 12 saal ke the: yaani 12 se kam umar ke 4,269 bachche [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh counts minimum hain, kyunki chhote bachche bahut kam batate hain.

Kitna kam? Sarkar ki main study purani hai. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein, jin bachchon ne sexual assault report kiya unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko report kiya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Sample nationally representative nahi tha aur yeh study POCSO se pehle ki hai, isliye ise exact measurement nahi, ek warning sign samjhiye.

Yaani bachche ko nuksaan pahunchane wala aksar koi aisa hota hai jise bachcha jaanta hai, aur grooming secrecy par hi tiki hoti hai [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Bachche ke paas nikalne ka raasta yahi hai ki woh kisi bade ko, shabdon mein, woh baat bataye jo woh bada sunna nahi chahta.

## Asli words bachche ko batane mein kaise madad karte hain

Pehli wajah clarity hai. "Usne meri vulva ko chhua" ko koi chhed-chhaad samajhkar taal nahi sakta. "Usne wahan tang kiya" ek second mein taal diya jaata hai.

Doosri wajah permission hai. Jis bachche ko sikhaya gaya ho ki yeh hisse "shame-shame" hain, woh maan leta hai ki inke baare mein bolna gandi baat hai, aur kisi aur ki harkat ki sharm khud dhota hai. Abusers isi ka fayda uthate hain, aisi lines ke saath: "Yeh gandi baat hai, batayegi toh tujhe hi daant padegi." Jis bachche ne nahate waqt "penis" aur "vulva" bola ho aur kisi bade ne muh na banaya ho, use pehle se pata hota hai ki ghar mein is topic par baat ho sakti hai.

Teesri wajah hai ghar ke bahar samjha jaana. Agar case police tak pahunche, to kanoon kehta hai ki bachche ka statement uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par record ho, aur jahan tak ho sake use ek woman officer le jo uniform mein na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Phir bhi statement bachche ke apne words se hi banta hai. Nickname se bachche ki baat kam sach nahi ho jaati, lekin precise word shak ki gunjaish kam chhodta hai.

Ek imaandaar limit: vocabulary abuse nahi rokti. Jis bachche ko har term pata ho, use bhi target kiya ja sakta hai, aur woh bhi itna dara hua ho sakta hai ki bol na paaye. Abuse rokna badon ka kaam hai; words bahut si rukawaton mein se sirf ek hatate hain.

## Naam sikhana, umar ke hisaab se

**Toddlers aur pre-schoolers.** Nahlate waqt genitals ke naam usi tone mein lijiye jismein aap "ghutna" bolte hain. Saath mein ek rule jodiye: yeh hisse private hain, inhe koi nahi chhuta siwaay tumhe saaf ya healthy rakhne ke liye, aur koi bhi tumse touch ke baare mein secret rakhne ko nahi keh sakta.

**Primary school.** Bachche se do-teen aise badon ke naam poochhiye jinhe woh batayega, jinmein kam se kam ek ghar ke bahar ka ho. Beton ko bhi wahi words aur wahi rules sikhaiye: 2007 ki study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein ladke ladkiyon se zyada the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

**Puberty se pehle, aur baad mein.** Periods, breast growth, erections aur wet dreams ke baare mein unke aane se pehle samjhaiye, taaki body ke changes ek aur secret na ban jaayein. Teenagers ke saath consent, online "friends" aur kanoon par baat kijiye.

Ismein kuch bhi radical nahi hai. September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne aisi comprehensive sex education ki recommendation ki jismein consent aur exploitation ke asar ki samajh shaamil ho, aur suggest kiya ki Union government health aur sex education aur chhoti umar se bachchon mein POCSO awareness ke liye ek expert committee banane par vichaar kare [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Yeh suggestions the, binding orders nahi. Sexuality education par UN ki international guidance, jo 2018 mein revise hui, saaf kehti hai ki sexuality education se sexual activity ya sexual risk-taking nahi badhti [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Jab tak schools yeh nahi karte, ghar hi classroom hai.

## Agar bachcha aapko bataye

Shaant rahiye; chaunka hua chehra bachche ko chup rehna sikhata hai. Teen baatein kahiye: "Mujhe tum par yakeen hai. Tumhari koi galti nahi hai. Tumne batakar bilkul sahi kiya." Bachche ko apne words use karne dijiye. Uski vocabulary theek mat kijiye, aur yeh mat poochhiye ki "pehle kyun nahi bataya".

Secret rakhne ka promise mat kijiye. POCSO Act ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke under, jise bhi child sexual abuse ka pata ho use report karna zaroori hai, aur report na karne par chhah mahine tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Iski jagah kahiye: "Hum tumhe safe rakhenge, aur sirf un logon ko batayenge jinka kaam ise rokna hai." Phir Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye, jo din-raat chalti hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Kanpur ki us chhah saal ki bachchi ne woh sab kiya jo ek bachcha kar sakta hai. Kami sirf ek word ki thi, aur woh word dena kabhi uski zimmedari thi hi nahi.

shame-buying-pads-condoms.en:
You ask for a packet of sanitary pads. The chemist does not simply hand it over. First he wraps it in a sheet of newspaper, or drops it into a black polythene bag he keeps for two or three products. A strip of paracetamol crosses the same counter in the open. Nobody ordered this. It is just done, in shop after shop, and it tells a 13-year-old something no textbook does: what your body needs every month is a thing to be hidden.

## The newspaper wrap

The wrap is offered as a courtesy. The shopkeeper believes he is saving the customer from embarrassment. But the embarrassment is taught, and the wrap is one of its teachers. The same ritual follows condoms, pregnancy test kits and emergency pills: the lowered voice, the wait until the shop empties, the purchase made three neighbourhoods from home.

The counter is repeating a rule that begins in the family. A 2016 review that pooled Indian studies found that only about half of adolescent girls, 48%, had been told about menstruation before their first period. It found that 77% were kept from religious activities during their periods, and that only one in eight faced no restriction at all [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Periods may happen, the rule says, but they must not be seen.

The product has won. The shame has not lost. Sanitary napkin use among women aged 15-24 rose from 41.8% in 2015-16 [[nfhs4-india-2016]] to 64.4% in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Far more packets cross the counter now, and they are still wrapped.

## What the surveys show about who knows what

India's National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) put two statements to men aged 15-49. In reply, 35.1% agreed that "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it". And 19.6% agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Put the two answers side by side. More than a third of men hand the job to women, and about a fifth are ready to judge a woman for doing it. She is expected to manage contraception and to be suspected because she does.

The same survey shows where that leaves young women. Among people aged 15-24, only 54.4% of women knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey counted any man who had used a condom in the past year as knowing a source, which lifts the male figure a little. It does not explain a gap this wide.

> Nearly half of young women could not name one place to get the only contraceptive that also cuts the risk of infections.

A chemist's counter is a place where men have been allowed to stand. A young man buying condoms may be teased. A young woman buying them risks being talked about. The survey does not measure shame directly, but a gap this size is consistent with a counter that young women are taught to avoid.

## When shame becomes a health risk

Shame does not stop anyone from having periods or sex. It changes what they do about them.

**Condoms.** They are the only contraceptive that also reduces the risk of sexually transmitted infections, though they do not remove it [[who-sti]]. In typical use, about 13 in 100 couples relying on external condoms have a pregnancy in a year. With no method it is about 85 [[who-fp]]. A condom that was too embarrassing to buy puts a couple in the second group.

**Emergency contraception.** It works up to 5 days after unprotected sex, and the sooner it is taken the better [[who-ec]]. It is not abortion. Each day spent gathering the courage to walk into a shop makes it less effective.

**Pads.** Consider a girl who cannot ask her father for pad money, or will not go to the shop where the owner knows her family. She makes one pad last far too long, or misses school. For a trans man or a non-binary person who has periods, the counter is harder still.

**Clinics.** The government has admitted the problem in its own words. In October 2025 the Health Ministry renamed Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics as "Centres", saying adolescents hesitated to come because a visit to a "clinic" was "looked upon with suspicion" [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]]. That is an official record of what stigma does to care.

## Buying pads, condoms or a test without embarrassment

- **No prescription is needed** for pads, condoms or a home pregnancy test. A pharmacist or a doctor can provide emergency contraception.
- **Name it plainly.** Brand and size, the way you would ask for toothpaste. You owe nobody a reason.
- **Check the pack.** Look at the expiry date and the seal. Keep condoms away from heat, so not in a wallet or a scooter's storage box.
- **Use the route that works.** A supermarket shelf, a bigger pharmacy or an online order are all legitimate. The goal is to have the product, not to win an argument.
- **Refuse the wrap if you want to.** "Bag nahi chahiye" is enough.
- **If you are under 18.** Buying condoms or asking about contraception is not an offence. But under POCSO any sexual act with a person under 18 is an offence whatever was agreed, and a doctor or counsellor who learns of one must report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. You are still entitled to information and care. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Changing the counter, one purchase at a time

Shopkeepers can stop wrapping unless a customer asks. Parents can put pads on the monthly grocery list beside soap and tea, and send sons to buy them.

Men can make sure they are not in the 35.1%: carry the condoms, pay for them, and buy pads for a sister or a partner without making it a favour.

The wrap survives because everyone at the counter goes along with it. It will end the same way, one unwrapped packet at a time.
shame-buying-pads-condoms.hg:
Tum sanitary pads ka ek packet maangti ho. Chemist use seedha pakda nahi deta. Pehle woh use akhbaar ke panne mein lapetta hai, ya us kaali polythene mein daal deta hai jo usne do-teen products ke liye hi rakhi hai. Paracetamol ki strip usi counter se khule mein nikal jaati hai. Kisi ne iska order nahi diya. Bas aisa hota hai, dukaan dar dukaan, aur yeh ek 13 saal ki ladki ko woh sikha deta hai jo koi textbook nahi sikhati: tumhari body ko har mahine jo chahiye, woh chhupane ki cheez hai.

## Akhbaar wala wrap

Wrap ko tameez ki tarah pesh kiya jaata hai. Dukaandaar ko lagta hai ki woh customer ko sharmindagi se bacha raha hai. Par yeh sharmindagi sikhayi jaati hai, aur wrap uske teachers mein se ek hai. Yahi rasam condoms, pregnancy test kits aur emergency pills ke saath bhi chalti hai: dheemi aawaz, dukaan khaali hone ka intezaar, aur ghar se teen mohalle door ki gayi khareedari.

Counter wahi rule dohra raha hai jo family mein shuru hota hai. 2016 ke ek review ne India ki kai studies ko jod kar dekha aur paaya ki sirf lagbhag aadhi adolescent girls, yaani 48%, ko pehle period se pehle menstruation ke baare mein bataya gaya tha. Usne yeh bhi paaya ki 77% ko periods ke dauraan religious activities se door rakha jaata tha, aur sirf aath mein se ek ladki par koi restriction nahi thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Rule yeh kehta hai: periods hon toh hon, par dikhne nahi chahiye.

Product jeet gaya hai. Sharam haari nahi hai. 15-24 saal ki women mein sanitary napkin ka use 2015-16 ke 41.8% [[nfhs4-india-2016]] se badh kar 2019-21 mein 64.4% ho gaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ab counter se kahin zyada packets nikalte hain, aur ab bhi lipte hue nikalte hain.

## Surveys kya dikhate hain: kaun kya jaanta hai

India ke National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) ne 15-49 saal ke men ke saamne do statements rakhe. Jawab mein 35.1% ne maana ki "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it", yaani contraception women ka kaam hai aur man ko iski fikr nahi karni chahiye. Aur 19.6% ne maana ki contraception use karne wali women promiscuous ho sakti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Dono jawab saath rakh kar dekho. Ek-tihai se zyada men yeh kaam women par daal dete hain, aur lagbhag paanchva hissa us woman ko judge karne ko taiyaar hai jo yeh kaam karti hai. Usse umeed hai ki contraception wahi sambhale, aur sambhalne par shak bhi usi par ho.

Wahi survey dikhata hai ki isse young women kahan pahunchti hain. 15-24 saal ke logon mein sirf 54.4% women ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey ne har us man ko, jisne pichhle saal condom use kiya tha, source jaanne wala gina, jisse men ka figure thoda upar jaata hai. Par itna bada gap isse explain nahi hota.

> Lagbhag aadhi young women ek bhi aisi jagah nahi bata payi jahan woh akela contraceptive milta hai jo infections ka risk bhi ghatata hai.

Chemist ka counter woh jagah hai jahan men ko khade hone ki ijazat rahi hai. Condom kharidne wale ladke ko shayad chidhaya jaye. Condom kharidne wali ladki ke baare mein baatein banti hain. Survey sharam ko seedhe nahi naapta, par itna bada gap usi counter se mel khaata hai jisse young women ko door rehna sikhaya jaata hai.

## Jab sharam health risk ban jaati hai

Sharam kisi ke periods ya sex ko nahi rokti. Woh bas yeh badal deti hai ki log uske baare mein kya karte hain.

**Condoms.** Yeh akela contraceptive hai jo sexually transmitted infections ka risk bhi kam karta hai, haalanki poora khatam nahi karta [[who-sti]]. Typical use mein, external condoms par depend karne wale 100 couples mein se lagbhag 13 ko ek saal mein pregnancy hoti hai. Koi method na ho toh yeh lagbhag 85 hai [[who-fp]]. Jo condom sharam ki wajah se kharida hi nahi gaya, woh couple ko doosre group mein daal deta hai.

**Emergency contraception.** Yeh unprotected sex ke baad 5 din tak kaam karta hai, aur jitna jaldi liya jaye utna behtar [[who-ec]]. Yeh abortion nahi hai. Dukaan mein ghusne ki himmat jutane mein jo bhi din nikalta hai, woh iska asar kam karta hai.

**Pads.** Socho ek ladki ke baare mein jo papa se pads ke paise nahi maang sakti, ya us dukaan par nahi jayegi jahan ka maalik uski family ko jaanta hai. Woh ek hi pad ko bahut der tak chalati hai, ya school miss karti hai. Jis trans man ya non-binary insaan ko periods hote hain, uske liye counter aur bhi mushkil hai.

**Clinics.** Government ne yeh problem apne shabdon mein maani hai. October 2025 mein Health Ministry ne Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics ka naam badal kar "Centres" kar diya, yeh kehte hue ki adolescents aane se hichkichate the kyunki "clinic" jaane ko "looked upon with suspicion", yaani shak ki nazar se dekha jaata tha [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]]. Yeh is baat ka official record hai ki stigma care ke saath kya karta hai.

## Pads, condoms ya test bina sharmindagi ke kaise khareedein

- **Prescription nahi chahiye** pads, condoms ya home pregnancy test ke liye. Emergency contraception pharmacist ya doctor de sakte hain.
- **Seedha naam lo.** Brand aur size, jaise toothpaste maangte ho. Tumhe kisi ko wajah batane ki zaroorat nahi.
- **Pack check karo.** Expiry date aur seal dekho. Condoms ko garmi se door rakho, yaani wallet ya scooter ki dikki mein nahi.
- **Jo raasta kaam kare, wahi lo.** Supermarket ka shelf, badi pharmacy ya online order, sab theek hain. Maqsad product haath mein hona hai, behes jeetna nahi.
- **Chaho toh wrap mana kar do.** "Bag nahi chahiye" kehna kaafi hai.
- **Agar tum 18 se kam ho.** Condoms kharidna ya contraception ke baare mein poochna offence nahi hai. Par POCSO ke under 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath koi bhi sexual act offence hai, chahe dono ne haan kaha ho, aur jis doctor ya counsellor ko iska pata chale use report karna padta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Information aur care ka haq tumhara phir bhi hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Counter badlega, ek-ek khareedari se

Dukaandaar tab tak wrap karna band kar sakte hain jab tak customer khud na maange. Parents pads ko mahine ki grocery list mein sabun aur chai ke saath likh sakte hain, aur beton ko kharidne bhej sakte hain.

Men yeh pakka kar sakte hain ki woh us 35.1% mein na hon: condoms khud rakho, khud paise do, aur behen ya partner ke liye pads kharido, bina ise ehsaan banaye.

Wrap isliye chal raha hai kyunki counter par khada har insaan iske saath chal deta hai. Yeh khatam bhi waise hi hoga, ek-ek bina lipte packet ke saath.

states-stall-menstrual-health-ruling.en:
On 30 January 2026, the Supreme Court of India tied a schoolgirl's period to the most basic promise in the Constitution. Menstrual health, it held, is part of the right to life under Article 21, and every school must give girls working, separate toilets with water, free sanitary napkins and a safe way to dispose of them [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Seven months later, the same court read the government's own figures and was not satisfied. This is how a fundamental right thins out between a Delhi courtroom and a school toilet in a district town, and what you can check before the next hearing.

## From a 2022 petition to a fundamental right

The case began in 2022 as a petition asking for free sanitary napkins and separate toilets for adolescent girls in schools [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-reserved-2024]]. In December 2024, the Union government told the court that a national menstrual hygiene policy for school-going girls had "recently been framed" and would have to be implemented by states and union territories, with distribution mainly through schools and anganwadis [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-reserved-2024]].

Hold on to that line. The Centre writes the policy; the states have to deliver it. Almost everything that went wrong afterwards happened in the gap between the two.

The judgment, by Justices J.B. Pardiwala and R. Mahadevan, went further. Beyond toilets, pads and disposal, it asked for "MHM corners" with spare uniforms, gender-responsive curricula from NCERT and the state councils, sensitisation of boys and male teachers, and inspections by District Education Officers [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. On paper, a girl whose period started in class would no longer have to walk home.

## What the Centre's September affidavit admitted

On 1 September 2026, the court took up compliance. The Union government's affidavit of 31 August, quoted in the court's order, said 39,439 girls' toilets had been identified as needing to be made functional. Of these, 30,458 had been built, 4,236 were under construction and 4,745 were still a gap: neither built nor being built [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. In the order's own arithmetic, that is 77% done, 11% in progress and 12% not begun.

The list came from UDISE+ 2024-25, the government's own school database, and states had been asked to close the gap before 8 March 2026 [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. By the end of August, that deadline had been missed by almost six months.

Notice two things. First, these figures count construction, while the judgment asked for functional toilets with usable water and handwashing [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. A toilet can be counted as "constructed" and still have no tap, no lock and no bin. Second, toilets are only one direction. These toilet figures say nothing about whether free pads, spare uniforms or sessions for boys have reached a single classroom.

## 'Mere formality': the court on the states' reports

The court did not soften its words. It said it was "discontent with the manner in which compliance is reported", and that the responses of some states showed "non-application of mind or rather mere formality" [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. It flagged data discrepancies in the reports of states including Tamil Nadu, Assam, Karnataka, Bihar, Gujarat, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh. Punjab's report could not even be read: the court found it illegible [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]].

Set that list beside what girls actually use. In the 2019-21 national family health survey (NFHS-5), only 59.2% of young women in Bihar used a hygienic method of period protection, against 98.4% in Tamil Nadu. Gujarat (66.9%) and Assam (67.0%) were also among the five lowest states [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

So unreliable reporting was not only a problem of the states already behind. But three of the five states where young women were worst served in 2019-21, Bihar, Gujarat and Assam, were among those whose compliance figures the court could not take at face value. When a state's paperwork cannot be trusted, nobody can say which school is still failing which girl.

## 'One last opportunity': the contempt warning

It got worse. LiveLaw reported on 15 October 2026 that the Union government's lawyer had told the court that states were not even answering the Centre's own requests for information [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]]. The court gave states "one last opportunity" to report compliance, and warned that it would issue contempt notices to the Chief Secretaries of states that failed to respond. The case is listed next on 14 December 2026 [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].

A Chief Secretary is the senior-most officer in a state's administration. A contempt notice is the court's formal step towards holding someone responsible for ignoring its orders. The court has moved from asking for reports to warning the officials who send them. A fundamental right that has to be enforced by warning Chief Secretaries is a right the system was not planning to deliver on its own.

## What to check in your school before 14 December

You do not need to wait for the hearing to know whether the order reached you. Our guide to what the ruling says every school owes girls has the full checklist. Here are the five questions the affidavit's figures could not answer:

- Is the girls' toilet functional, with a door that locks, running water and a place to wash hands, or only "constructed"?
- Can girls get free sanitary napkins at school quietly, without asking in front of the class?
- Is there a covered bin or another safe way to dispose of used pads?
- Is there an MHM corner with spare uniforms and pads for emergencies?
- Have boys and male teachers had any session on periods?

If any answer is no, write it down with the date and give it to the principal. The judgment gave District Education Officers the job of inspecting schools [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]], so a dated letter to the district education office is a fair next step; keep a copy. This is general information, not legal advice. A ruling becomes real only when the girl it was written for can use it on an ordinary school day.
states-stall-menstrual-health-ruling.hg:
30 January 2026 ko Supreme Court of India ne ek school jaane wali ladki ke periods ko Constitution ke sabse basic promise se jod diya. Court ne kaha ki menstrual health Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa hai. Har school ko ladkiyon ke liye alag, chaalu toilets dene honge jinmein paani ho, free sanitary napkins dene honge, aur used pads ko safely dispose karne ka intezaam karna hoga [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Saat mahine baad usi court ne sarkar ke apne figures padhe, aur court khush nahi tha. Yeh story batati hai ki ek fundamental right Delhi ke courtroom se nikal kar kisi district town ke school toilet tak pahunchte-pahunchte kaise patla pad jaata hai. Aur agli hearing se pehle tum apne school mein kya check kar sakte ho.

## 2022 ki ek petition se fundamental right tak

Yeh case 2022 mein ek petition se shuru hua. Maang thi ki schools mein adolescent ladkiyon ko free sanitary napkins aur alag toilets milein [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-reserved-2024]]. December 2024 mein Union government ne court ko bataya ki school jaane wali ladkiyon ke liye ek national menstrual hygiene policy "recently" banayi gayi hai, jise states aur union territories ko implement karna hoga, aur distribution zyada tar schools aur anganwadis ke through hoga [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-reserved-2024]].

Yeh line yaad rakhna. Policy Centre likhta hai; deliver states ko karna hota hai. Aage jo bhi gadbad hui, woh zyada tar inhi dono ke beech ke gap mein hui.

Judgment Justices J.B. Pardiwala aur R. Mahadevan ki bench ne diya, aur yeh policy se aage gaya. Toilets, pads aur disposal ke alawa court ne "MHM corners" maange jahan spare uniforms hon, NCERT aur state councils se gender-responsive curriculum maanga, boys aur male teachers ki sensitisation maangi, aur District Education Officers se schools ki inspection maangi [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Kaagaz par ab kisi ladki ka period class mein shuru ho jaaye, toh use ghar wapas nahi jaana padna chahiye tha.

## September mein Centre ke affidavit ne kya maana

1 September 2026 ko court ne compliance check ki. Court ke order mein Union government ke 31 August ke affidavit ka hisaab quote hai: 39,439 girls' toilets aise identify hue the jinhe functional banana tha. Inmein se 30,458 ban chuke the, 4,236 under construction the, aur 4,745 ab bhi gap the, yaani na bane the, na ban rahe the [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. Order ke apne hisaab se 77% ban gaye, 11% pe kaam chal raha tha aur 12% pe kaam shuru hi nahi hua tha.

Yeh list UDISE+ 2024-25 se bani thi, jo sarkar ka apna school database hai. States ko yeh gap 8 March 2026 se pehle bharne ko kaha gaya tha [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. August khatam hote-hote woh deadline lagbhag chhe mahine peeche chhoot chuki thi.

Do baatein notice karo. Pehli, yeh figures sirf construction count karte hain, jabki judgment ne aise functional toilets maange the jinmein use karne layak paani aur haath dhone ki jagah ho [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Ek toilet kaagaz par "constructed" gina ja sakta hai aur phir bhi usmein na nal ho, na lock, na dustbin. Doosri, toilets court ke kai directions mein se sirf ek hain. Toilets ke yeh figures yeh nahi batate ki free pads, spare uniforms ya boys ke sessions ek bhi classroom tak pahunche ya nahi.

## 'Mere formality': states ki reports par court

Court ne baat ghuma-phira kar nahi kahi. Order mein likha hai: "we are discontent with the manner in which compliance is reported", yaani jis tarah compliance report ho rahi hai, usse court naakhush hai. Court ke mutabik kuch states ke jawab "non-application of mind or rather mere formality" dikhate hain, yaani bina soche-samjhe likhe gaye ya sirf khanapoorti [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]]. Court ne Tamil Nadu, Assam, Karnataka, Bihar, Gujarat, Delhi aur Uttar Pradesh samet kai states ki reports mein data ki gadbad flag ki. Punjab ki report toh padhi hi nahi ja saki: court ne use illegible paaya [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]].

Ab is list ko is baat ke saath rakh kar dekho ki ladkiyan asal mein kya use karti hain. 2019-21 ke national family health survey (NFHS-5) mein Bihar ki sirf 59.2% young women periods mein hygienic method use karti thi, jabki Tamil Nadu mein yeh 98.4% tha. Gujarat (66.9%) aur Assam (67.0%) bhi sabse neeche ke paanch states mein the [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Matlab bharose ke layak na hone wali reporting sirf peechhe chal rahe states ki problem nahi thi. Lekin 2019-21 mein jin paanch states mein young women ki haalat sabse kharaab thi, unmein se teen, Bihar, Gujarat aur Assam, un states mein bhi the jinke compliance figures par court aankh band karke bharosa nahi kar saka. Jab kisi state ke kaagaz par hi bharosa na ho, toh koi nahi bata sakta ki kaunsa school aaj bhi kis ladki ko uska haq nahi de raha.

## 'One last opportunity': contempt ki warning

Phir baat aur bigdi. LiveLaw ne 15 October 2026 ko report kiya ki Union government ke lawyer ne court ko bataya ki states toh Centre ke apne information requests ka bhi jawab nahi de rahe [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]]. Court ne states ko compliance report karne ka "one last opportunity", yaani aakhri mauka diya, aur warning di ki jo states jawab nahi denge, unke Chief Secretaries ko contempt notice jayega. Case ki agli hearing 14 December 2026 ko listed hai [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].

Chief Secretary kisi state ki administration ka sabse senior officer hota hai. Contempt notice court ka woh formal step hai jisse woh apne orders ko ignore karne wale ki zimmedari tay karne ki taraf badhta hai. Court ab sirf reports nahi maang raha; ab woh un officers ko warn kar raha hai jo yeh reports bhejte hain. Jis fundamental right ko lagu karwane ke liye Chief Secretaries ko warning deni pade, use system apne aap dene ki taiyari mein tha hi nahi.

## 14 December se pehle apne school mein kya check karo

Order tumhare school tak pahuncha ya nahi, yeh jaanne ke liye hearing ka wait karne ki zaroorat nahi. Judgment ke hisaab se har school ko ladkiyon ko kya-kya dena hai, uski poori checklist hamari alag guide mein hai. Yahan woh paanch sawaal hain jinka jawab affidavit ke figures nahi de paaye:

- Kya ladkiyon ka toilet sach mein chaalu hai, ya sirf "constructed" hai? Lock wala darwaza, nal mein paani aur haath dhone ki jagah hai?
- Kya school mein ladkiyon ko free sanitary napkins chupchaap mil jaate hain, bina poori class ke saamne maange?
- Kya used pads dispose karne ke liye dhakkan wala dustbin ya koi aur safe intezaam hai?
- Kya koi MHM corner hai jahan emergency ke liye spare uniforms aur pads rakhe hon?
- Kya boys aur male teachers ke liye periods par koi session hua hai?

Agar kisi ka bhi jawab "nahi" hai, toh date ke saath likh lo aur principal ko do. Judgment ne District Education Officers ko schools inspect karne ka kaam diya hai [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]], isliye district education office ko date wali letter bhejna agla sahi step hai; ek copy apne paas rakho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Koi judgment tabhi asli banta hai jab jis ladki ke liye woh likha gaya, woh kisi normal school day par uska faayda utha sake.

teen-mood-hormones-or-depression.en:
Imagine a 15-year-old in Nagpur, in Class 10. In June he slammed a door over the wifi and was laughing with his cousins an hour later. By November he has dropped cricket, eats in his room, falls asleep near 3 am and has twice told his mother "kuch farak nahi padta". The family's verdict has not changed in five months: "Yeh umar hi aisi hai. Hormones hain." They were right in June. They may be wrong by November, and nobody has checked.

## What puberty does to mood and sleep

"Just hormones" is half true. Puberty brings shifting hormones alongside a changing body, new pressures at school and new questions about friends and attraction. For many teenagers, irritation, embarrassment, excitement and sadness all arrive louder than they did at ten. Some people who menstruate also notice low mood or irritability in the days before a period.

Sleep shifts too. Many teenagers genuinely do not feel sleepy at their old bedtime, while school still starts early, and too little sleep can leave anyone irritable, low and unable to concentrate. WHO describes adolescence as a time when physical, emotional and social changes can leave young people vulnerable to mental health problems [[who-adolescent-mh]].

The mark of ordinary moodiness is that it passes. It lasts hours, or a day or two, and in between the teenager still enjoys things: friends, food, a match, a silly reel.

## When it is more than hormones: warning signs

The test is not how dramatic a mood is. It is how long it stays and how much of life it takes over. Take it seriously when you see:

- sadness, emptiness, anger or worry for most of the day, on most days, for weeks at a stretch;
- no interest in things they used to love;
- sleep or eating that has changed sharply;
- falling marks, missed school, pulling away from friends;
- repeated headaches or stomach aches with no clear cause;
- talk of being a burden, of things never getting better or of not wanting to be alive, or any self-harm.

In teenagers raised not to cry, especially boys, distress can show up as anger or silence rather than tears. The last sign on the list needs a response the same day, not after the exams.

A lasting change in mood can also mean that something is being done to the teenager: bullying, sexual abuse, blackmail online. Anxiety, depression, sleep problems and changes in mood are among the common behavioural signs of child sexual abuse [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. So ask "has something happened?" before "what is wrong with you?"

Student suicides in India rose about 80% in a decade to 14,488 in 2024, and 1,23,918 students died by suicide between 2014 and 2024, according to NCRB data [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]. Suicide never has a single cause, and depression is treatable. The numbers are a reason to stop filing lasting distress under "phase".

## Why teenagers hide it

Often because they tried once and heard "drama", "phone ka asar" or "humare time mein yeh sab nahi hota tha". After that, hiding is the sensible choice. They also fear becoming a burden, being called "mental", or the news reaching relatives and school. Boys have "mard ko dard nahi hota" to get past first.

The stigma is strong enough that the government has had to design around it. In October 2025 the Health Ministry renamed its Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics as "Centres", saying adolescents hesitated to visit because the word "clinic" carried stigma and a visit was "looked upon with suspicion" [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

The adults they depend on often go untreated themselves. The National Mental Health Survey 2015-16, which surveyed adults, found treatment gaps of 28% to 83% for mental disorders [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. A teenager needs an adult's permission, money and transport to reach care that many adults with a disorder never reach.

## How parents can respond

Choose a side-by-side moment, a drive or a walk, not a face-to-face inquiry. Say what you saw, not what you concluded: "Tum do hafte se khelne nahi gaye. Main gussa nahi hoon, pareshan hoon." Then listen for longer than is comfortable. Do not fix, compare or bargain with marks.

If you are worried about self-harm, ask directly: "Kya kabhi aisa lagta hai ki jeene ka mann nahi hai?" A plain question tells a teenager that this can be spoken about in your house. If the answer is yes, stay with them and connect them to help that day.

Protect sleep with a fixed wake-up time, morning daylight and a phone kept away from the bed. And go with them to a doctor, who can also check for physical causes of tiredness and low mood.

## Getting help: Tele-MANAS 14416 and beyond

- **Tele-MANAS, 14416.** The Health Ministry's helpline, launched in October 2022, is free, runs round the clock and offers counselling to anyone who calls [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. A teenager can call alone, and so can a parent [[tele-manas]].
- **Adolescent Friendly Health Centres.** These offer counselling at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. About 1.7 crore adolescents used them in 2024-25 by the ministry's count, which may include repeat visits [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].
- **A counsellor or doctor.** A counsellor or psychologist offers talking therapy. A psychiatrist is a doctor who can judge whether medicine is needed, and only a doctor should prescribe it. Government hospitals have psychiatry departments.
- **Immediate danger.** Call 112 and do not leave the person alone.

A teenager should know one limit in advance. A counsellor keeps most things private, but cannot promise secrecy if the teenager is in danger or discloses sexual abuse, which the law requires adults to report [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Hormones explain June. They do not explain November. The difference between the two is a few weeks of paying attention and one direct question.
teen-mood-hormones-or-depression.hg:
Nagpur ke ek 15 saal ke ladke ko imagine kijiye, Class 10 mein. June mein usne wifi ko lekar darwaza zor se band kiya tha aur ek ghante baad cousins ke saath hans raha tha. November tak usne cricket chhod diya hai, khana apne kamre mein khaata hai, raat ke kareeb 3 baje sota hai, aur do baar apni mummy se keh chuka hai, "kuch farak nahi padta". Paanch mahine mein family ka faisla nahi badla: "Yeh umar hi aisi hai. Hormones hain." June mein woh sahi the. November mein shayad galat hon, aur kisi ne check hi nahi kiya.

## Puberty mood aur neend ke saath kya karti hai

"Bas hormones hain" aadha sach hai. Puberty mein hormones badalte hain, aur saath mein badalti body, school ka naya pressure, aur dosti aur attraction ke naye sawaal bhi aate hain. Bahut se teenagers ke liye chidchidahat, sharmindagi, excitement aur udaasi, sab das saal ki umar ke muqable zyada zor se mehsoos hoti hain. Jinhe periods aate hain, unmein se kuch logon ko period se pehle ke dinon mein low mood ya chidchidapan bhi mehsoos hota hai.

Neend bhi shift hoti hai. Bahut se teenagers ko purane bedtime par sach mein neend nahi aati, jabki school ab bhi subah jaldi shuru hota hai, aur kam neend kisi ko bhi chidchida, low aur concentrate na kar paane wala bana sakti hai. WHO ke mutabiq adolescence woh daur hai jab physical, emotional aur social changes young logon ko mental health problems ke liye vulnerable bana sakte hain [[who-adolescent-mh]].

Normal moodiness ki pehchaan yeh hai ki woh guzar jaati hai. Woh kuch ghante ya ek-do din rehti hai, aur beech mein teenager cheezon ko enjoy karta rehta hai: dost, khana, match, koi bekaar si reel.

## Jab baat hormones se aage ho: warning signs

Test yeh nahi hai ki mood kitna dramatic hai. Test yeh hai ki woh kitni der tikta hai aur zindagi ka kitna hissa gher leta hai. Ise seriously lijiye jab yeh dikhe:

- udaasi, khaalipan, gussa ya worry, din ke zyadatar waqt, zyadatar dinon mein, hafton tak lagataar;
- un cheezon mein koi interest nahi jo pehle bahut pasand thi;
- neend ya khaane mein tez badlaav;
- girte marks, school miss karna, doston se door hona;
- baar-baar sir dard ya pet dard, bina kisi saaf wajah ke;
- khud ko bojh kehna, yeh kehna ki kuch kabhi theek nahi hoga ya jeene ka mann nahi hai, ya kisi bhi tarah ka self-harm.

Jin teenagers ko rona mana sikhaya gaya ho, khaas kar ladkon mein, takleef aksar aansuon ki jagah gusse ya chuppi ki shakal mein dikhti hai. List ke aakhiri sign par usi din response chahiye, exams ke baad nahi.

Mood mein lamba badlaav is baat ka sign bhi ho sakta hai ki teenager ke saath kuch galat ho raha hai: bullying, sexual abuse, online blackmail. Anxiety, depression, neend ki problems aur mood mein badlaav child sexual abuse ke common behavioural signs mein aate hain [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Isliye "tumhe kya ho gaya hai?" se pehle poochhiye, "kya kuch hua hai?"

NCRB data ke mutabiq India mein student suicides ek dashak mein lagbhag 80% badhkar 2024 mein 14,488 ho gaye, aur 2014 se 2024 ke beech 1,23,918 students ki suicide se maut hui [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]. Suicide ki kabhi ek akeli wajah nahi hoti, aur depression ka ilaaj mumkin hai. Yeh numbers is baat ki wajah hain ki lambi chalti takleef ko "phase" kehkar taalna band kiya jaaye.

## Teenagers ise kyun chhupate hain

Aksar isliye ki unhone ek baar koshish ki thi aur jawab mila "drama", "phone ka asar" ya "humare time mein yeh sab nahi hota tha". Uske baad chhupana hi samajhdaari lagti hai. Unhe yeh darr bhi hota hai ki woh bojh ban jaayenge, unhe "mental" kaha jaayega, ya baat rishtedaaron aur school tak pahunch jaayegi. Ladkon ko pehle "mard ko dard nahi hota" paar karna padta hai.

Stigma itna gehra hai ki sarkar ko bhi uske hisaab se design badalna pada. October 2025 mein Health Ministry ne apne Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics ka naam badalkar "Centres" kar diya, yeh kehte hue ki adolescents wahan jaane mein hichkichate the kyunki "clinic" word ke saath stigma juda tha aur wahan jaane ko "looked upon with suspicion", yaani shak ki nazar se dekha jaata tha [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

Jin badon par woh depend karte hain, woh khud aksar bina ilaaj ke rehte hain. National Mental Health Survey 2015-16, jo adults par hua tha, ne mental disorders ke liye 28% se 83% tak ka treatment gap paaya [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Teenager ko us care tak pahunchne ke liye kisi bade ki permission, paise aur transport chahiye, jis care tak disorder wale bahut se adults khud kabhi nahi pahunchte.

## Parents kaise respond karein

Aamne-saamne ki poochh-taachh ki jagah saath-saath wala moment chuniye, jaise drive ya walk. Jo dekha woh kahiye, apna conclusion nahi: "Tum do hafte se khelne nahi gaye. Main gussa nahi hoon, pareshan hoon." Phir suniye, us waqt ke baad bhi jab sunna uncomfortable lagne lage. Fix mat kijiye, compare mat kijiye, marks ki saudebaazi mat kijiye.

Agar self-harm ki chinta ho, to seedha poochhiye: "Kya kabhi aisa lagta hai ki jeene ka mann nahi hai?" Seedha sawaal teenager ko batata hai ki aapke ghar mein is baare mein baat ho sakti hai. Jawab haan ho, to uske saath rahiye aur usi din use help se jodiye.

Neend ko protect kijiye: fixed wake-up time, subah ki dhoop aur phone bistar se door. Aur uske saath doctor ke paas jaiye, jo thakaan aur low mood ki physical wajahein bhi check kar sakta hai.

## Help kahan milegi: Tele-MANAS 14416 aur uske aage

- **Tele-MANAS, 14416.** Health Ministry ki yeh helpline October 2022 mein launch hui thi; yeh free hai, din-raat chalti hai aur har call karne wale ko counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Teenager akele call kar sakta hai, aur parent bhi [[tele-manas]].
- **Adolescent Friendly Health Centres.** Yeh primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling dete hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Ministry ki ginti ke hisaab se 2024-25 mein lagbhag 1.7 crore adolescents ne inhe use kiya; is ginti mein repeat visits bhi ho sakti hain [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].
- **Counsellor ya doctor.** Counsellor ya psychologist talking therapy dete hain. Psychiatrist ek doctor hota hai jo tay kar sakta hai ki dawa ki zaroorat hai ya nahi, aur dawa sirf doctor ko hi likhni chahiye. Government hospitals mein psychiatry departments hote hain.
- **Turant khatra.** 112 par call kijiye aur us insaan ko akela mat chhodiye.

Teenager ko ek limit pehle se pata honi chahiye. Counsellor zyadatar baatein private rakhta hai, lekin agar teenager khatre mein ho ya sexual abuse ke baare mein bataye, to woh secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakta, kyunki kanoon ke mutabiq badon ko ise report karna hi hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Hormones June ko explain karte hain. November ko nahi. Dono ke beech ka farak hai kuch hafton ka dhyaan aur ek seedha sawaal.

testicles-foreskin-steroids-men-checks.en:
Imagine a 16-year-old in Bhopal who wakes at 2 am with a sudden, sharp pain in one testicle. It is the worst pain he has felt, but he cannot bring himself to wake his father and say where it hurts. He decides to wait until morning. That decision, made out of embarrassment, could cost him the testicle. This guide is about the checks Indian boys and men skip, and the few moments when skipping one is dangerous.

## Why men do not get checked

Boys learn early that "mard ko dard nahi hota" and that anything below the waist is not discussed. Nobody teaches them what their own body should look and feel like.

Government data shows who walks into a sexual-health clinic. India's designated STI clinics, branded Suraksha Clinics, recorded 71.95 lakh visits in 2024-25, and 60.9% of them were by women [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The clinics also treat reproductive tract infections that are common in women, so some gap is expected. Yet among people screened for syphilis at the same clinics, 1.54% of tests on men were reactive, more than three times the 0.48% for women, and 4.12% for transgender clients [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. These are clinic attendees, not the whole population, but the pattern is clear: fewer men come in, and the men who do come in test positive more often.

Many men go instead to "gupt rog" and "sex problem" clinics advertised on walls and phone screens. Advertising drugs that claim to treat conditions such as sexual impotence or venereal diseases is a crime under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, 1954, punishable with up to six months in jail, a fine or both for a first conviction [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. In March 2025 the Supreme Court said there was "no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit" and ordered states to set up enforcement and complaint systems [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

## How to check your testicles

Testicular cancer is uncommon, but it mostly affects young and middle-aged men, exactly the group that avoids doctors. Its most common sign is a painless lump or swelling in one testicle; others include a feeling of heaviness in the scrotum and a dull ache [[nhs-testicular]]. Found early, it is very treatable.

Check once a month, after a warm bath or shower, when the scrotum is relaxed:

- Hold the scrotum in your palm and roll each testicle gently between your thumb and fingers.
- Feel for any lump, hard area, swelling, or change in size or firmness.
- Know what is normal: one testicle often hangs lower or is slightly bigger, and the soft, coiled tube at the back of each one (the epididymis) is meant to be there.

A new lump is not an emergency, and most lumps turn out not to be cancer. But only a doctor can tell, so book an appointment within days, not months.

## Pain that cannot wait until morning

Sudden, severe pain in one testicle, sometimes with swelling, pain in the belly, nausea or vomiting, can mean testicular torsion: the testicle twists on its cord and cuts off its own blood supply. It is most common in teenage boys, and it can happen during sleep or sport.

Torsion is a surgical emergency. An operation within hours can save the testicle; waiting until morning can mean losing it. Go to a hospital emergency department immediately, or call 112 for an ambulance. Infection and injury can cause similar pain and also need a same-day check. Doctors will not be shocked; this is routine emergency work for them.

## Foreskin, hygiene and steroids

In young boys, a tight foreskin is normal. It loosens by itself over the years, sometimes not until the teenage years, and should never be forced back [[nhs-tight-foreskin]]. See a doctor if a tight foreskin causes pain, redness, swelling, a discharge or trouble peeing. If the foreskin is pulled back and gets stuck behind the head of the penis, that is an emergency [[nhs-tight-foreskin]].

Wash under the foreskin daily with warm water and avoid harsh soaps. Itching, redness and a white discharge under the foreskin can be thrush, a common, treatable fungal infection that is not always sexually transmitted [[nhs-thrush]].

Then there is the gym. Anabolic steroids and testosterone injections tell the body it has more than enough testosterone, so it stops making its own. Testicles can shrink, sperm production can fall, and some men develop swelling in the chest. Fertility may take months to recover after stopping, and may not recover fully.
